Et quidem de filiis Levi sacerdotium accipientes, id est filii Aaron nati ex filiis Levi, fungentes sacerdotio secundum legem, mandatum habent in lege decimas sumere a populo, id est ab inferioribus, non ab excellentioribus: et hoc, secundum legem, id est a fratribus suis, puta Judæis, et etiam ab inferioribus Levitis. Inferiores enim Levitæ sacerdotibus decimas dabant, in signum suæ subjectionis. Hæc autem decima, vocabatur decima decimæ: quia de decimis sibi datis, decimas persolverunt. Quanquam et ipsi fratres sacerdotum, puta Judæi omnes fere et inferiores Levitæ, exierint de lumbis Abrahæ, id est, de semine ejus nati sint, quemadmodum sacerdotes. Quasi dicat: Sacerdotes aliis pares sunt genere, sed majores sunt sacerdotii auctoritate. Non ergo Judæi dedissent sacerdotibus decimas, nisi propter excellentiam sacerdotum, quam ex divina ordinatione habebant. Ergo nec Abraham decimas dedisset Melchisedech, nisi major eo fuisset. Et quoniam iste Melchisedech a tam excellenti Patriarcha, sine legis mandato, quasi propria auctoritate, decimas sumpsit, constat quod ejus sacerdotium excellentius sit sacerdotio Levitico. Cujus autem generatio non annumeratur in eis, id est Melchisedech, cujus generationem Scriptura non recitat, qui etiam non fuit de semine Abrahæ sicut Judæi, a quibus Levitæ decimas acceperunt, decimas sumpsit ab Abraham, tanquam ab inferiori: ergo major fuit eo et posteris ejus.
paras.en: Moreover, he sets Melchisedech himself above the Levites. [[7:5|And indeed they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the priesthood|Et quidem de filiis Levi sacerdotium accipientes]], that is, the sons of Aaron, born of the sons of Levi, exercising the priesthood according to the law, [[7:5|have a commandment to take tithes of the people|mandatum habent in lege decimas sumere a populo]][[Num 18:21||]], that is, from those beneath them, not from those more excellent: and this [[7:5|according to the law, that is to say, of their brethren|secundum legem, id est a fratribus suis]], namely the Jews, and also from the lesser Levites. For the lesser Levites gave tithes to the priests, as a sign of their subjection; and this tithe was called the tithe of the tithe[[Num 18:26||]], because of the tithes given to them they paid tithes. [[7:5|though they themselves also|Quanquam et ipsi]], the brethren of the priests (namely nearly all the Jews, and the lesser Levites), [[7:5|came out of the loins of Abraham|exierint de lumbis Abrahæ]], that is, were born of his seed, just as the priests were. As if to say: the priests are equal to the others by birth, but greater by the authority of the priesthood. So the Jews would not have given tithes to the priests but for the excellence of the priests, which they had by divine ordinance. Therefore neither would Abraham have given tithes to Melchisedech, had Melchisedech not been greater than he. And since this Melchisedech took tithes from so excellent a patriarch, without the commandment of a law, as it were by his own authority, it is clear that his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical priesthood. [[7:6|But he, whose pedigree is not numbered among them|Cujus autem generatio non annumeratur in eis]], that is, Melchisedech, whose generation Scripture does not recite, who moreover was not of the seed of Abraham as the Jews were, from whom the Levites received tithes, [[7:6|received tithes of Abraham|decimas sumpsit ab Abraham]], as from an inferior: therefore he was greater than Abraham and his descendants.

paras.t: Cujus aliam rationem subdit Apostolus. Et hunc Abraham patriarcham qui habebat repromissiones, id est, cui Deus multa promisit, videlicet quod in semine ejus benedicerentur omnes gentes, et ipse in bona senectute moreretur, benedixit ipse Melchisedech, dicens: Benedictus Abraham Deo excelso, […] (id est nullo negante […] minus est, id est inferius, a meliore, id est a sublimiori, benedicitur. Benedicens enim, inter Deum et eum qui benedicitur, medius est: quod intelligendum est de benedictione consecrationis. Ergo Melchisedech major fuit quam Abraham.
paras.en: Of this the Apostle adds another reason. And [[7:6|him|hunc]], Abraham the patriarch, [[7:6|that had the promises|qui habebat repromissiones]], that is, to whom God promised many things, namely that in his seed all nations should be blessed[[Gen 22:18||]], and that he himself should die in a good old age, Melchisedech himself [[7:6|blessed|benedixit ipse]], saying: [[Gen 14:19|Blessed be Abram by the most high God|Benedictus Abraham Deo excelso]], […] (that is, with no one gainsaying it […] [[7:7|that which is less|minus est]], that is, the lower, [[7:7|is blessed by the better|a meliore]], that is, by the higher. For he who blesses stands as mediator between God and him who is blessed: which is to be understood of the blessing of consecration. Therefore Melchisedech was greater than Abraham.

paras.t: Tertiam quoque rationem ad idem subdit Apostolus. Et hic quidem, in sacerdotio Levitico, homines morientes, id est sacerdotes mortales, per mortem sibi invicem succedentes, decimas accipiunt a Judæis; ibi autem, id est in ipso Melchisedech, contestatur Scriptura quia vivit ipse Melchisedech, quoniam nil dicit de morte ipsius, quasi sit sine fine dierum. Quod fit in figura Christi pontificis nostri, cujus sacerdotium discernitur a sacerdotio Levitico per Melchisedech. Hæc verba quidam male intelligentes, dixerunt Melchisedech immortalem fuisse. Patet ergo quod sacerdotium Melchisedech dignius erat sacerdotio Levitico.
paras.en: He adds a third reason to the same effect. [[7:8|And here indeed|Et hic quidem]], in the Levitical priesthood, [[7:8|men that die|homines morientes]], that is, mortal priests, succeeding one another through death, [[7:8|receive tithes|decimas accipiunt]] from the Jews; [[7:8|but there|ibi autem]], that is, in Melchisedech himself, [[7:8|he hath witness|contestatur]] [Denis takes the verb with *Scriptura*: Scripture bears witness] [[7:8|that he liveth|quia vivit]], Melchisedech himself, since it says nothing of his death, as though he were without end of days. This is done in figure of Christ our high priest, whose priesthood is distinguished from the Levitical priesthood by means of Melchisedech. Some, misunderstanding these words, said that Melchisedech was immortal. It is plain, then, that the priesthood of Melchisedech was worthier than the Levitical priesthood.

paras.t: Et ut ita dictum sit, id est sic loquendo, videlicet per figuram quæ appellatur synecdoche, per Abraham dantem decimas ipsi Melchisedech, et Levi, id est ordo sacerdotum Leviticorum, qui decimas accepit secundum legem a populo Israel, decimatus est, id est, decimas dedit sacerdoti Melchisedech. Et recte dixi quod Levi per Abraham, seu in Abraham, non per se ipsum, decimas dedit, quoniam nondum erat: Adhuc enim in lumbis patris sui, videlicet Abrahæ, erat Levi, quando obviavit ei, scilicet Abrahæ, ipse Melchisedech. Per lumbos autem significat Apostolus membra in quibus est semen, id est virtus generativa. Quemadmodum ergo Adam peccante, omnes peccavimus qui eramus in lumbis ejus; sic Abraham dante decimas, Levi et ceteri exsistentes in lumbis ejus, decimas præstiterunt. Ideo inferiores fuerunt ipso Melchisedech, quia dans decimas inferior est recipiente. — Non tamen Christus in Abraham decimatus est, sicut nec in Adam peccavit, quamvis fuerit in lumbis amborum. Fuit nempe in lumbis Adæ ac Abrahæ alio modo quam ceteri, utputa tantum secundum corpoream substantiam, non secundum rationem seminalem: quia non fuit conceptus naturali virtute seminis, sed supernaturali potentia Sancti Spiritus. Sacerdotium ergo Melchisedech dignius sacerdotio fuerat Levitico, non autem sacerdotio Christi aut christiano.
paras.en: [[7:9|And (as it may be said)|Et ut ita dictum sit]], that is, so to speak, namely by the figure called synecdoche [a figure of speech in which a part is put for the whole, or the whole for a part], [[7:9|in Abraham|per Abraham]], who gave tithes to Melchisedech himself, [[7:9|even Levi|et Levi]], that is, the order of the Levitical priests, [[7:9|who received tithes|qui decimas accepit]] according to the law from the people of Israel, [[7:9|paid tithes|decimatus est]], that is, gave tithes to the priest Melchisedech. And rightly did I say that Levi paid tithes through Abraham, or in Abraham, and not by himself, since he did not yet exist: [[7:10|For he was yet in the loins of his father|Adhuc enim in lumbis patris]], namely of Abraham (Levi, that is), [[7:10|when Melchisedech met him|quando obviavit ei]], namely Abraham. Now by the loins the Apostle means the members in which the seed is, that is, the generative power. As, then, when Adam sinned, all of us sinned who were in his loins[[Rom 5:12||]], so when Abraham gave tithes, Levi and the others who were in his loins paid tithes. They were therefore inferior to Melchisedech himself, since he who gives tithes is inferior to him who receives them. — Christ, however, did not pay tithes in Abraham, just as he did not sin in Adam, although he was in the loins of both. For he was in the loins of Adam and of Abraham in another way than the rest, namely only according to bodily substance, not according to seminal reason [that is, not as one to be begotten by the natural power of the father's seed]: since he was not conceived by the natural power of seed, but by the supernatural power of the Holy Spirit[[Luke 1:35||]]. The priesthood of Melchisedech, then, was worthier than the Levitical priesthood, but not than the priesthood of Christ, or the Christian priesthood.

paras.t: Consequenter probat Apostolus, quod sacerdotium Christi præstantius sit sacerdotio Levitico, ipsumque evacuet, et per consequens legem veterem cessare faciat. Si ergo consummatio, id est hominum perfectio, per sacerdotium Leviticum erat, id est, si sacerdotium illud legale, in se perfectum aliosque perficiens fuit; populus enim Israel sub ipso sacerdotio legem accepit in monte Sinai. Vetus enim lex ministrata est populo Israel per sacerdotes Levitici generis. Quoniam ergo populus sub illo sacerdotio legem accepit, indiguit perfici illo sacerdotio; ideo recte quæsivi, an consummatio per sacerdotium Leviticum erat. Si ergo sic fuit, quid adhuc necessarium fuit, secundum ordinem Melchisedech, alium ritu ac tribu surgere sacerdotem, videlicet Christum, qui non est sacerdos ex tribu Levi descendens, nec ritum legalium sacerdotum observans, et non secundum ordinem Aaron dici, id est Christum non appellari sacerdotem secundum ordinem Aaron, sicut vocatus est sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedech? quasi dicat Apostolus: Si per sacerdotium Leviticum potuissent homines a peccato purgari et gratia perfici, non prædixisset Scriptura alium sacerdotem surrecturum, non secundum ordinem Aaron, sed Melchisedech. Alias namque sacerdotium hujus superfluum esset. Quum ergo Scriptura prænunciaverit Christum fore sacerdotem secundum ordinem Melchisedech, constat quod sacerdotium Leviticum fuerat imperfectum ac figurativum: propter quod, adveniente sacerdotio Christi cessare debebat, quemadmodum figura et imperfectum cessant adveniente re figurata atque perfecta.
paras.en: Next the Apostle proves that the priesthood of Christ is more excellent than the Levitical priesthood, and makes it void, and consequently causes the old law to cease. [[7:11|If then perfection|Si ergo consummatio]], that is, the perfecting of men, [[7:11|was by the Levitical priesthood|per sacerdotium Leviticum erat]], that is, if that legal priesthood was perfect in itself and made others perfect; [[7:11|for under it the people received the law|populus enim Israel sub ipso sacerdotio legem accepit]] (the people of Israel, under that priesthood) on Mount Sinai[[Ex 19:1||]][[Ex 20:1||]]. For the old law was ministered to the people of Israel through priests of the Levitical race. Since, then, the people received the law under that priesthood, it needed to be perfected by that priesthood; therefore I rightly asked whether perfection was by the Levitical priesthood. If, then, it was so, [[7:11|what further need was there|quid adhuc necessarium fuit]], [[7:11|according to the order of Melchisedech|secundum ordinem Melchisedech]], [[7:11|that another priest should rise|alium ritu ac tribu surgere sacerdotem]], another in rite and in tribe, namely Christ, who is not a priest descended from the tribe of Levi, nor one who observes the rite of the legal priests, [[7:11|and not be called according to the order of Aaron|et non secundum ordinem Aaron dici]], that is, that Christ is not called a priest according to the order of Aaron, as he is called a priest according to the order of Melchisedech? As if the Apostle were to say: if through the Levitical priesthood men could have been cleansed from sin and perfected by grace, Scripture would not have foretold that another priest would arise, not according to the order of Aaron, but of Melchisedech. For otherwise the priesthood of this one would be superfluous. Since, then, Scripture foretold that Christ would be a priest [[Ps 109:4|according to the order of Melchisedech|fore sacerdotem secundum ordinem Melchisedech]], it is clear that the Levitical priesthood was imperfect and figurative: for which reason it had to cease at the coming of the priesthood of Christ, as the figure and the imperfect cease at the coming of the thing figured and of the perfect.

paras.t: Porro quod frustra alius sacerdos surgeret, si sacerdotium Leviticum consummaret, declarat Apostolus. Translato enim […] translatio fiat. Lex namque et sacerdotium simul sunt, et se concomitantur, nec unum prodest sine officio alterius. Ideo quod de uno dicitur, de alio intelligitur: unde […] mutato, aliud quoque mutatur. Quia ergo teste Scriptura, surgit alius sacerdos a sacerdotibus legalibus, scilicet Christus, de quo scriptum est, Tu es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech, liquet quod lex vetus per […]stum cessaverit.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle makes clear that another priest would arise to no purpose if the Levitical priesthood made perfect. [[7:12|For the priesthood being translated|Translato enim]] […] [[7:12|that a translation also be made|translatio fiat]]. For the law and the priesthood go together and accompany one another, and neither is of use without the office of the other. Therefore what is said of the one is understood of the other: hence when […] is changed, the other also is changed. Since, then, on the witness of Scripture, another priest arises, other than the legal priests, namely Christ, of whom it is written, [[Ps 109:4|Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|Tu es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech]] [the margin gives Ps. cx, 4; the verse is Ps 109:4], it is plain that the old law has ceased through […] [the text reads *per* …*stum*, no doubt *per Christum*, "through Christ"].

paras.t: Cessationem vero legalis seu Levitici sacerdotii adhuc probat Apostolus, ecce […] Christus non sit de tribu Levi. In quo enim hæc dicuntur, id est Christus, […] cujus persona, ista de sacerdotio secundum ordinem Melchisedech recitantur, de alia tribu quam sit tribus Levi, est, videlicet de tribu Juda, de qua nullus altari præsto fuit, id est, nemo ad ministerium altaris accessit. Quod autem de alia tribu sit Christus, ostenditur. Manifestum enim quod ex Juda patriarcha ortus est Dominus noster Jesus Christus. Virgo Maria, sicut et Joseph, de tribu Juda […]cessit. Unde in Apocalypsi habetur […] leo de tribu Juda. In qua tribu nihil de sacerdotibus Moyses locutus est, scilicet, ut aliquis de tribu Juda esset sacerdos legalis.
paras.en: The Apostle further proves the ceasing of the legal or Levitical priesthood, […] Christ is not of the tribe of Levi [the transcription reads *ecce* here; probably *ex eo quod*, "from the fact that"]. [[7:13|For he of whom these things are spoken|In quo enim hæc dicuntur]], that is, Christ, […] whose person these things concerning the priesthood according to the order of Melchisedech are recited, [[7:13|is of another tribe|de alia tribu]] than the tribe of Levi, namely of the tribe of Juda, [[7:13|of which no one attended on the altar|de qua nullus altari præsto fuit]], that is, no one approached the ministry of the altar. That Christ is of another tribe is then shown. [[7:14|For it is evident|Manifestum enim]] that [[7:14|out of Juda|ex Juda]] the patriarch [[7:14|sprung|ortus est]] [[7:14|our Lord|Dominus noster]] Jesus Christ[[Gen 49:10||]] [the margin's verse number is unreadable; Gen 49:10 is the prophecy of the sceptre of Juda]. The Virgin Mary, like Joseph, […] of the tribe of Juda[[Matt 1:16||]][[Luke 1:27||]] [of the verb only …*cessit* survives, probably *processit*, "came forth"]. Hence in the Apocalypse he is called […] [[Apoc 5:5|the lion of the tribe of Juda|leo de tribu Juda]]. [[7:14|in which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priests|In qua tribu nihil de sacerdotibus Moyses locutus est]], namely, that anyone of the tribe of Juda should be a legal priest.

paras.t: Et amplius, id est alia ratio, adhuc manifestum est quod in præcedenti ratione ostensum est, scilicet quod sacerdotium Leviticum sit translatum: quia, secundum similitudinem, id est […]tum et ordinem, Melchisedech exsurgat alius sacerdos, videlicet Christus, […] Scriptura prædixit: qui sub specie panis et vini corpus suum et sanguinem dedit discipulis, sicut Melchisedech […] et vinum obtulit: qui Christus […] dum hoc […] secundum institutionem legis Mosaicæ […]nalia præcipientis, factus est sacerdos; non enim fuit de tribu Levi, nec […] sacrificia immolavit; sed secundum virtutem vitæ insolubilis, id est potestate divina, qua dat suis electis vitam insolubilem seu æternam. Divina enim virtute simul ac ordinatione factus est Christus sacerdos.
paras.en: [[7:15|And it is yet far more|Et amplius]] (that is, by another reason) [[7:15|evident|adhuc manifestum est]] what was shown by the preceding reason, namely that the Levitical priesthood is translated: because [[7:15|according to the similitude|secundum similitudinem]], that is, the […] and order [of this word only …*tum* survives, perhaps *ritum*, "rite"], [[7:15|of Melchisedech there ariseth another priest|Melchisedech exsurgat alius sacerdos]], namely Christ, […] Scripture foretold: who under the species of bread and wine gave his body and blood to his disciples[[1 Cor 11:23||]][[Matt 26:26||]], as Melchisedech offered […] and wine: [[7:16|Who|qui Christus]], Christ, […] this […] according to the institution of the Mosaic law, which prescribed […] things [of this word only …*nalia* survives, probably *carnalia*, "carnal"], [[7:16|is made|factus est]] a priest; for he was not of the tribe of Levi, nor did he offer […] sacrifices; [[7:16|but according to the power of an indissoluble life|sed secundum virtutem vitæ insolubilis]], that is, by the divine power by which he gives his elect a life indissoluble, or eternal[[John 10:28||]]. For it was by divine power and ordinance together that Christ was made a priest.

paras.t: Quod autem Christus sit sacerdos secundum similitudinem Melchisedech, probat. Contestatur enim David in Psalmo: Quoniam tu, Christe, es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech.
paras.en: That Christ is a priest according to the similitude of Melchisedech, he proves: [[7:17|For he testifieth|Contestatur enim]], namely David in the Psalm[[Ps 109:4||]]: [[7:17|Thou|Quoniam tu]], O Christ, [[7:17|art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech]].

paras.t: Reprobatio quidem fit præcedentis mandati, id est, nunc tempore gratiæ vetus lex reprobatur, seu evacuata docetur, ita ut non liceat eam servari, propter infirmitatem, id est propter imperfectionem quam habuit quando stetit: non enim plene justificavit, nec ad beatitudinem introduxit, eo quod non continuit gratiam; et etiam propter inutilitatem ejus pro tempore gratiæ. Jam enim ejus observantia nil confert, nec ad gratiam præparat, sed potius obest. Nihil enim ad perfectionem adduxit lex, id est, propria virtute nullum ad perfectionem perduxit: imo nihil operabatur ad perfectionem internam, quia non continuit gratiam. Non enim sacramenta ejus gratiam continebant, quemadmodum sacramenta novæ legis, quæ ratione suorum sacramentorum dicitur gratiam continere atque præstare. Quamvis ergo lex perfectionem præcepit per mandata moralia, non tamen virtutem implendi donavit. Idcirco sua virtute nullum perfecit. Et quamvis multi in veteri lege erant perfecti, hoc tamen non fuit per legem, sed per fidem et gratiam Christi tunc venturi. Elucescit itaque quod lex, etiam quoad præcepta moralia, non adduxit ad perfectionem sua virtute. Propter quod dictum est ad Galatas: Si data esset lex quæ posset vivificare, vere ex lege esset justitia. Introductio vero melioris spei, id est exhibitio spei nobis a Christo proposita, qua non terrena, sed cœlestia bona exspectamus, est per quam, id est cujus virtute, proximamus ad Deum, id est, ad Deum accedimus, acquirendo perfectionem gratiæ in præsenti et perfectionem gloriæ in futuro. Hæc enim est vera atque formata spes, quæ non confundit, sed salvat.
paras.en: [[7:18|There is indeed a setting aside of the former commandment|Reprobatio quidem fit præcedentis mandati]], that is, now, in the time of grace, the old law is set aside, or is taught to have been made void, so that it is not lawful to keep it, [[7:18|because of the weakness|propter infirmitatem]], that is, because of the imperfection it had while it stood: for it did not fully justify, nor bring in to beatitude, since it did not contain grace; and also because of [[7:18|unprofitableness thereof|inutilitatem ejus]] for the time of grace. For now its observance confers nothing, nor prepares for grace, but rather does harm. [[7:19|For the law brought nothing to perfection|Nihil enim ad perfectionem adduxit lex]], that is, by its own power it brought no one to perfection: indeed it wrought nothing toward inward perfection, because it did not contain grace. For its sacraments did not contain grace, as do the sacraments of the new law, which by reason of its sacraments is said to contain and bestow grace. So although the law commanded perfection through the moral precepts, it did not give the power to fulfil them. Therefore by its own power it perfected no one. And although many under the old law were perfect, this was not through the law, but through faith and the grace of Christ, who was then to come. It is clear, then, that the law, even as regards the moral precepts, did not bring to perfection by its own power. For which reason it is said to the Galatians: [[Gal 3:21|if there had been a law given which could give life, verily justice should have been by the law|Si data esset lex quæ posset vivificare, vere ex lege esset justitia]]. [[7:19|but a bringing in of a better hope|Introductio vero melioris spei]], that is, the showing forth of the hope set before us by Christ, by which we look not for earthly but for heavenly goods, is that [[7:19|by which|per quam]], that is, by whose power, [[7:19|we draw nigh to God|proximamus ad Deum]], that is, we approach God, acquiring the perfection of grace in the present and the perfection of glory in the future. For this is the true and formed hope [*spes formata*: hope given its form, and so made living, by charity], which [[Rom 5:5|confoundeth not|non confundit]], but saves.

paras.t: Insuper probat Apostolus, sacerdotium Christi firmius ac dignius esse sacerdotio Levitico: quoniam Christus institutus est sacerdos a Deo cum jurejurando; sacerdotes vero legales, sine jurejurando seu juramento divino. Et quantum est, id est illud quod de sacerdotio Christi perhibetur, non sine jurejurando factum est, nec intelligendum sine eo. Alii quidem, puta Levitici sacerdotes, non in perpetuum duraturi, sine jurejurando, id est sine confirmatione divini juramenti, sacerdotes facti sunt. Unde in Exodo ubi de ordinatione sacerdotum legalium agitur, nullum interponitur juramentum. Sic quippe Dominus ait ad Moysen: Applica fratrem tuum cum filiis suis de medio filiorum Israel, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi. Hic autem, videlicet Christus, sacerdos effectus est secundum assumptam naturam, cum jurejurando per eum, id est ab eo, puta a Deo Patre, qui dixit ad illum in Psalmo: Juravit Dominus, haud dubium quin per se ipsum, et non pœnitebit eum jurasse. Nunquam enim pœnitet de eo quod semel decretum est in suo æterno consilio, quamvis interdum pœniteat, id est, per modum pœnitentis se habeat, mutando factum seu variando sententiam. Unde in libro Regum legitur: Porro Triumphator in Israel non parcet, et pœnitudine non flectetur; neque enim homo est, ut agat pœnitentiam. Tu es sacerdos in æternum. In quo patet invariabilitas sacerdotii Christi.
paras.en: Moreover, the Apostle proves that the priesthood of Christ is firmer and worthier than the Levitical priesthood, since Christ was instituted a priest by God with an oath, but the legal priests without an oath, that is, without divine swearing. [[7:20|And inasmuch as it is|Et quantum est]], that is, what is declared of the priesthood of Christ, [[7:20|not without an oath|non sine jurejurando]] was it done, nor is it to be understood without one. [[7:20|for the others indeed|Alii quidem]], namely the Levitical priests, who were not to last for ever, [[7:20|without an oath|sine jurejurando]], that is, without the confirmation of a divine oath, [[7:20|were made priests|sacerdotes facti sunt]]. Hence in Exodus, where the ordination of the legal priests is treated, no oath is interposed. For thus the Lord says to Moses: [[Ex 28:1|Take|Applica]] [[Ex 28:1|thy brother with his sons, from among the children of Israel, that they may minister to me in the priest's office|fratrem tuum cum filiis suis de medio filiorum Israel, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi]]. [[7:21|But this|Hic autem]], namely Christ, was made a priest according to the nature he assumed, [[7:21|with an oath, by him|cum jurejurando per eum]], that is, from him, namely from God the Father, [[7:21|that said unto him|qui dixit ad illum]] in the Psalm[[Ps 109:4||]]: [[7:21|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]], doubtless by himself, [[7:21|and he will not repent|et non pœnitebit eum]] of having sworn. For God never repents of what has once been decreed in his eternal counsel, although at times he repents, that is, behaves after the manner of one who repents, by changing what he has done or varying his sentence. Hence we read in the book of Kings: [[1 Kings 15:29|But the triumpher in Israel will not spare, and will not be moved to repentance: for he is not a man that he should repent|Porro Triumphator in Israel non parcet, et pœnitudine non flectetur; neque enim homo est, ut agat pœnitentiam]]. [[7:21|Thou art a priest for ever|Tu es sacerdos in æternum]]. In this the unchangeableness of the priesthood of Christ is plain.

paras.t: In tantum, id est tam multum, sicut sacerdotium Christi præfulget sacerdotio legali, videlicet quod est æternum et juramento firmatum, melioris testamenti, id est perfectioris legis, sponsor, id est assertor, factus est Jesus. Docuit enim evangelicam legem seu novum testamentum, quod veteri testamento vehementer præfertur. Promittit namque bona æterna, gratiam continet, et ad felicitatem, quæ finis est legis, introducit. Vel sic: Melioris testamenti, id est præstantiorum bonorum, puta cœlestium, sponsor et promissor factus est Jesus: qui in exordio suæ prædicationis, Pœnitentiam, inquit, agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum. Nomine autem testamenti, interdum exprimitur bonum quod per testamentum præstatur. Vetus vero testamentum spondebat terrena.
paras.en: [[7:22|By so much|In tantum]], that is, by as much as the priesthood of Christ outshines the legal priesthood, namely in that it is eternal and confirmed by an oath, [[7:22|of a better testament|melioris testamenti]], that is, of a more perfect law, [[7:22|a surety|sponsor]], that is, one who vouches for it, [[7:22|is Jesus made|factus est Jesus]]. For he taught the gospel law, or new testament, which is far to be preferred to the old testament: for it promises eternal goods, contains grace, and brings in to happiness, which is the end of the law. Or thus: [[7:22|of a better testament|Melioris testamenti]], that is, of more excellent goods, namely heavenly ones, [[7:22|a surety|sponsor]] and promiser [[7:22|is Jesus made|factus est Jesus]]: who at the beginning of his preaching: [[Matt 4:17|Do penance|Pœnitentiam]], he says, [[Matt 4:17|for the kingdom of heaven is at hand|appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum]]. For by the name of testament is sometimes expressed the good that is bestowed through the testament; and the old testament promised earthly things.

paras.t: Præterea agit Apostolus de unitate sacerdotii Christi. Et alii quidem Levitici generis plures facti sunt sacerdotes summi, sibi invicem succedentes, secundum legem, quæ præcepit filium succedere patri in sacerdotio, idcirco quod morte, id est per mortem, prohiberentur permanere, id est jugiter vivere; hic autem Christus eo quod maneat in æternum, non solum secundum divinitatem, sed et secundum humanam naturam post resurrectionem: unde Judæi dixerunt, Nos audivimus ex lege, quia Christus manet in æternum; sempiternum habet sacerdotium.
paras.en: Next the Apostle treats of the oneness of the priesthood of Christ. [[7:23|And the others indeed|Et alii quidem]], of the Levitical race, [[7:23|were made many priests|plures facti sunt sacerdotes]], high priests, succeeding one another according to the law, which commanded the son to succeed the father in the priesthood[[Lev 6:22||]][[Lev 16:32||]], [[7:23|because by reason of death|idcirco quod morte]], that is, through death, [[7:23|they were not suffered to continue|prohiberentur permanere]], that is, to live on without end; [[7:24|But this|hic autem]], Christ, [[7:24|for that he continueth for ever|eo quod maneat in æternum]], not only according to the divinity, but also according to the human nature after the resurrection (hence the Jews said, [[John 12:34|We have heard out of the law that Christ abideth for ever|Nos audivimus ex lege, quia Christus manet in æternum]]), [[7:24|hath an everlasting priesthood|sempiternum habet sacerdotium]].

paras.t: Ex his elicit Apostolus efficaciam sacerdotii Christi. Unde, id est propter sempiternitatem sacerdotii sui, et salvare, id est salutem conferre, in perpetuum potest, videlicet quamdiu est aliquis salvandus; vel, Salvare in perpetuum, id est perpetuam beatitudinem dare; accedens spirituali accessu, per se ipsum, id est in propria persona, secundum quod homo, non per aliquem mediatorem seu aliam hostiam, ad Deum Patrem, tanquam advocatus noster ac mediator; semper vivens, id est vigorosus ac vivax exsistens: resurgens enim ex mortuis, jam non moritur; ad interpellandum pro nobis. Quomodo autem conveniat Christo interpellare, id est orare, pro nobis, diligenter tractatum est ad Romanos, ubi hæc eadem verba ponit Apostolus.
paras.en: From these things the Apostle draws out the efficacy of the priesthood of Christ. [[7:25|Whereby|Unde]], that is, on account of the everlastingness of his priesthood, [[7:25|he is able also to save|et salvare]], that is, to bestow salvation, [[7:25|for ever|in perpetuum potest]], namely as long as there is anyone to be saved; or, [[7:25|to save for ever|Salvare in perpetuum]], that is, to give everlasting beatitude; [[7:25|them that come|accedens]] [Denis reads *accedens*, "coming", in the singular, and takes it of Christ himself; the Vulgate has *accedentes*] with a spiritual approach, [[7:25|by him|per se ipsum]], that is, by himself, in his own person, as man, not through some other mediator or other victim, [[7:25|to God|ad Deum]] the Father, as our advocate[[1 John 2:1||]] and mediator; [[7:25|always living|semper vivens]], that is, being vigorous and full of life[[Apoc 1:18||]]: for [[Rom 6:9|rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|resurgens enim ex mortuis, jam non moritur]]; [[7:25|to make intercession for us|ad interpellandum pro nobis]]. How it befits Christ to make intercession, that is, to pray, for us was treated carefully on Romans, where the Apostle sets down these same words[[Rom 8:34||]].

paras.t: Quod vero Christus sit idoneus ad interpellandum pro nobis, consequenter ostenditur. Talis enim, sicut subscribitur, decebat ut nobis, id est ad nostram salutem procurandam, esset pontifex, utpote sanctus in anima per omnis culpæ carentiam, innocens quantum ad alios, quia non est inventus dolus in ore ejus, impollutus a corpore, segregatus a peccatoribus, id est grege iniquorum remotus nunc loco et opere. Verumtamen Christus in hac vita non erat corporaliter a peccatoribus segregatus, nec eos vitavit. Nam quum Pharisæi dixissent discipulis, Quare cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducat et bibit magister vester? Christus respondit: Non indigent, qui sani sunt, medico, sed qui male habent: venit enim Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat. Opere tamen et consensu separatus fuit ab eis. Et excelsior cœlis factus. Ascendit enim super omnes cœlos, et universis creaturis cœlestibus dignior est, quoniam Pater omnia subjecit sub pedibus ejus.
paras.en: That Christ is fit to make intercession for us is shown next. [[7:26|For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest|Talis enim, sicut subscribitur, decebat ut nobis, id est ad nostram salutem procurandam, esset pontifex]] (*such* as is described below; *for us*, that is, for procuring our salvation), being [[7:26|holy|sanctus]] in soul, through the absence of all fault, [[7:26|innocent|innocens]] as regards others, because [[1 Pet 2:22|neither was guile found in his mouth|non est inventus dolus in ore ejus]][[Is 53:9||]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 9; Denis's words are those of 1 Pet 2:22, which quotes it], [[7:26|undefiled|impollutus]] in body, [[7:26|separated from sinners|segregatus a peccatoribus]], that is, removed from the flock of the wicked, now, in place and in deed. Yet in this life Christ was not bodily separated from sinners, nor did he shun them. For when the Pharisees had said to the disciples, [[Matt 9:11|Why doth your master eat with publicans and sinners?|Quare cum publicanis et peccatoribus manducat et bibit magister vester?]][[Luke 5:30||]] [Denis's wording, with *et bibit*, "and drink", joins Matt 9:11 and Luke 5:30], Christ answered: [[Luke 5:31|They that are whole need not the physician: but they that are sick|Non indigent, qui sani sunt, medico, sed qui male habent]][[Matt 9:12||]]: [[Luke 19:10|For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.|venit enim Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]] [the margin gives Luc. v, 10; the words are Luke 19:10]. Yet in deed and in consent he was separate from them. [[7:26|and made higher than the heavens|Et excelsior cœlis factus]]. For he [[Eph 4:10|ascended above all the heavens|Ascendit enim super omnes cœlos]], and is worthier than all the heavenly creatures, since the Father [[1 Cor 15:26|hath put all things under his feet|omnia subjecit sub pedibus ejus]][[Ps 8:8||]] [the margin gives Ps. viii, 7; the words are in Ps 8:8].

paras.t: Qui Christus non habet quotidie necessitatem, quemadmodum sacerdos legalis necessitatem habebat, prius pro suis delictis hostias offerre, deinde pro populo, id est populi delicto expiando. Hoc namque erat imperfectionis in sacerdotibus veteris Testamenti, quod prius pro propria reconciliatione hostias immolabant. Sed Christus, qui peccatum non fecit, talis non fuit: nec indiget quotidie offerre pro populo hostiam: hoc enim fecit semel, id est, una vice obtulit hostiam pro populo, se ipsum offerendo Deo Patri in ara crucis pro nobis. Quæ hostia tantæ est dignitatis, ut pro omnium peccatis sufficientissima fuerit: ideo non indiget iterari. Sed sacrificia legis propter insufficientiam suam iterabantur quotidie.
paras.en: [[7:27|Who|Qui]] (Christ) [[7:27|needeth not daily|non habet quotidie necessitatem]], [[7:27|as the other priests|quemadmodum sacerdos legalis]] (as the legal priest had need) [[7:27|to offer sacrifices, first for his own sins|prius pro suis delictis hostias offerre]], [[7:27|and then for the people's|deinde pro populo]][[Lev 16:6||]], that is, for expiating the sin of the people. For this was a mark of imperfection in the priests of the old Testament, that they first offered victims for their own reconciliation. But Christ, [[1 Pet 2:22|Who did no sin|qui peccatum non fecit]][[Is 53:9||]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 9; Denis's words are those of 1 Pet 2:22, which quotes it], was not such: nor does he need to offer a victim daily for the people: [[7:27|for this he did once|hoc enim fecit semel]], that is, at one time he offered a victim for the people, [[7:27|in offering himself|se ipsum offerendo]] to God the Father on the altar of the cross for us. And this victim is of such dignity that it was more than sufficient for the sins of all: therefore it does not need to be repeated. But the sacrifices of the law, because of their insufficiency, were repeated daily.

paras.t: Ideo sequitur: Lex enim Mosaica homines de semine Aaron constituit sacerdotes, infirmitatem peccandi ac moriendi habentes, qui et peccabant sicut et ceteri: ideo pro se ipsis indigebant offerre. Sermo autem jurisjurandi, id est sermo Dei juramento firmatus, seu jusjurandum sermone prolatum, qui sermo post legem, id est legislationem in monte Sinai factam, est dictus per David in Psalmo, ubi dicitur, Juravit Dominus et non pœnitebit eum; Filium Dei incarnatum constituit sacerdotem perfectum, id est plenum gratiæ et veritatis, in æternum. Christus enim secundum divinam naturam est simpliciter perfectus, quemadmodum Pater; secundum naturam vero humanam, tantæ exstitit perfectionis, quantam capere potest natura creata, quia non ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum homini Christo.
paras.en: Therefore it follows: [[7:28|For the law|Lex enim]] of Moses [[7:28|maketh men|homines]] of the seed of Aaron [[7:28|priests|constituit sacerdotes]], [[7:28|who have infirmity|infirmitatem peccandi ac moriendi habentes]] of sinning and of dying, who sinned just as the others did: therefore they needed to offer for themselves. [[7:28|but the word of the oath|Sermo autem jurisjurandi]], that is, the word of God confirmed by an oath, or the oath uttered in a word, [[7:28|which was since the law|qui sermo post legem]], that is, after the lawgiving made on Mount Sinai, was spoken by David in the Psalm, where it is said, [[Ps 109:4|The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent|Juravit Dominus et non pœnitebit eum]]: this word has appointed [[7:28|the Son|Filium]] of God incarnate a priest [[7:28|who is perfected|perfectum]], that is, [[John 1:14|full of grace and truth|plenum gratiæ et veritatis]], [[7:28|for evermore|in æternum]]. For Christ according to the divine nature is simply perfect, just as the Father is; but according to the human nature he was of as great perfection as created nature can receive, since [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|non ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum]] to the man Christ.

8.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI OCTAVI : CAPITULUM AUTEM SUPER EA QUÆ DICITUR.
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: Now of the things which we have spoken, this is the sum.

paras.t: Multis jam de dignitate sacerdotii Christi præmemoratis, nunc summarie breviterque perstringit Apostolus ea quæ materiam istam concernunt, ostendens etiam eminentiam sacerdotii Christi ratione sacerdotalis officii.
paras.en: Many things having now been said about the dignity of Christ's priesthood, the Apostle now touches summarily and briefly on what concerns this matter, showing also the eminence of Christ's priesthood by reason of the priestly office.

paras.t: Capitulum autem, id est brevis multorum complexio. Capitulum namque a capite nomen sortitur, quoniam sicut in capite omnes sensus vigent et continentur, sic capitulum totam summam breviter comprehendit. Itaque, Capitulum super ea, id est de his quæ dicuntur de sacerdotio Christi, est hoc quod immediate subjungitur : ubi et capitulum incipit. Talem habemus pontificem, qui consedit, id est, simul cum Patre sedit ab hora ascensionis secundum humanitatem, secundum divinitatem vero a principio […] dextera sedis, id est throni, vel potius sedentis, […] id est paternæ majestatis, seu Dei Patris, in cœlis, id est in cœlo empyreo cœlique civibus. Quomodo autem conveniat Christo secundum utramque naturam sedere ad dexteram Patris, in expositione primi capituli hujus epistolæ dictum est plenius.
paras.en: [[8:1|this is the sum|Capitulum autem]] [Latin *capitulum*, literally 'a little head': a heading or summary], that is, a brief gathering-up of many things. For *capitulum* takes its name from *caput*, the head: since just as in the head all the senses flourish and are contained, so a *capitulum* briefly comprehends the whole sum. And so the sum [[8:1|of the things|super ea]], that is, of those things [[8:1|which we have spoken|quæ dicuntur]] about the priesthood of Christ, is what immediately follows; and there the summary begins. [[8:1|We have such an high priest|Talem habemus pontificem]], [[8:1|who is set|qui consedit]], that is, who sat together with the Father from the hour of the ascension according to his humanity, but according to his divinity from the beginning […] [[8:1|on the right hand of the throne|dextera sedis]], that is, of the seat, or rather of him who is seated, […] [the lost word is probably the lemma's *magnitudinis*, 'of majesty'] that is, of the Father's majesty, or of God the Father, [[8:1|in the heavens|in cœlis]], that is, in the empyrean heaven and among the citizens of heaven. How it befits Christ according to each nature to sit at the right hand of the Father has been said more fully in the exposition of the first chapter of this epistle[[Heb 1:3||]].

paras.t: Sanctorum minister, id est sacrorum Dei donorum, videlicet gratiæ in præsenti et gloriæ in futuro, ministrator seu dator instrumentalis secundum quod homo. Ipsis etiam sanctis discipulis suis Christus ministravit in terra, juxta illud : Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat. Sanctis quoque in patria ministrat vitam æternam, secundum quod scriptum est : Præcinget se, et transiens ministrabit eis. Hæc est servitus dignationis, non subjectionis, qua et angeli ministrant hominibus. Et tabernaculi veri, id est Ecclesiæ militantis seu triumphantis (de qua legitur in Apocalypsi : Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis; item in Psalmo : Domine, quis habitabit in tabernaculo tuo?), quod aliud nihil est nisi electi et sancti, quorum Christus minister est, secundum sensum jam tactum : venit enim Filius hominis ministrare, non ministrari; quod fixit, id est, gratia atque virtutibus stabilivit, Deus, qui solus hoc potest, videlicet mentes electorum per gratiam figere, et non homo purus.
paras.en: [[8:2|A minister of the holies|Sanctorum minister]] [Latin *sanctorum*, 'of holy things' or 'of the saints': Denis takes it both ways], that is, of the sacred gifts of God, namely of grace in the present and of glory in the future: their minister or instrumental giver, according as he is man. Christ also ministered on earth to his holy disciples themselves, according to that saying: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat]]. To the saints in the fatherland too he ministers life everlasting, according as it is written: [[Luke 12:37|he will gird himself|Præcinget se]], [[Luke 12:37|and passing will minister unto them|et transiens ministrabit eis]]. This is a service of condescension, not of subjection, the service by which the angels also minister to men[[Heb 1:14||]]. [[8:2|And of the true tabernacle|Et tabernaculi veri]], that is, of the Church militant or triumphant (of which we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis]]; and again in the Psalm: [[Ps 14:1|Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle?|Domine, quis habitabit in tabernaculo tuo?]]), which is nothing else than the elect and the saints, whose minister Christ is, in the sense already touched on: for [[Matt 20:28|the Son of man is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister|venit enim Filius hominis ministrare, non ministrari]]; [[8:2|which the Lord hath pitched|quod fixit]], that is, made firm with grace and the virtues: *God* [Denis reads *Deus*, 'God', where the Vulgate has *Dominus*, 'the Lord'], who alone can do this, namely fix the minds of the elect by grace, [[8:2|and not man|et non homo]], a mere man.

paras.t: Quod autem Christus sit Sanctorum minister, hinc patet : Omnis enim pontifex legalis sive catholicus, ad offerenda munera spiritualia ac corporalia sui ipsius ac proprii gregis, et hostias laudis pro se ipso ac subditis, constituitur, id est, pontifex ordinatur : hoc est enim officium ejus, quum sit inter Deum et populum medius. Unde quæ populi sunt, offert Deo; et quæ Dei sunt, impetrat populo. Unde necesse est et hunc sacerdotem, videlicet Christum, habere aliquid quod offerat, non pro se, sed pro suis, utpote carnem, quam propter nos immolavit, quam et incessabiliter pro nobis Patris conspectui præsentat cum desiderio nostræ salutis.
paras.en: That Christ is the minister of the holies is clear from this: [[8:3|For every high priest|Omnis enim pontifex]], whether of the Law or of the Catholic Church, [[8:3|is appointed|constituitur]], that is, is ordained high priest, [[8:3|to offer gifts|ad offerenda munera]], spiritual and bodily, for himself and for his own flock, [[8:3|and sacrifices|et hostias]] of praise for himself and for those under him: for this is his office, since he stands between God and the people. Hence what belongs to the people he offers to God, and what belongs to God he obtains for the people. [[8:3|wherefore it is necessary that he also|Unde necesse est et hunc sacerdotem]], namely Christ, [[8:3|should have some thing to offer|habere aliquid quod offerat]], not for himself but for his own: that is, his flesh, which he immolated for our sake, and which he also unceasingly presents for us to the sight of the Father, with desire for our salvation[[Heb 9:24||]].

paras.t: Si ergo esset super terram, id est, si sacrificium a Christo offerendum, esset terrenum, legale aut transitorium, nec esset sacerdos, id est, tunc ipse Christus non esset sacerdos secundum ordinem (ut dictum est) Melchisedech. Nam sacerdotium ejus superfluum esset, eo quod sacrificium ejus offerri posset a sacerdotibus veteris legis. Secundum quod subditur : quum essent, id est, ex quo forent sacerdotes legales, qui offerrent secundum legem scriptam munera terrena et sacrificia similia hujuscemodi sacrificio Christi. Qui sacerdotes legis exemplari et umbræ deserviunt cælestium, id est, circa figuras et sacramenta legalia occupantur : quæ sunt exemplar cœlestium, quoniam ad eorum cognitionem aliquo modo inducunt. Quia tamen hoc faciunt multum obscure ac imperfecte, umbra cœlestium appellantur. Umbra enim inter evidentem imaginem et rem ipsam est media. Sunt ergo exemplar cœlestium, id est a cœlestibus exemplata. Sicut responsum est Moysi Dominum consulenti, quum Moyses consummaret, id est compleret, tabernaculum per manum Beseleel. Deinde ponitur divina responsio.
paras.en: [[8:4|If then he were on earth|Si ergo esset super terram]], that is, if the sacrifice to be offered by Christ were earthly, of the Law, or passing, [[8:4|he would not be a priest|nec esset sacerdos]], that is, then Christ himself would not be a priest according to the order of Melchisedech (as has been said). For his priesthood would be superfluous, since his sacrifice could be offered by the priests of the Old Law. As follows: [[8:4|seeing that there would be others|quum essent]], that is, since there would be priests of the Law, [[8:4|to offer|qui offerrent]] [[8:4|according to the law|secundum legem]], the written Law, earthly [[8:4|gifts|munera]], and sacrifices like this sacrifice of Christ. [[8:5|Who|Qui]], the priests of the Law, [[8:5|serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things|exemplari et umbræ deserviunt cælestium]], that is, are busied about the figures and sacraments of the Law: these are the *example* [Latin *exemplar*, a pattern, or here a thing patterned on another] of heavenly things, since in some way they lead to the knowledge of them. Yet because they do this very obscurely and imperfectly, they are called the *shadow* of heavenly things: for a shadow is midway between a clear image and the thing itself. They are, then, the *example* of heavenly things, that is, patterned upon heavenly things. [[8:5|As it was answered to Moses|Sicut responsum est Moysi]] when he consulted the Lord, [[8:5|when he was to finish|quum Moyses consummaret]], that is, to complete, [[8:5|the tabernacle|tabernaculum]] by the hand of Beseleel. Then the divine answer is given.

paras.t: Vide, inquit Dominus, omnia ad tabernaculum pertinentia facito, id est, fieri præcipe, secundum exemplar quod tibi ostensum est in monte, id est secundum formam tibi ab angelo demonstratam in monte Sinai. Angelus enim docuit Moysen de omnibus construendis et offerendis in tabernaculo. — Differunt autem exemplum et exemplar : quia exemplum est, quod fit ad imitationem alterius, estque posterius illo; exemplar vero vocatur, ad cujus imitationem aliquid fit vel producitur, et est prius illo. Ea itaque in quibus sacerdotes legis deserviebant, absolute loquendo, erant exempla, respectu exemplaris in monte monstrati, posterioraque illo; sed per comparationem ad nos, dici possent exemplaria, prout nostra cognitio tendit ex illis ad cognitionem cœlestium.
paras.en: [[8:5|See (saith he)|Vide, inquit]], that is, the Lord, [[8:5|that thou make all things|omnia ad tabernaculum pertinentia facito]] belonging to the tabernacle, that is, command them to be made, [[8:5|according to the pattern which was shewn thee on the mount|secundum exemplar quod tibi ostensum est in monte]], that is, according to the form shown thee by an angel on Mount Sinai. For an angel taught Moses about all that was to be built and offered in the tabernacle. Now *exemplum* and *exemplar* differ [*exemplum*, a copy; *exemplar*, a pattern or original: the Douay-Rheims renders *exemplari* in this verse 'example' and *exemplar* 'pattern']: for an *exemplum* is what is made in imitation of another, and it is later than that other; but that is called an *exemplar* in imitation of which something is made or produced, and it is prior to it. So the things in which the priests of the Law served were, absolutely speaking, *exempla*, copies with respect to the *exemplar* shown on the mount, and later than it; but by comparison with us they could be called *exemplaria*, patterns, inasmuch as our knowledge proceeds from them to the knowledge of heavenly things.

paras.t: Nunc autem melius sortitus est ministerium, id est, Christus dignius sacerdotium officiumque suscepit, quam fuit obsequium sacerdotum legalium, quanto et melioris testamenti, id est perfectioris legis, videlicet evangelicæ, quæ præfertur legi Mosaicæ, mediator, id est medians dator, est : nam inter Deum et homines mediat, et ex parte Dei legem novam hominibus contulit; quod testamentum novum in melioribus repromissionibus, id est divinis atque æternis promissis, sanctum, id est confirmatum, est. Vetus quippe testamentum promittebat abundantiam temporalium, novum autem affluentiam bonorum cœlestium. Sacramenta etiam novam legem confirmantia, multo præstantiora censentur sacramentis legis antiquæ.
paras.en: [[8:6|But now he hath obtained a better ministry|Nunc autem melius sortitus est ministerium]], that is, Christ has received a worthier priesthood and office than was the service of the priests of the Law, [[8:6|by how much also|quanto et]] [[8:6|of a better testament|melioris testamenti]], that is, of a more perfect law, namely the Gospel law, which is preferred to the Law of Moses, he [[8:6|is a mediator|mediator]], that is, a mediating giver: for he mediates between God and men[[1 Tim 2:5||]], and on God's part bestowed the new law on men; [[8:6|which|quod]] new testament [[8:6|on better promises|in melioribus repromissionibus]], that is, on divine and everlasting promises, [[8:6|is established|sanctum]], that is, confirmed [Denis's text reads *sanctum*, 'holy', for the Vulgate's *sancitum*, 'established'; his gloss shows he takes it in that sense]. For the Old Testament promised an abundance of temporal goods, but the New a wealth of heavenly goods. The sacraments, too, which confirm the new law are reckoned far more excellent than the sacraments of the old law.

paras.t: Nam si illud prius, id est vetus testamentum, a culpa vacasset, id est, culpam perfecte delevisset, suosque servatores perfecte mundasset; non utique secundi, id est novi testamenti, locus inquireretur, id est, necessaria non esset, nec exigeretur lex nova, imo superflua esset.
paras.en: [[8:7|For if that former|Nam si illud prius]], that is, the Old Testament, [[8:7|had been faultless|a culpa vacasset]], that is, had perfectly blotted out guilt and perfectly cleansed those who kept it, [[8:7|there should not indeed|non utique]] [[8:7|a place have been sought|locus inquireretur]] [[8:7|for a second|secundi]], that is, for the New Testament: that is, it would not be necessary, nor would a new law be required; indeed it would be superfluous.

paras.t: Quod autem novum testamentum necessarium sit, probat auctoritate scripturæ quæ habetur apud Jeremiam : quam Apostolus hic allegat secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum. Vituperans enim eos, id est Judæos tanquam per legem perfici non potentes, dicit Jeremias : Ecce dies gratiæ et evangelicæ legis veniunt, dicit Dominus; et consummabo super domum Israel et super domum Juda, id est, completive dabo populo Judæorum in duo regna et duodecim tribus diviso, testamentum novum. Hoc enim Christus in propria persona Judæis proposuit in sermone facto in monte, et in Cœna : de quibus et dixit, Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel.
paras.en: That a new testament is necessary he proves by the authority of the Scripture found in Jeremias, which the Apostle cites here according to the translation of the Seventy Interpreters [that is, the Septuagint, the Greek Old Testament]. [[8:8|For, finding fault with them|Vituperans enim eos]], that is, with the Jews, as unable to be made perfect through the Law, [[8:8|he saith|dicit]], namely Jeremias[[Jer 31:31||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxi, 31–34, the whole passage quoted in vv. 8–12]: [[8:8|Behold the days|Ecce dies]] of grace and of the Gospel law [[8:8|shall come, saith the Lord|veniunt, dicit Dominus]]: [[8:8|and I will perfect, unto the house of Israel and unto the house of Juda|et consummabo super domum Israel et super domum Juda]], that is, I will give in fulfilment to the people of the Jews, divided into two kingdoms and twelve tribes, [[8:8|a new testament|testamentum novum]]. For Christ in his own person set this before the Jews in the sermon given on the mount, and at the Supper; of whom he also said: [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]].

paras.t: Non secundum testamentum quod feci patribus eorum, id est, non tale testamentum, puta in terrenis promissis et cærimonialibus jussis consistens, dabo istis, quale dedi per Moysen patribus eorum in die qua apprehendi manum illorum, id est, quum eos sic ducerem atque præcederem, sicut pater ducit parvulum filium, per se ire non valentem et viæ ignarum, […] […] terram Ægypti, quod et le[…]ci. Quoniam ipsi non permanserunt per obedientiam cordis in testamento meo, id est in lege a me data, unum verum Deum colendo, sicut lex jubet; sed statim fecerunt vitulum aureum conflatilem, et adoraverunt eum; et ego neglexi, id est, oblivioni tradidi, eos, dicit Dominus, pietatis meæ respectum eis subtrahendo, et multos eorum occidendo. Quomodo autem Deus dicatur recordari vel negligere, dictum est sæpius.
paras.en: [[8:9|Not according to the testament which I made to their fathers|Non secundum testamentum quod feci patribus eorum]], that is, I will not give these such a testament (one, say, consisting in earthly promises and ceremonial commands) as I gave through Moses to their fathers [[8:9|on the day when I took them by the hand|in die qua apprehendi manum illorum]], that is, when I thus led them and went before them, as a father leads a little son who cannot walk by himself and does not know the way[[Osee 11:3||]], […] […] [the lost words probably held the lemma 'to lead them out of'] [[8:9|the land of Egypt|terram Ægypti]], which also le[…]ci [the end of this sentence is lost]. [[8:9|Because they continued not|Quoniam ipsi non permanserunt]] by obedience of heart [[8:9|in my testament|in testamento meo]], that is, in the law given by me, by worshipping the one true God as the Law commands; but straightway they made a molten golden calf and adored it[[Ex 32:4||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxxii, 1–6; the calf is made in v. 4]; [[8:9|and I regarded them not|et ego neglexi]], that is, I gave them over to forgetfulness, [[8:9|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]], by withdrawing from them the regard of my loving-kindness, and by slaying many of them[[Ex 32:28||]]. How God is said to remember or to neglect has been said often.

paras.t: Quia hoc est testamentum novum quod disponam, id est, ordinate proponam, domui Israel, id est electis, præsertim Judæis : quibus primo prædicatum est Evangelium regni; deinde omnibus gentibus Deum per fidem speculantibus dispositum est per Apostolos hoc testamentum : post dies illos, id est post tempus divinitus præordinatum, videlicet consummato cursu veteris testamenti, quando advenit temporis plenitudo. Disponam itaque testamentum hoc eis, dando leges meas in mente eorum, id est, intellectibus eorum imprimam evangelica mandata, et in corde, id est voluntate, eorum superscribam eas, id est, promptum affectum obediendi legibus meis dabo eis. Hoc modo datum est primitivæ Ecclesiæ novum testamentum a Christo, præsertim in die sancto Pentecostes, quando Spiritus Sanctus per inspirationem et supernaturalem illustrationem impressit cordibus discipulorum evangelicam legem. Et ero eis in Deum, id est, pie et gratiose agam cum eis, et ipsi erunt mihi in populum, id est, devote et religiose me colent.
paras.en: [[8:10|For this is the testament which I will make|Quia hoc est testamentum novum quod disponam]] [Denis adds *novum*, 'new'], that is, will set forth in order, [[8:10|to the house of Israel|domui Israel]], that is, to the elect [the name Israel was commonly taken to mean 'a man seeing God'], especially the Jews, to whom the Gospel of the kingdom was preached first; and afterwards this testament was set forth through the Apostles to all the nations that behold God by faith; [[8:10|after those days|post dies illos]], that is, after the time ordained beforehand by God, namely when the course of the Old Testament had been run, when the fulness of time came. So I will make this testament for them: [[8:10|I will give my laws into their mind|dando leges meas in mente eorum]], that is, I will print the Gospel commandments on their understandings, [[8:10|and in their heart|et in corde]], that is, in their will, [[8:10|will I write them|eorum superscribam eas]], that is, I will give them a ready affection to obey my laws. In this way the new testament was given by Christ to the primitive Church, above all on the holy day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:1||]], when the Holy Ghost, by inspiration and supernatural enlightenment, imprinted the Gospel law on the hearts of the disciples. [[8:10|And I will be their God|Et ero eis in Deum]], that is, I will deal with them lovingly and graciously, [[8:10|and they shall be my people|et ipsi erunt mihi in populum]], that is, they will worship me devoutly and religiously.

paras.t: Et non docebit unusquisque proximum suum et unusquisque fratrem suum, dicens : Cognosce Dominum. Secundum Augustinum et alios plerosque, hæc intelligenda sunt pro statu patriæ, in qua omnes non docebunt alium quantum ad cognitionem Dei, et in quibus beatitudo consistit : quamvis superiores docebunt inferiores, quantum ad quosdam effectus divinæ providentiæ. Omnes enim quos beati Deum in medio cum pertinet[…] […] […] a minore usque ad majorem. Et ideo scient me in patria, quia nunc in via propitius ero iniquitatibus eorum, dando eis gratiam pœnitendi, et peccatorum illorum jam non memorabor ad puniendum ea in igne gehennæ.
paras.en: [[8:11|And they shall not teach every man his neighbour and every man his brother, saying: Know the Lord|Et non docebit unusquisque proximum suum et unusquisque fratrem suum, dicens : Cognosce Dominum]]. According to Augustine and very many others, these words are to be understood of the state of the fatherland, in which none shall teach another as regards the knowledge of God, in which beatitude consists; although the higher will teach the lower as regards certain effects of divine providence. For all [the transcription here reads *quos beati Deum in medio cum*, which cannot be construed; it seems to have spoken of the blessed seeing God] pertain[…] […] […] [[8:11|from the least to the greatest|a minore usque ad majorem]]. And therefore they shall know me in the fatherland, [[8:12|Because|quia]] now, on the way [that is, in this life, while they are still wayfarers], [[8:12|I will be merciful to their iniquities|propitius ero iniquitatibus eorum]], by giving them the grace of repentance, [[8:12|and their sins I will remember no more|et peccatorum illorum jam non memorabor]], to punish them in the fire of hell.

paras.t: Alii exponunt hæc specialiter de primitiva Ecclesia, maxime de Apostolis, qui omnes immediate edocti fuerunt a Spiritu Sancto. Videtur autem generaliter posse intelligi de ipsa Ecclesia militanti, sic tamen ut sit distributio pro generibus singulorum, et locutio comparativa. Non enim loquitur Dominus de quacumque doctrina seu scientia, sed specialiter de cognitione sui : Quoniam omnes scient me, inquit. Quum ergo per orbem terrarum in Ecclesia militanti exstirpata sit idololatria, omnes scient me esse unum dumtaxat verum Deum. Tanta quoque est misericordia Dei hoc tempore, ut dicatur tempus gratiæ. Vel dicuntur hæc comparative. In tantum quippe abundat cognitio Dei in mundo tempore evangelicæ legis magis quam ante, ut jam pene omnes videantur cognoscere Deum. Et juxta hunc sensum scriptum est : Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes. In omnem enim terram exivit sonus Apostolorum.
paras.en: Others explain these words specially of the primitive Church, and above all of the Apostles, who were all taught immediately by the Holy Ghost. But it seems they can be understood generally of the Church militant itself, yet so that the distribution is for the kinds of individuals [*distributio pro generibus singulorum*: 'all' means people of every kind, not every single person], and the speech is comparative. For the Lord is not speaking of any teaching or knowledge whatever, but specially of the knowledge of himself: [[8:11|For all shall know me|Quoniam omnes scient me]], he says. Since then idolatry has been rooted out throughout the world in the Church militant, all shall know me to be the one and only true God. So great too is the mercy of God in this time that it is called the time of grace. Or else these things are said comparatively: for in the time of the Gospel law the knowledge of God abounds in the world so much more than before that now almost all seem to know God. And in this sense it is written: [[Is 11:9|the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea|Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes]]. For [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem enim terram exivit sonus Apostolorum]] [Denis writes 'the sound of the Apostles' for the Psalm's 'their sound'].

paras.t: Consequenter pandit Apostolus cessationem veteris testamenti. Dicendo autem Dominus per Jeremiam, novum, id est, testamentum Christi novum vocando, veteravit, id est, vetus esse declaravit, prius testamentum datum per Moysen. Quod autem antiquatur et senescit, prope interitum est, id est, cito corrumpetur. Ideo testamentum illud evacuatur adveniente testamento Christi, quod usque in finem sæculi perseverabit.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows the ceasing of the Old Testament. [[8:13|Now in saying|Dicendo autem]], namely the Lord through Jeremias, [[8:13|a new|novum]], that is, by calling the testament of Christ new, [[8:13|he hath made the former old|veteravit]], that is, he declared [[8:13|the former|prius]] testament, given through Moses, to be old. [[8:13|And that which decayeth and groweth old is near its end|Quod autem antiquatur et senescit, prope interitum est]], that is, it will soon perish. Therefore that testament is made void at the coming of the testament of Christ, which will last until the end of the world.

9.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI NONI : HABUIT QUIDEM ET PRIUS JUSTIFICATIONES, ETC.
9.title_en: Exposition of the ninth chapter: The former indeed had also justifications of divine service, etc.

paras.t: Denique excellentiam sacerdotii Christi consequenter ostendit Apostolus ex ritu et schemate tabernaculi. Habuit quidem et prius, id est præcedens et vetus testamentum, justificationes culturæ, id est observantias auferentes impedimenta quædam divini cultus. Quemadmodum enim sacramenta novæ legis virtute gratiæ in eis contentæ, purgant a vitiis interioribus, quibus fit homo simpliciter ineptus ad cultum divinum ; sic sacramenta veteris legis gratiam non continentia, emundabant a corporalibus immunditiis et irregularitatibus, propter quas prohibebantur Judæi a cultu divino, scilicet ab accessu templi et cœtus fidelium, sicut erant contactus mortui vel immundi. Hæ ergo observationes, per quas talia impedimenta tollebantur, dicuntur justificationes culturæ.
paras.en: Next, the Apostle goes on to show the excellence of Christ's priesthood from the rite and the plan of the tabernacle. [[9:1|The former indeed had also|Habuit quidem et prius]], that is, the preceding and old testament, [[9:1|justifications of divine service|justificationes culturæ]], that is, observances that took away certain hindrances to divine worship. For as the sacraments of the new law, by the power of the grace contained in them, cleanse from the inward vices by which a man is made simply unfit for divine worship, so the sacraments of the old law, which did not contain grace, cleansed from bodily uncleannesses and irregularities [that is, legal disqualifications from taking part in worship], on account of which the Jews were barred from divine worship, that is, from access to the temple and to the assembly of the faithful: such as the touching of a dead body or of something unclean[[Lev 5:2||]]. These observances, then, by which such hindrances were taken away, are called [[9:1|justifications of divine service|justificationes culturæ]].

paras.t: Habuit quoque et sanctum sæculare, id est exteriorem quamdam immunditiam hominibus apparentem. Quidam per sanctum sæculare, intelligunt templum materiale, quod Judæi sanctum putabant, et aliquo modo erat, quia ad cultum Dei fuerat ordinatum. Cui expositioni consonat littera sequens.
paras.en: It had also [[9:1|a sanctuary|sanctum sæculare]] [Latin *sanctum sæculare*, literally "a worldly holy thing"], that is, a certain outward cleanness apparent to men [the Latin reads *immunditiam*, "uncleanness", evidently a slip for *munditiam*, "cleanness"]. Some understand by the *worldly sanctuary* the material temple, which the Jews thought holy, and which in some manner was so, because it had been ordained for the worship of God. With this exposition the text that follows agrees.

paras.t: Tabernaculum enim factum est primum, id est, primum tabernaculum humano artificio fabricatum est. Per primum autem tabernaculum, designatur exterior pars tabernaculi a Moyse facti, a qua erat ingressus. Per secundum vero tabernaculum, significatur interior pars ejusdem tabernaculi. Tabernaculum enim Moysis, habens triginta cubitos in longitudine, decem vero in latitudine, et decem in altitudine, quantum ad longitudinem divisum erat in duas partes per cortinam seu velum intermedium, quarum exterior habuit viginti cubitos in longitudine. Et propter suam venerationem, et significationem qua significavit Ecclesiam militantem, dicebatur Sanctum vel Sancta. Interior vero pars tabernaculi post cortinam, dicta est Sancta vel Sanctum sanctorum, propter præcipuam suam venerationem, et quoniam figuravit Ecclesiam triumphantem.
paras.en: [[9:2|For there was a tabernacle made the first|Tabernaculum enim factum est primum]], that is, the first tabernacle was built by human craft[[Ex 26:1||]][[Ex 27:1||]]. By the first tabernacle is meant the outer part of the tabernacle made by Moses, by which one went in; by the second tabernacle, the inner part of the same tabernacle. For the tabernacle of Moses, which was thirty cubits in length, ten in breadth and ten in height, was divided lengthwise into two parts by a curtain or veil in between[[Ex 26:33||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxv, 33; the veil that divides the tabernacle is at Ex 26:33], and of these the outer part was twenty cubits long. And on account of the veneration due to it, and of its meaning, for it signified the Church militant, it was called the Holy or the Holies. But the inner part of the tabernacle, behind the curtain, was called the Holies or the Holy of Holies, on account of the special veneration due to it, and because it figured the Church triumphant.

paras.t: In quo primo tabernaculo erant candelabra, id est unum candelabrum aureum, quod hic pluraliter candelabra dicitur, quia habebat septem lucernas. Hoc fuit in parte meridionali. Et mensa propositionis quadrata, facta de lignis setim, atque purissimo auro vestita. Hæc fuit in parte aquilonari. Et propositio panum, id est duodecim panes, qui quolibet sabbato ponebantur super mensam recentes. Erat quoque in hac parte tabernaculi altare incensi, de quo tacet Apostolus. Quod primum tabernaculum dicitur Sancta, sicut jam patuit.
paras.en: [[9:2|wherein|In quo]], that is, in the first tabernacle, [[9:2|were the candlesticks|erant candelabra]], that is, one golden candlestick[[Ex 25:31||]], which is here called candlesticks in the plural because it had seven lamps[[Ex 25:37||]]. This stood on the south side. [[9:2|and the table|Et mensa]] of proposition[[Ex 25:30||]], square, made of setim wood[[Ex 25:23||]] and overlaid with the purest gold. This stood on the north side. [[9:2|and the setting forth of loaves|Et propositio panum]], that is, twelve loaves[[Lev 24:5||]], which were set fresh upon the table every sabbath. There was also in this part of the tabernacle the altar of incense[[Ex 30:1||]], of which the Apostle says nothing. This first tabernacle, then, is that [[9:2|which is called the Holy|dicitur Sancta]], as has already been shown.

paras.t: Post velamentum autem, id est retro velum seu post cortinam intermediam, erat secundum tabernaculum, id est secunda pars totius tabernaculi, quod secundum dicitur Sancta sanctorum, propter rationem prædictam, aureum habens thuribulum. De hoc non legitur in veteri Testamento. Propter quod quidam per thuribulum intelligunt incensorium, in quo summus sacerdos Sanctum sanctorum ingrediens, ponebat incensum, ut fumus inde consurgens, impediret eos qui erant in alia parte tabernaculi, ne adspicerent ea quæ fuerant in secunda parte tabernaculi. Alii opinantur quod tempore David vel Salomonis, dum auctus est cultus divinus, factum et illic locatum sit thuribulum aureum. Et arcam testamenti, […] tectum ex omni parte auro. Erat namque de imputribilibus lignis setim, intus et extra aureis laminis cooperta. In qua arca erat urna aurea habens manna ad mensuram gomor, in commemorationem miraculi quo Deus pavit filios Israel manna annis quadraginta in deserto, […] Aaron quæ fronduerat intra unam noctem, in signum quod Aaron divinitus electus esset in sacerdotem, et tabulæ testamenti, id est duæ tabulæ in quibus lex scripta fuit, puta Decalogus.
paras.en: [[9:3|And after the second veil|Post velamentum autem]], that is, behind the veil or after the curtain in the middle, was the second [[9:3|tabernacle|secundum tabernaculum]] [Denis takes *secundum*, "second", with *tabernaculum*, not with *velamentum*, "veil", as the Douay-Rheims does], that is, the second part of the whole tabernacle, [[9:3|which is called the Holy of Holies|quod secundum dicitur Sancta sanctorum]], for the reason given above, [[9:4|Having a golden censer|aureum habens thuribulum]]. Of this nothing is read in the Old Testament. For which reason some understand by the censer the incense-burner in which the high priest, entering the Holy of Holies, put incense, so that the smoke rising from it might keep those who were in the other part of the tabernacle from seeing the things that were in the second part of the tabernacle[[Lev 16:12||]][[Lev 16:13||]]. Others think that in the time of David or of Solomon, when divine worship was enlarged, a golden censer was made and placed there. [[9:4|and the ark of the testament|Et arcam testamenti]], […] [[9:4|covered about on every part with gold|tectum ex omni parte auro]]. For it was of the incorruptible setim wood[[Ex 25:10||]], covered within and without with plates of gold[[Ex 25:11||]]. [[9:4|in which was a golden pot that had manna|In qua arca erat urna aurea habens manna]] to the measure of a gomor[[Ex 16:32||]][[Ex 16:33||]], in memory of the miracle by which God fed the children of Israel with manna for forty years in the desert, […] [[9:4|of Aaron that had blossomed|Aaron quæ fronduerat]] within a single night, as a sign that Aaron had been chosen by God for the priesthood[[Num 17:10||]], [[9:4|and the tables of the testament|et tabulæ testamenti]], that is, the two tables on which the law was written, namely the Decalogue[[3 Kings 8:9||]].

paras.t: Superque eam, id est super arcam, erant duo Cherubim gloriæ, id est gloriose ac splendide facta ad instar angelorum, vel gloriæ Dei figurativa, obumbrantia, id est, alis suis extensis, invicemque connexis, tegentia propitiatorium, id est tabulam auream quæ erat super arcam : quæ ideo dicta est propitiatorium, quoniam inde dedit Deus responsum Moysi pro multitudine exeuntis. De quibus non est modo dicendum per singula. Pauciora namque sufficiunt.
paras.en: [[9:5|And over it|Superque eam]], that is, over the ark, [[9:5|were|erant]] two [[9:5|cherubims of glory|Cherubim gloriæ]], that is, made gloriously and splendidly in the likeness of angels[[Ex 25:18||]], or figuring the glory of God, [[9:5|overshadowing|obumbrantia]], that is, covering with their wings spread out and joined to one another, [[9:5|the propitiatory|propitiatorium]], that is, the golden plate that was over the ark; which is called the propitiatory [that is, the mercy-seat, the place of propitiation] because from there God gave answer to Moses for the multitude as it went on its way[[Ex 25:22||]]. [[9:5|of which it is not needful to speak now particularly|De quibus non est modo dicendum per singula]]. For a few things are enough.

paras.t: Apostolus autem prosequitur hæc breviter et allegorice tantum. His vero ita compositis, id est, duabus partibus tabernaculi prædicto modo dispositis : in priori quidem tabernaculo, quod dicitur Sancta, semper, id est quotidie bis, intrabant sacerdotes, videlicet hora sacrificii matutini ac vespertini : utraque enim hac hora immolabatur agnus ; sacrificiorum officia consummantes, id est, complentes ea quæ ad ritum sacrificiorum spectabant. Immolatio enim sacrificiorum fiebat extra tabernaculum sub dio in atrio in altari holocaustorum : ubi accenso igne, sumpsit sacerdos in thuribulo prunas, sicque procedebat ad altare incensi, intra tabernaculum primum situm ; positoque in thuribulo thure, dimisit super altare incensi, et ita sacrificium consummabatur.
paras.en: The Apostle, however, goes through these things only briefly and allegorically. [[9:6|Now these things being thus ordered|His vero ita compositis]], that is, the two parts of the tabernacle being arranged in the way described: [[9:6|into the first tabernacle|in priori quidem tabernaculo]], which is called the Holy, [[9:6|always|semper]], that is, twice every day, [[9:6|the priests|sacerdotes]] [[9:6|entered|intrabant]], namely at the hour of the morning and of the evening sacrifice, for at each of these hours a lamb was sacrificed[[Num 28:3||]][[Num 28:4||]]; [[9:6|accomplishing the offices of sacrifices|sacrificiorum officia consummantes]], that is, fulfilling what belonged to the rite of the sacrifices. For the sacrifices were slain outside the tabernacle, under the open sky, in the court, on the altar of holocausts[[Lev 16:7||]]; where, the fire being kindled, the priest took live coals in the censer[[Lev 16:12||]], and so went on to the altar of incense, which stood within the first tabernacle; and having put incense in the censer, he set it down upon the altar of incense, and so the sacrifice was completed.

paras.t: In secundo autem tabernaculo, videlicet in Sanctis sanctorum, semel in anno solus pontifex introivit, videlicet in festo Expiationis, non sine sanguine. Tulit enim secum de sanguine hostiæ immolatæ, ad offerendum illum coram propitiatorio. Ideo sequitur : quem sanguinem offerret pro sua et populi ignorantia, id est pro remissione propriorum ac populi sui peccatorum ex ignorantia commissorum. Secundum Glossam, pontifex semper intrabat Sancta sanctorum sine sanguine, sed non nisi semel cum sanguine.
paras.en: [[9:7|But into the second|In secundo autem]] tabernacle, namely into the Holy of Holies, [[9:7|the high priest alone, once a year|semel in anno solus pontifex]] entered, namely on the feast of the Expiation[[Lev 16:2||]][[Lev 16:29||]], [[9:7|not without blood|non sine sanguine]]. For he took with him some of the blood of the victim that had been slain, to offer it before the propitiatory. Therefore there follows: [[9:7|which he offereth for his own and the people's ignorance|quem sanguinem offerret pro sua et populi ignorantia]], that is, for the remission of his own sins and of those of his people, committed through ignorance. According to the Gloss, the high priest always entered the Holy of Holies without blood, but only once with blood.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus mysticam significationem istorum. Hoc significante figuraliter Spiritu Sancto per dispositionem tabernaculi Moysis, nondum propalatam esse Sanctorum viam, id est nondum patefactum esse ingressum regni cœlestis, vel ipsum Christum, qui est via qua itur ad patriam, adhuc priore tabernaculo, id est prima parte tabernaculi quæ dicitur Sancta, habente statum, id est prohibitionem ingrediendi secundum tabernaculum, scilicet Sancta sanctorum. Per velum namque inter partes tabernaculi positum, significabatur clausam esse viam regni cœlestis, quod significabatur per Sancta sanctorum.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows the mystical meaning of these things.
