[[9:8|The Holy Ghost signifying this|Hoc significante figuraliter Spiritu Sancto]] in figure, by the arrangement of the tabernacle of Moses, [[9:8|That the way into the Holies was not yet made manifest|nondum propalatam esse Sanctorum viam]], that is, that the entrance into the heavenly kingdom had not yet been opened, or Christ himself, who is the way by which one goes to the fatherland[[John 14:6||]], [[9:8|whilst the former tabernacle|adhuc priore tabernaculo]], that is, the first part of the tabernacle, which is called the Holy, [[9:8|was yet standing|habente statum]] [Latin *habente statum*, "having its standing", which Denis takes as a barring of the way], that is, the prohibition against entering the second tabernacle, that is, the Holy of Holies. For by the veil set between the parts of the tabernacle it was signified that the way of the heavenly kingdom, which was signified by the Holy of Holies, was shut.

paras.t: Quæ res, videlicet dispositio cultus et ritus tabernaculi, parabola, id est similitudo vel figura, est temporis instantis, scilicet temporis gratiæ, id est eorum quæ in novo testamento geruntur sub tempore gratiæ. Omnia enim in figura contingebant eis. Et vetus testamentum erat figura novi. Juxta quam parabolam, id est legalem et figurativam observantiam, munera de rebus inanimatis, et hostiæ de carnibus animalium, offeruntur a sacerdotibus Leviticæ stirpis pro tempore veteris testamenti. Quæ hostiæ et munera non possunt juxta conscientiam, id est secundum dictamen rectæ conscientiæ, vel intus in conscientia, perfectum, id est a vitiis purum et gratia decoratum, facere servientem, id est eum qui servit Deo, solummodo in cibis et potibus, id est in esu et abstinentia quorumdam alimentorum secundum legis præcepta, quæ quosdam cibos prohibuit, et variis baptismatibus, id est lotionibus corporis seu membri alicujus in aqua propter contactum mortui seu leprosi, et justitiis carnis, id est observantiis corporalem immunditiam seu irregularitatem tollentibus, usque ad tempus correctionis impositis, id est jussis atque durantibus usque ad tempus evangelicæ legis, quæ legem Mosaicam perficit, et observatorum illius vitia corrigit et emendat. Ex divino enim imperio servanda erant usque ad Evangelii publicationem. Itaque præinducta legalia non poterant perfectum facere servientem.
paras.en: [[9:9|Which|Quæ]] thing, namely the arrangement of the worship and rite of the tabernacle, [[9:9|is a parable|parabola]], that is, a likeness or figure, [[9:9|of the time present|est temporis instantis]], namely of the time of grace, that is, of the things that are done in the new testament under the time of grace. For [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|Omnia enim in figura contingebant eis]]; and the old testament was a figure of the new. [[9:9|according to which|Juxta quam]] parable, that is, the legal and figurative observance, [[9:9|gifts|munera]] of lifeless things, [[9:9|and sacrifices|et hostiæ]] of the flesh of animals, [[9:9|are offered|offeruntur]] by the priests of the Levitical stock for the time of the old testament. Which sacrifices and gifts [[9:9|cannot, as to the conscience|non possunt juxta conscientiam]], that is, according to the dictate of a right conscience, or inwardly in the conscience, [[9:9|make him perfect|perfectum]], that is, pure of vices and adorned with grace, [[9:9|that serveth|facere servientem]], that is, him who serves God, [[9:9|only in meats and in drinks|solummodo in cibis et potibus]], that is, in eating certain foods and abstaining from others according to the precepts of the law, which forbade certain foods[[Lev 11:1||]], [[9:10|And divers washings|et variis baptismatibus]] [Latin *baptismatibus*, "baptisms"], that is, washings of the body or of some member in water on account of touching a dead body or a leper, [[9:10|and justices of the flesh|et justitiis carnis]], that is, observances that took away bodily uncleanness or irregularity, [[9:10|laid on them until the time of correction|usque ad tempus correctionis impositis]], that is, commanded and lasting until the time of the gospel law, which perfects the Mosaic law, and corrects and amends the vices of those who kept it. For by divine command they were to be kept until the publishing of the Gospel. And so the legal observances set out above could not [[9:9|make him perfect that serveth|perfectum facere servientem]].

paras.t: Deinde ostendit Apostolus, quid figurabatur per hoc quod summus sacerdos seu pontifex in lege, introivit in Sancta sanctorum cum sanguine, semel in anno, ad deprecandum pro se et pro aliis. Per pontificem enim figuratus est Christus ; per Sancta sanctorum, cœlum. Christus autem adsistens Deo Patri ad interpellandum pro nobis, adsistens quoque seu paratus succurrere nobis, pontifex, id est summus ac sacerdotalis minister, prout homo ; vel, Pontifex, id est suo pontificatu collator ; futurorum, id est cœlestium, bonorum : de quibus legitur in Psalmo, Credo videre bona Domini in terra viventium ; per amplius, id est multo majus atque capacius, et perfectius tabernaculum, utputa cœlum, non manufactum, id est non hominum manibus fabricatum, id est non hujus creationis, hoc est non humanæ industriæ ; vel, Non hujus creationis, id est non exsistens de natura inferiorum creaturarum, quæ corruptibiles sunt : illud enim incorruptibile est ; neque per sanguinem hircorum aut vitulorum, ut pontifex legalis ; sed per proprium sanguinem, id est cum prævia proprii sanguinis effusione, introivit semel, videlicet in die ascensionis, in Sancta, id est in cœleste tabernaculum præfiguratum per Sancta sanctorum, æterna redemptione inventa, id est vera beatitudine nobis recuperata, atque a nobis comperta.
paras.en: Then the Apostle shows what was figured by the high priest or pontiff of the law entering the Holy of Holies with blood once a year, to pray for himself and for others. For by the high priest Christ was figured; by the Holy of Holies, heaven. [[9:11|But Christ, being come|Christus autem adsistens]] [Latin *adsistens*, "standing by", which Denis takes in two ways; the Douay-Rheims has "being come"], standing before God the Father [[Heb 7:25|to make intercession for us|ad interpellandum pro nobis]][[Rom 8:34||]] [the margin gives Rom. viii, 24; the verse on Christ's intercession is Rom 8:34], and standing by also, that is, ready to help us, [[9:11|an high Priest|pontifex]], that is, the supreme and priestly minister, in so far as he is man; or, *high priest*, that is, the bestower by his high priesthood [[9:11|of the good things|bonorum]] [[9:11|to come|futurorum]], that is, heavenly, of which we read in the Psalm: [[Ps 26:13|I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living|Credo videre bona Domini in terra viventium]]; [[9:11|by a greater|per amplius]], that is, much larger and more spacious, [[9:11|and more perfect tabernacle|et perfectius tabernaculum]], namely heaven, [[9:11|not made with hand|non manufactum]], that is, not built by the hands of men, [[9:11|that is, not of this creation|id est non hujus creationis]], that is, not of human skill; or, *not of this creation*, that is, not being of the nature of the lower creatures, which are corruptible, for that tabernacle is incorruptible; [[9:12|Neither by the blood of goats or of calves|neque per sanguinem hircorum aut vitulorum]], as the high priest of the law did, [[9:12|but by his own blood|sed per proprium sanguinem]], that is, with the shedding of his own blood going before, [[9:12|entered once|introivit semel]], namely on the day of the Ascension, [[9:12|into the Holies|in Sancta]], that is, into the heavenly tabernacle prefigured by the Holy of Holies, [[9:12|having obtained eternal redemption|æterna redemptione inventa]] [Latin *inventa*, "found"], that is, true beatitude having been recovered for us and found by us.

paras.t: Quod autem sanguis Christi idoneus fuerit ad salvandum, demonstrat Apostolus. Si enim sanguis hircorum et taurorum, et cinis vitulæ combustæ mixtus aqua, adspersus cum aqua super immundos, inquinatos macula exterioris hominis, sanctificat, id est, purgat a macula tali, ad emundationem carnis, id est ad acquirendam munditiam corporalem. Talia enim, peccata auferre non poterant, sed ab exteriori impuritate mundabant. Quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spiritum Sanctum, id est cooperante ac inspirante Spiritu Sancto, semetipsum ratione naturæ assumptæ, obtulit in cruce immaculatum Deo Patri pro nobis, emundabit conscientiam nostram in Baptismo vel Pœnitentia, seu aliis sacramentis, per quæ virtus seu meritum ejus nobis applicatur, ab operibus mortuis, id est peccatis, ad serviendum, id est, ut a peccatis mundati serviamus, Deo viventi, omnis vitæ fonti principio, in sanctitate et justitia jugiter coram ipso?
paras.en: That the blood of Christ was fit to save, the Apostle shows. [[9:13|For if the blood of goats and of oxen, and the ashes of an heifer|Si enim sanguis hircorum et taurorum, et cinis vitulæ]], burnt and mixed with water, [[9:13|being sprinkled|adspersus]] with the water upon the unclean, [[9:13|sanctify|sanctificat]] [[9:13|such as are defiled|inquinatos]] with a stain of the outward man, that is, cleanse them from such a stain, [[9:13|to the cleansing of the flesh|ad emundationem carnis]], that is, so as to gain bodily cleanness. For such things could not take away sins, but they cleansed from outward impurity. [[9:14|How much more shall the blood of Christ|Quanto magis sanguis Christi]], [[9:14|who by the Holy Ghost|qui per Spiritum Sanctum]], that is, with the Holy Ghost working with him and inspiring him, [[9:14|offered|obtulit]] [[9:14|himself|semetipsum]], by reason of the nature he had assumed, on the cross, [[9:14|unspotted unto God|immaculatum Deo]] the Father for us, [[9:14|cleanse our conscience|emundabit conscientiam nostram]] in Baptism or Penance, or the other sacraments, through which his power or merit is applied to us, [[9:14|from dead works|ab operibus mortuis]], that is, from sins, [[9:14|to serve|ad serviendum]], that is, so that, cleansed from sins, [[Luke 1:74|we may serve|serviamus]] [[9:14|the living God|Deo viventi]], the fount and beginning of all life, [[Luke 1:75|In holiness and justice|in sanctitate et justitia]] continually [[Luke 1:75|before him|coram ipso]]?

paras.t: Et ideo, id est, quoniam Christus obtulit se pro nobis, idcirco novi testamenti mediator, id est medius dator, est, inter Deum et homines medians, et novam legem proponens; ut morte intercedente, id est merito passionis Christi pro nobis interveniente, in redemptionem earum prævaricationum, id est ad obtinendam indulgentiam transgressionum, quæ erant sub priori testamento, id est, tempore veteris testamenti vigebant, nec per legem auferri valebant, repromissionem accipiant, id est, bonum promissum consequantur, qui vocati sunt vocatione æternæ prædestinationis (de qua ad Romanos dicitur, Quos prædestinavit, hos et vocavit) æternæ hereditatis, id est ipsam æternam hereditatem seu felicitatem hominibus promissam. Christi enim morte aperta est janua patriæ, et merito passionis dominicæ omnes electi salvantur. Porro vocatio duplex est, scilicet: æternæ prædestinationis, sicque vocati sunt electi; alia est vocatio præsentis justificationis, de qua in Evangelio legitur, Multi sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
paras.en: [[9:15|And therefore|Et ideo]], that is, since Christ offered himself for us, for that reason [[9:15|he is the mediator of the new testament|novi testamenti mediator]], that is, *medius dator* [a play on *mediator*, read as *medius dator*, "one who gives in the middle"], standing in the middle between God and men[[1 Tim 2:5||]], and setting forth the new law; [[9:15|that by means of his death|ut morte intercedente]], that is, the merit of Christ's passion coming in on our behalf, [[9:15|for the redemption of those transgressions|in redemptionem earum prævaricationum]], that is, to obtain pardon for the transgressions [[9:15|which were under the former testament|quæ erant sub priori testamento]], that is, which flourished in the time of the old testament and could not be taken away by the law[[Rom 3:25||]], [[9:15|they that are called|qui vocati sunt]] with the calling of eternal predestination (of which it is said to the Romans: [[Rom 8:30|whom he predestinated, them he also called|Quos prædestinavit, hos et vocavit]]) [[9:15|may receive the promise|repromissionem accipiant]], that is, may attain the good that was promised, [[9:15|of eternal inheritance|æternæ hereditatis]], that is, the eternal inheritance itself, or the happiness promised to men. For by the death of Christ the gate of the fatherland was opened, and by the merit of the Lord's passion all the elect are saved. Now calling is twofold: one is of eternal predestination, and in this way the elect are called; the other is the calling of present justification, of which we read in the Gospel: [[Matt 20:16|many are called but few chosen|Multi sunt vocati, pauci vero electi]].

paras.t: Quod autem testamentum novum confirmatum sit per Christi passionem, probat Apostolus primo per consuetudinem humanam. Ubi enim testamentum est, mors necesse est intercedat testatoris, id est, ad valorem ac robur testamenti hominis requiritur, ut mors testatoris interveniat seu mediet inter testamenti dispositionem et ejus confirmationem. Testamentum enim […] in mortuis, id est per mortem testatorum, confirmatum est: alioquin nondum valet, id est, nondum efficaciam habet testamentum, dum vivit qui testatus est, id est, qui testamentum condidit. Hoc ita est secundum leges civiles atque canonicas. Nam ante mortem potest mutari, quum sit ultima voluntas testatoris. Simili modo novum testamentum, quod est promissio vitæ æternæ evangelicaque doctrina, in morte Christi firmatum est. Unde in cruce dicebat: Consummatum est. In assertionem enim promissionis ac doctrinæ suæ mori voluit Christus.
paras.en: That the new testament was confirmed by the passion of Christ, the Apostle proves first from human custom. [[9:16|For where there is a testament the death of the testator must of necessity come in|Ubi enim testamentum est, mors necesse est intercedat testatoris]], that is, for a man's testament to be valid and firm it is required that the death of the testator come in, or stand in the middle, between the making of the testament and its confirmation. [[9:17|For a testament|Testamentum enim]] […] [[9:17|after men are dead|in mortuis]], that is, by the death of the testators, [[9:17|is of force|confirmatum est]]: [[9:17|otherwise it is as yet of no strength|alioquin nondum valet]], that is, the testament as yet has no effect, [[9:17|whilst the testator liveth|dum vivit qui testatus est]], that is, he who made the testament. This is so according to both the civil and the canon laws. For before death it can be changed, since it is the last will of the testator. In like manner the new testament, which is the promise of eternal life and the teaching of the gospel, was made firm in the death of Christ. Hence on the cross he said: [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]. For Christ willed to die in confirmation of his promise and of his teaching.

paras.t: Consequenter probat Apostolus idem auctoritate divina. Unde nec primum quidem, id est in principio legis datæ; vel, Primum, id est vetus testamentum, sine sanguine dedicatum, id est roboratum, est, ad figurandum quod novum testamentum Christi sanguine firmaretur. Lecto enim omni mandato legis morali, cæremoniali, ac judiciali a Moyse universo populo Israel, accipiens Moyses sanguinem vitulorum et hircorum oblatorum, cum aqua, id est aqua admixtum: quod præfiguravit mundationem quæ fit in aqua Baptismi virtute sanguinis Christi, de cujus latere exivit sanguis et aqua, quorum virtute omnia sacramenta efficaciam sortiuntur; et lana coccinea et hyssopo. De his duobus fecit adspersorium ad sanguinem adspergendum. Verumtamen in Exodo non fit mentio nisi de sanguine vitulorum; sed credendum est Apostolo, quod alia nunc expressa, tunc aderant. Ipsum quoque librum legis, et omnem populum cui lex conferebatur, adspersit. Fortassis ponit partem pro toto. Non enim videntur tot millia sanguine a Moyse adspersa. Adspersit ergo eos, dicens: Hic sanguis testamenti est, id est roborativus testamenti, quod mandavit ad vos Deus, id est, per me vobis misit ac jussit. Etiam […] id est, in quibus ministrabant Levitæ ac sacerdotes in tabernaculo Moysis, […] similiter adspersit, non tunc quando […] librum adspersit et populum : nondum enim factum erat tabernaculum et vasa ipsius ; sed ista adspersio facta est in die consecrationis tabernaculi atque vasorum.
paras.en: Next the Apostle proves the same by divine authority. [[9:18|Whereupon neither was the first indeed|Unde nec primum quidem]], that is, at the beginning, when the law was given; or, *the first*, that is, the old testament, [[9:18|dedicated without blood|sine sanguine dedicatum]], that is, made strong, to figure that the new testament would be made firm by the blood of Christ. [[9:19|For when every commandment of the law had been read|Lecto enim omni mandato legis]], moral, ceremonial and judicial, [[9:19|by Moses to all the people|a Moyse universo populo]] of Israel[[Ex 24:7||]][[Ex 24:8||]], Moses, [[9:19|he took the blood of calves and goats|accipiens Moyses sanguinem vitulorum et hircorum]] that had been offered, [[9:19|with water|cum aqua]], that is, mixed with water: which prefigured the cleansing that is done in the water of Baptism by the power of the blood of Christ, from whose side [[John 19:34|there came out blood and water|exivit sanguis et aqua]], by whose power all the sacraments receive their efficacy; [[9:19|and scarlet wool and hyssop|et lana coccinea et hyssopo]]. Of these two he made a sprinkler to sprinkle the blood. Yet in Exodus no mention is made except of the blood of calves[[Ex 24:5||]]; but we must believe the Apostle that the other things named here were there then. And he [[9:19|sprinkled|adspersit]] [[9:19|both the book itself|Ipsum quoque librum]] of the law, [[9:19|and all the people|et omnem populum]] to whom the law was being given. Perhaps he puts the part for the whole, for so many thousands do not seem to have been sprinkled with blood by Moses. He sprinkled them, then, [[9:20|Saying: This is the blood of the testament|dicens: Hic sanguis testamenti est]], that is, the blood that makes the testament strong, [[9:20|which God hath enjoined unto you|quod mandavit ad vos Deus]], that is, has sent and commanded to you through me. [[9:21|also|Etiam]] […], that is, those with which the Levites and priests ministered in the tabernacle of Moses, […] [[9:21|in like manner, he sprinkled|similiter adspersit]], not at the time when […] he sprinkled the book and the people, for the tabernacle and its vessels had not yet been made; but this sprinkling was done on the day of the consecration of the tabernacle and of the vessels[[Num 7:1||]].

paras.t: Et omnia pene in sanguine, id est sanguinis adspersione seu effusione, mundantur ab exteriori immunditia vel ineptitudine, secundum legem. Dicit, Pene, quoniam aliqua mundabantur per ignem, videlicet quæ ignem poterant sustinere, et aliqua vasa mundabantur per aquam. Et sine sanguinis effusione facta in aliquo sacrificio, non fit remissio, id est, non fiebat expiatio culpæ, nisi necessitas impediret oblationem. Tunc enim sufficiebat bonum propositum. Hoc fuit figura quod per effusionem sanguinis Christi fit remissio peccatorum. In nobis quippe nihil mundatur interius sine sanguine Christi.
paras.en: [[9:22|And almost all things|Et omnia pene]] [[9:22|with blood|in sanguine]], that is, by the sprinkling or shedding of blood, [[9:22|are cleansed|mundantur]] from outward uncleanness or unfitness, [[9:22|according to the law|secundum legem]]. He says *almost*, because some things were cleansed by fire, namely those that could bear the fire, and some vessels were cleansed by water[[Num 31:23||]] [the margin gives Ibid. xxx, 23, that is, Numbers; the passage is Num 31:23]. [[9:22|and without shedding of blood|Et sine sanguinis effusione]] made in some sacrifice [[9:22|there is no remission|non fit remissio]], that is, there was no expiation of guilt, unless necessity prevented the offering, for then a good purpose was enough. This was a figure that through the shedding of the blood of Christ the remission of sins is made. For in us nothing is cleansed inwardly without the blood of Christ[[1 John 1:7||]].

paras.t: Necesse est ergo exemplaria quidem, id est figuras, cœlestium, id est Ecclesiæ militantis, cujus conversatio est in cœlis, his mundari, videlicet sanguine sacrificiorum. Exemplaria dicit ea quæ erant in veteri testamento, et figurabant ea quæ in Ecclesia fiunt. Ipsa autem cœlestia, id est personas ecclesiasticas ad cœlum tendentes, necesse est mundari melioribus hostiis quam istis legalibus, utputa corpore et sanguine Christi : aliter non ingrederentur regnum cœleste. Sed ingrediuntur post mortem in illud, sequendo caput suum, videlicet Christum. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: [[9:23|It is necessary therefore that the patterns|Necesse est ergo exemplaria quidem]], that is, the figures, [[9:23|of heavenly things|cœlestium]], that is, of the Church militant, whose [[Phil 3:20|conversation is in heaven|conversatio est in cœlis]], [[9:23|should be cleansed with these|his mundari]], namely with the blood of sacrifices. He calls *patterns* the things that were in the old testament and figured what is done in the Church. [[9:23|but the heavenly things themselves|Ipsa autem cœlestia]], that is, the persons of the Church who are making their way to heaven, must be cleansed [[9:23|with better sacrifices than these|melioribus hostiis quam istis]] of the law, namely with the body and blood of Christ; otherwise they would not enter the heavenly kingdom. But after death they do enter it, following their head, namely Christ[[Eph 1:22||]]. Therefore there is added:

paras.t: Non enim in manufacta Sancta, id est in tabernacula terrena hominum artificio fabricata, ut erat tabernaculum Moysis, Jesus introivit finaliter, scilicet in ascensione, quamvis ante passionem ingressus sit templum et synagogas, exemplaria, id est figuras, verorum, id est cœlestium. Sunt enim æterna tabernacula de quibus in Evangelio legitur, quorum figuræ sunt manufacta Sancta vitæ præsentis. Sed in ipsum cœlum empyreum introivit Jesus in ascensione, ut appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis, id est, Patri se ipsum præsentet ad interpellandum pro nobis. Hæc est una causa ascensionis Christi.
paras.en: [[9:24|For|Non enim]] [[9:24|into the Holies made with hands|in manufacta Sancta]], that is, into earthly tabernacles built by the craft of men, as the tabernacle of Moses was, [[9:24|Jesus is not entered|Jesus introivit]] at the last, namely in the Ascension, though before his passion he went into the temple and the synagogues[[John 18:20||]] [the margin gives Joann. xxvi, 20, which does not exist; the passage is John 18:20], [[9:24|the patterns|exemplaria]], that is, the figures, [[9:24|of the true|verorum]], that is, of the heavenly. For there are [[Luke 16:9|everlasting dwellings|æterna tabernacula]] [Latin *tabernacula*, "tabernacles"], of which we read in the Gospel, whose figures are the Holies made with hands of the present life. [[9:24|But into Heaven itself|Sed in ipsum cœlum]], the empyrean [that is, the highest heaven], Jesus entered in the Ascension[[Mark 16:19||]], [[9:24|that he may appear now in the presence of God for us|ut appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis]], that is, that he may present himself to the Father to make intercession for us[[Rom 8:34||]]. This is one reason for Christ's ascension.

paras.t: Neque ut sæpe offerat semetipsum, id est, non ideo Christus intravit in cœlum, et Patri pro nobis apparet, ut frequenter pro nostra salute patiatur, quemadmodum pontifex legis intrat, id est, intravit, sub veteri testamento, in Sancta sanctorum per singulos annos, id est unoquoque anno semel, in sanguine alieno, id est cum sanguine hircorum ac vitulorum quem offert. Propter insufficientiam enim hostiarum legalium, necesse erat eas sæpius iterari. Nec pontifex ingreditur Sancta sanctorum per proprium sanguinem. Hostia vero quam obtulit Christus, ob suæ dignitatis efficaciam sufficientissima est omnium auferre peccata : ideo non oportet eam reiterari, seu Christum denuo pati. Alioqui, id est, si ita non esset, sed oporteret eam iterari, sequitur quod oportebat eum, videlicet Christum, frequenter pati ab origine mundi usque in præsens, imo et usque in finem sæculi hujus. Ab origine namque mundi usque ad finem continuantur, multiplicantur, et vigent scelera hominum. Verumtamen Joannes in Apocalypsi : Agnus, inquit, qui occisus est ab origine mundi. Sed hoc intelligendum est, quod passio Christi profuit futura, sicut et facta. Nunc autem, id est in principio temporis gratiæ, semel, puta in die Parasceves, in consummatione sæculorum, id est in fine seu ultima mundi ætate (nos enim sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt : unde Joannes testatur, Novissima hora est), ad destructionem peccati, id est propter tollenda peccata, per hostiam suam apparuit, id est, per sui ipsius oblationem in cruce præsentatus est.
paras.en: [[9:25|Nor yet that he should offer himself often|Neque ut sæpe offerat semetipsum]], that is, Christ did not enter heaven and appear before the Father for us so that he might suffer often for our salvation, [[9:25|as the high priest|quemadmodum pontifex]] of the law [[9:25|entereth|intrat]], that is, entered, under the old testament[[Lev 16:2||]][[Lev 16:14||]], [[9:25|into the Holies|in Sancta sanctorum]] [[9:25|every year|per singulos annos]], that is, once in each year, [[9:25|with the blood of others|in sanguine alieno]], that is, with the blood of goats and calves, which he offers. For because the victims of the law were not sufficient, they had to be repeated often. Nor does the high priest enter the Holy of Holies by his own blood. But the victim that Christ offered, by the efficacy of its dignity, is fully sufficient to take away the sins of all; therefore it need not be repeated, nor Christ suffer again. [[9:26|For then|Alioqui]], that is, if it were not so, but it had to be repeated, it follows that [[9:26|he ought|oportebat eum]], namely Christ, [[9:26|to have suffered often from the beginning of the world|frequenter pati ab origine mundi]] until now, and indeed until the end of this world. For from the beginning of the world until the end the crimes of men go on, multiply and flourish. Yet John says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 13:8|the Lamb|Agnus]] [[Apoc 13:8|which was slain from the beginning of the world|qui occisus est ab origine mundi]]. But this is to be understood thus: that the passion of Christ availed while it was still to come, as it does now that it has been accomplished. [[9:26|But now|Nunc autem]], that is, at the beginning of the time of grace, [[9:26|once|semel]], namely on the day of the Parasceve [that is, Good Friday], [[9:26|at the end of ages|in consummatione sæculorum]], that is, at the end, or the last age, of the world (for we are those [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]]; whence John bears witness: [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]]), [[9:26|for the destruction of sin|ad destructionem peccati]], that is, to take away sins, [[9:26|by the sacrifice of himself|per hostiam suam]] [[9:26|he hath appeared|apparuit]], that is, was presented by the offering of himself on the cross.

paras.t: Præterea probat Apostolus, quod Christus non debuit nisi semel pro hominibus pati, per simile seu exemplum. Et quemadmodum statutum, id est a divina sapientia ac justitia determinatum seu præfixum, est hominibus semel mori in pœnam originalis peccati, post hoc autem, id est post mortem, fit eis judicium particulare sigillatim statim dum moriuntur, et universale in fine mundi: sic et Christus semel oblatus est in cruce ad multorum exhaurienda, id est extrahenda ac dirimenda, peccata. Ad omnium enim exhaurienda peccata oblatus est secundum sufficientiam, sed ad electorum tollenda peccata oblatus dumtaxat est secundum efficientiam. Hoc dictum est sæpius. Secundo autem, id est post hæc, nempe in secundo suo adventu, sine peccato apparebit, id est, sine similitudine peccati videbitur : non in carne passibili, quæ est similitudo carnis peccati, sed in glorioso corpore, cujus puritas erit omnibus conspicua ; exspectantibus se longanimiter. Apparebit autem eis in salutem, id est ad æternam felicitatem eis tunc largiendam.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle proves by a likeness or example that Christ ought to suffer for men only once. [[9:27|And as it is appointed|Et quemadmodum statutum]], that is, determined or fixed beforehand by the divine wisdom and justice, [[9:27|unto men once to die|est hominibus semel mori]], as the penalty of original sin, [[9:27|and after this|post hoc autem]], that is, after death, there comes to them [[9:27|the judgment|judicium]]: the particular one, of each singly, straightway as they die, and the universal one at the end of the world: [[9:28|So also Christ was offered once|sic et Christus semel oblatus est]] on the cross [[9:28|to exhaust|exhaurienda]], that is, to draw out and do away, [[9:28|the sins|peccata]] [[9:28|of many|ad multorum]][[Rom 5:9||]][[1 Tim 2:6||]]. For he was offered to exhaust the sins of all as to sufficiency, but to take away the sins of the elect only as to efficacy [that is, his offering is enough for all, but takes effect only in the elect]. This has been said often. [[9:28|The second time|Secundo autem]], that is, after this, namely at his second coming, [[9:28|he shall appear without sin|sine peccato apparebit]], that is, he will be seen without the likeness of sin: not in flesh that can suffer, which is the [[Rom 8:3|likeness of sinful flesh|similitudo carnis peccati]], but in a glorious body, whose purity will be plain to all; [[9:28|to them that expect him|exspectantibus se]] with long-suffering. And he will appear to them [[9:28|unto salvation|in salutem]], that is, to bestow eternal happiness on them then.

10.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI DECIMI : UMBRAM ENIM HABENS LEX FUTURORUM BONORUM, ETC.
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: For the law having a shadow of the good things to come, etc.

paras.t: Quoniam in præcedenti capitulo dictum est, quod per sacrificia legis non auferebantur peccata, sed quod Christus unica sui ipsius oblatione abstersit omnium vitia, quantum in ipso est, ideo nunc declarat Apostolus hoc ipsum lucidius.
paras.en: Since it was said in the preceding chapter that sins were not taken away by the sacrifices of the law[[Heb 9:9||]], but that Christ by the single offering of himself wiped away the vices of all, as far as lies in him, the Apostle now declares this same thing more clearly [the margin also gives Hebr. x, 1–4, the verses expounded next].

paras.t: Umbram enim, id est obscuram et remotam similitudinem, habens lex Moysis futurorum bonorum, id est cœlestium præmiorum, non ipsam imaginem rerum, id est non expressam et propinquam similitudinem eorumdem. Ut enim Dionysius protestatur, status evangelicæ legis, medius est inter statum Synagogæ seu veteris Testamenti ac patriæ: ideo sacramenta et cærimonialia novæ legis habent imaginem, id est perfectam similitudinem bonorum cœlestium. Aperte enim ea promittunt, significant, et ad ea immediate introducunt. Sacramenta vero et cærimoniæ veteris legis umbram eorum habuerunt. Non enim promittebant nec figurabant bona ista futura in lege, nisi sub velamine et confuse. Per singulos annos in eisdem ipsis hostiis, id est eisdem sacrificiis, quas offerunt sacerdotes indesinenter, videlicet bis omni die in Sancta, et semel in anno pontifex in Sancta sanctorum, numquam potest accedentes, id est, lex per hostias istas nunquam valet populum pro quo offertur, vel sacerdotem qui hostiam offert, perfectos facere, id est a vitiis expurgare et gratia decorare.
paras.en: [[10:1|For the law, having a shadow|Umbram enim]], that is, an obscure and distant likeness (the law of Moses), [[10:1|of the good things to come|futurorum bonorum]], that is, of the heavenly rewards, [[10:1|not the very image of the things|non ipsam imaginem rerum]], that is, not an express and close likeness of them. For as Dionysius affirms, the state of the law of the Gospel is midway between the state of the Synagogue, or of the Old Testament, and that of the fatherland [that is, of heaven]: therefore the sacraments and ceremonies of the new law have the image, that is, the perfect likeness, of the heavenly goods. For they openly promise them and signify them, and lead into them immediately. But the sacraments and ceremonies of the old law had their shadow. For they did not promise or figure those good things to come, in the law, except under a veil and confusedly. The law, [[10:1|every year|Per singulos annos]], [[10:1|by the selfsame sacrifices|in eisdem ipsis hostiis]], that is, by the same sacrifices, [[10:1|which they offer continually|quas offerunt sacerdotes indesinenter]] (namely, the priests twice every day in the Holy place[[Heb 9:6||]], and the high priest once a year in the Holy of holies[[Heb 9:7||]]), [[10:1|can never make the comers thereunto|numquam potest accedentes]]: that is, the law by these sacrifices can never make the people for whom it is offered, or the priest who offers the sacrifice, [[10:1|perfect|perfectos facere]], that is, cleanse them from vices and adorn them with grace.

paras.t: Alioqui, id est, si possent perficere sacerdotes, cessassent hostiæ istæ Deo offerri, ideo quod nullam haberent ultra, videlicet post hostiam immolatam, conscientiam peccati cultores, id est legis observatores, semel mundati intus a vitiis propter hostiæ oblationem semel factam; sed in ipsis hostiarum oblationibus commemoratio peccatorum per singulos annos fit, quoties hostia pro peccato iteratur. Non ergo ablata erant peccata omnia per hostiam primam.
paras.en: [[10:2|For then|Alioqui]], that is, if the priests could make perfect, these sacrifices [[10:2|would have ceased to be offered|cessassent hostiæ istæ Deo offerri]] to God, [[10:2|because|ideo quod]] [[10:2|the worshippers|cultores]], that is, the observers of the law, [[10:2|once cleansed|semel mundati]] within from vices by the offering of the sacrifice made once, [[10:2|should have no|nullam haberent ultra]] (namely, after the victim had been sacrificed) [[10:2|conscience of sin any longer|conscientiam peccati]]; [[10:3|But in them|sed in ipsis]] offerings of the sacrifices [[10:3|there is made a commemoration of sins every year|commemoratio peccatorum per singulos annos fit]], as often as the sacrifice for sin is repeated. Not all sins, therefore, had been taken away by the first sacrifice.

paras.t: Impossibile enim est sanguines hircorum et taurorum, vel similium holocaustorum, auferri peccata: quia nec virtute propria habent vim purgativam peccati, quum sit quid corporeum, non attingens nec agens in animam; nec ex influxu divinæ virtutis, quemadmodum sacramenta novæ legis, quamvis sint corporalia. Multoties tamen Moyses dicit, quod qui obtulerit illud vel illud pro peccato tali vel tali, dimittetur ei. Sed illa remissio non fiebat virtute sacrificii, sed fide et devotione offerentis, et propter orationem sacerdotis.
paras.en: [[10:4|For it is impossible that with the blood of oxen and goats|Impossibile enim est sanguines hircorum et taurorum]], or of like holocausts, [[10:4|sin should be taken away|auferri peccata]]: for neither have they by their own power any force to cleanse from sin, since blood is something bodily, which does not reach or act upon the soul; nor do they have it from an inflowing of divine power, as the sacraments of the new law do, though these are bodily things. Yet Moses says many times that if anyone offers this or that for such or such a sin, it shall be forgiven him. But that remission did not come about by virtue of the sacrifice, but by the faith and devotion of the offerer, and because of the prayer of the priest.

paras.t: Ideo Christus Filius Dei […] assumens, id est humanam naturam assumens, dicit in Psalmo ad Patrem: Hostiam de rebus animatis et oblationem de inanimatis noluisti, o Pater, id est, non acceptasti quasi per se idonea ad auferenda peccata, et tempore gratiæ nullo modo ea acceptas; corpus autem aptasti mihi, id est, corpus conveniens ad redimendum genus humanum animæ meæ seu Divinitati unisti, videlicet corpus passibile et immaculatum, atque per omnia rationi obedientissimum. Nostra translatio habet: Aures autem perfecisti mihi. Et redit in idem, quoniam sensus est: Aures obedientes ad sustinendum crucis tormentum mihi donasti.
paras.en: [[10:5|Wherefore|Ideo]] Christ the Son of God, […] assuming, that is, assuming human nature, [[10:5|he saith|dicit]] in the Psalm[[Ps 39:7||]] to the Father: [[10:5|Sacrifice|Hostiam]] of living things [[10:5|and oblation|et oblationem]] of lifeless things [[10:5|thou wouldest not|noluisti]], O Father; that is, thou didst not accept them as fit of themselves to take away sins, and in the time of grace thou dost in no way accept them; [[10:5|but a body thou hast fitted to me|corpus autem aptasti mihi]], that is, thou hast united to my soul, or to the Godhead, a body suited to redeeming the human race, namely a body passible and spotless, and in all things most obedient to reason. Our translation has: [[Ps 39:7|but thou hast pierced ears for me|Aures autem perfecisti mihi]] [the Latin of the psalm is literally "thou hast perfected ears for me"]. And it comes to the same thing, since the sense is: Thou hast given me ears obedient to bear the torment of the cross.

paras.t: Holocautomata, id est sacrificia quæ totaliter incendebantur ad divinæ majestatis honorem, et erant ceteris digniora, et pro peccato, id est sacrificia pro remissione peccati oblata, non tibi placuerunt per se seu propria efficacia, sed ex devotione offerentis. Non enim poterant justificare. Tempore autem novæ legis nullatenus placent Deo. Ideo scriptum est apud Prophetam: Quid dignum offeram Domino? Numquid offeram ei holocautomata? Numquid placari potest Deus in millibus arietum, aut in multis millibus hircorum pinguium? Et apud alium: Numquid carnes sanctæ auferent a te malitias tuas? Et Dominus quoque ait in Psalmo: Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, neque de gregibus tuis hircos.
paras.en: [[10:6|Holocausts|Holocautomata]], that is, the sacrifices which were wholly burnt to the honour of the divine majesty and were worthier than the rest, [[10:6|for sin|et pro peccato]] [Denis's text reads "and for sin", a second kind of sacrifice], that is, sacrifices offered for the remission of sin, [[10:6|did not please thee|non tibi placuerunt]] of themselves or by their own efficacy, but by the devotion of the offerer. For they could not justify. And in the time of the new law they in no way please God. Therefore it is written in the Prophet: [[Mich 6:6|What shall I offer to the Lord that is worthy|Quid dignum offeram Domino?]]? [[Mich 6:6|shall I offer holocausts unto him|Numquid offeram ei holocautomata?]]? [[Mich 6:7|May the Lord be appeased with thousands of rams, or with many thousands of fat he goats?|Numquid placari potest Deus in millibus arietum, aut in multis millibus hircorum pinguium?]] And in another: [[Jer 11:15|shall the holy flesh take away from thee thy crimes|Numquid carnes sanctæ auferent a te malitias tuas?]]? And the Lord also says in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:9|I will not take calves out of thy house: nor he goats out of thy flocks|Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, neque de gregibus tuis hircos]].

paras.t: Tunc, quando videlicet vidi tibi omnia illa displicere, et mihi corpus aptum adesse, dixi: Ecce venio paratus ad passionem, ut me ipsum tibi pro hominibus offeram. In capite libri, id est in principio totius sacræ Scripturæ. Vel, In capite libri, id est in primo psalmo, qui est caput libri Psalmorum: in quo psalmo habetur, In lege Domini voluntas ejus. Vel, In capite libri, id est in notitia prædestinationis æternæ, quæ potissimum meam humanitatem concernit, per quam omnes electi salvantur. Ideo dicitur, In capite, quasi in principali hujus notitia. Scriptum est de me, ut faciam voluntatem tuam, o Deus Pater.
paras.en: [[10:7|Then|Tunc]], that is, when I saw that all those things displeased thee, and that a fitting body was at hand for me, [[10:7|said I: Behold I come|dixi: Ecce venio]], ready for the passion, to offer myself to thee for men. [[10:7|in the head of the book|In capite libri]]: that is, in the beginning of the whole of sacred Scripture. Or, [[10:7|in the head of the book|In capite libri]], that is, in the first psalm, which is the head of the book of Psalms, in which psalm we have: [[Ps 1:2|his will is in the law of the Lord|In lege Domini voluntas ejus]]. Or, [[10:7|in the head of the book|In capite libri]], that is, in the knowledge of eternal predestination, which chiefly concerns my humanity, through which all the elect are saved. That is why it says *in the head*, as it were in the principal part of this knowledge. [[10:7|it is written of me: that I should do thy will, O God|Scriptum est de me, ut faciam voluntatem tuam, o Deus]] the Father[[Ps 39:8||]][[Ps 39:9||]].

paras.t: Insuper præinductam scripturam ad propositum applicans, et quasi exponens Apostolus, subdit: Superius, id est paulo ante, dicens Christus ad Patrem: Quia hostias et oblationes et holocautomata et pro peccato noluisti: quæ jam exposita sunt; nec placita sunt tibi sacrificia exteriora, quæ secundum legem offeruntur: juxta intellectum præmemoratum. Hoc tamen supra dictum non est formaliter, sed virtualiter, quia ex dictis infertur. Tunc dixi: Ecce venio, ut faciam, Deus, voluntatem tuam. Hoc jam dictum est atque expositum. Aufert primum, id est legale sacrificium, et per consequens vetus testamentum, tanquam inutile, ut sequens statuat, id est, novæ legis sacrificium, scilicet Christi sacramentum, stabiliat, jugiterque frequentandum affirmet. Unde per Danielem inducitur: In dimidio hebdomadæ deficiet hostia et sacrificium. De hoc in Isaia multa habentur.
paras.en: Moreover, applying the scripture brought forward to his purpose, and as it were expounding it, the Apostle adds: [[10:8|In saying|dicens]], Christ speaking to the Father, [[10:8|before|Superius]], that is, a little earlier: [[10:8|Sacrifices, and oblations, and holocausts for sin thou wouldest not|Quia hostias et oblationes et holocautomata et pro peccato noluisti]], which have already been expounded; [[10:8|neither are they pleasing to thee|nec placita sunt tibi]], the outward sacrifices, [[10:8|which are offered according to the law|quæ secundum legem offeruntur]], in the sense set out before. Yet this was not said above in so many words, but in effect, since it follows from what was said. [[10:9|Then said I: Behold, I come to do thy will, O God|Tunc dixi: Ecce venio, ut faciam, Deus, voluntatem tuam]]. This has already been said and expounded. [[10:9|He taketh away the first|Aufert primum]], that is, the sacrifice of the law, and consequently the old testament, as useless, [[10:9|that he may establish that which followeth|ut sequens statuat]], that is, that he may establish the sacrifice of the new law, namely the sacrament of Christ, and declare that it is to be frequented continually. Hence it is brought in through Daniel: [[Dan 9:27|in the half of the week the victim and the sacrifice shall fail|In dimidio hebdomadæ deficiet hostia et sacrificium]]. Much is found on this in Isaias[[Is 1:11||]] [the margin gives Is. i only; see especially Is 1:11].

paras.t: In qua voluntate Dei, id est Deo clementer volente, seu voluntate ejus qua voluit Christum pati, sanctificati sumus effective ac principaliter, suscipiendo remissionem culpæ infusionemque gratiæ, per oblationem corporis Jesu Christi semel factam in crucis patibulo, tanquam per causam meritoriam ac instrumentalem.
paras.en: [[10:10|In the which will|In qua voluntate]] of God, that is, by God's merciful willing, or by that will of his by which he willed that Christ should suffer, [[10:10|we are sanctified|sanctificati sumus]] effectively and principally, by receiving the remission of guilt and the infusion of grace, [[10:10|by the oblation of the body of Jesus Christ once|per oblationem corporis Jesu Christi semel]] made on the gibbet of the cross, as by the meritorious and instrumental cause.

paras.t: Ex his infert Apostolus differentiam inter sacerdotem legalem, et Christum sacerdotem nostrum. Et omnis quidem sacerdos legalis præsto est, id est paratus. Loquitur autem Paulus in istis capitulis de præterito per modum præsentis. Quotidie ministrans in prima parte tabernaculi, et eadem specie sæpe offerens hostias, id est frequenter immolans agnum vel aliud simile, quæ nunquam possunt auferre peccata: ut dictum est sæpius. Quotidie namque fiebat juge sacrificium, id est duorum agnorum oblatio, unius de mane, alteriusque de vespere, in prima parte tabernaculi.
paras.en: From this the Apostle infers the difference between the priest of the law and Christ our priest. [[10:11|And every priest indeed|Et omnis quidem sacerdos]] of the law [[10:11|standeth|præsto est]], that is, is ready. (Now in these chapters Paul speaks of the past in the manner of the present.) He stands [[10:11|daily ministering|Quotidie ministrans]] in the first part of the tabernacle, [[10:11|and often offering the same sacrifices|et eadem specie sæpe offerens hostias]] [Denis's text reads *eadem specie*, "of the same kind"], that is, often sacrificing a lamb or something like it, [[10:11|which can never take away sins|quæ nunquam possunt auferre peccata]], as has been said many times. For every day there was the continual sacrifice, that is, the offering of two lambs, one in the morning and the other in the evening[[Ex 29:38||]][[Ex 29:39||]][[Num 28:3||]][[Num 28:4||]][[Num 28:5||]][[Num 28:6||]], in the first part of the tabernacle.

paras.t: Hic autem Christus unam pro peccatis omnibus offerens hostiam, utique semetipsum, in sempiternum sedet, id est sine fine jam requiescit, in dextera Dei Patris, id est in potioribus bonis, seu ad æqualitatem ipsius: de cetero, id est pro tempore restante, exspectans impletionem ordinationis divinæ de hominum justa præmiatione, donec ponantur inimici ejus, id est perversi ac reprobi, scabellum pedum ejus, id est, suæ potestati perfecte subjiciantur, quantum ad exsecutionem et manifestationem, ut sæpius dictum recordor, hoc est, usque in diem judicii, in quo venient ad eum et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei.
paras.en: [[10:12|But this man|Hic autem]], Christ, [[10:12|offering one sacrifice for sins|unam pro peccatis omnibus offerens hostiam]] (for all sins), namely himself, [[10:12|for ever sitteth|in sempiternum sedet]], that is, now rests without end, [[10:12|on the right hand of God|in dextera Dei]] the Father, that is, in his better goods, or in equality with him; [[10:13|From henceforth|de cetero]], that is, for the time remaining, [[10:13|expecting|exspectans]] the fulfilment of the divine ordinance concerning the just rewarding of men, [[10:13|until his enemies be made|donec ponantur inimici ejus]], that is, the perverse and reprobate, [[10:13|his footstool|scabellum pedum ejus]][[Ps 109:1||]] [the margin gives Ps. cx, 1; in the Vulgate numbering this is Ps 109:1], that is, until they are perfectly subjected to his power as to its execution and manifestation, as I remember having said many times: that is, until the day of judgment, in which [[Is 45:25|they shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded|venient ad eum et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei]] [the margin's numerals are lost (Is. […]); the words are those of Is 45:25].

paras.t: Una enim oblatione, id est merito suæ unicæ passionis, seu immolationis in cruce, consummavit, id est, plene redemit, et quantum in se est, ad perfectionem adduxit, in sempiternum sanctificatos, id est electos, seu omnes qui in hoc sæculo per gratiam sanctificantur. Æternam enim beatitudinem eis promeruit, imo gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro.
paras.en: [[10:14|For by one oblation|Una enim oblatione]], that is, by the merit of his one passion, or sacrifice on the cross, [[10:14|he hath perfected|consummavit]], that is, has fully redeemed and, as far as lies in him, brought to perfection, [[10:14|for ever them that are sanctified|in sempiternum sanctificatos]], that is, the elect, or all who in this world are sanctified by grace. For he merited eternal beatitude for them; or rather, grace in the present and glory in the future.

paras.t: Præterea hanc efficientiam oblationis seu passionis Christi semel factæ, probat Apostolus auctoritate Jeremiæ superius allegata. Contestatur autem nos, id est, testimonium nostræ assertioni seu omnibus nobis exhibet et affirmat, et Spiritus Sanctus per Jeremiam. Postquam enim dixit hoc loco Spiritus Sanctus, Hoc autem testamentum quod testabor ad illos post dies illos, dicit Dominus Christus, in cujus persona hæc proprie asseruntur, dabo leges meas in cordibus eorum, et in mentibus eorum superscribam eas; et peccatorum et iniquitatum eorum jam non recordabor amplius. Hæc Jeremiæ auctoritas superius jam inducta est et explanata: idcirco hoc ipsum prætereo. Deinde concludit intentum suum Apostolus. Ubi autem horum remissio, id est in populo Dei, cui peccata remissa sunt merito Christi, jam non est oblatio pro peccato, id est, non requiritur iterata Christi passio seu legalis oblatio pro remissione peccati. Una namque Christi oblatio facta in cruce, sufficiens est. Propter quod omnia sacrificia legis cessare debent.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle proves this efficacy of the offering, or passion, of Christ, made once, by the authority of Jeremias cited above. [[10:15|doth testify this to us|Contestatur autem nos]], that is, gives and affirms a testimony to our assertion, or to all of us: [[10:15|And the Holy Ghost also|et Spiritus Sanctus]], through Jeremias. [[10:15|For after that he said|Postquam enim dixit]], the Holy Ghost, in this place: [[10:16|And this is the testament which I will make unto them after those days, saith the Lord|Hoc autem testamentum quod testabor ad illos post dies illos, dicit Dominus]] (Christ, in whose person these things are properly said), [[10:16|I will give my laws in their hearts and on their minds will I write them|dabo leges meas in cordibus eorum, et in mentibus eorum superscribam eas]][[Jer 31:33||]]; [[10:17|And their sins and iniquities I will remember no more|et peccatorum et iniquitatum eorum jam non recordabor amplius]]. This authority of Jeremias has already been brought forward above and explained[[Heb 8:10||]]: therefore I pass over it here. Then the Apostle concludes what he set out to show. [[10:18|Now, where there is a remission of these|Ubi autem horum remissio]], that is, among the people of God, whose sins have been remitted by the merit of Christ, [[10:18|there is no more an oblation for sin|jam non est oblatio pro peccato]], that is, there is not required a repeated passion of Christ, or an oblation of the law, for the remission of sin. For the one offering of Christ made on the cross is sufficient. For which reason all the sacrifices of the law must cease.

paras.t: Consequenter ponit Apostolus instructionem moralem. Habentes itaque, scilicet, quia per unam oblationem Christi redempti sumus, o fratres, idcirco habentes fiduciam in introitu Sanctorum, id est de ingressu cœlestium mansionum seu patriæ quam Sancti introeunt, in sanguine Christi, id est virtute et merito dominicæ passionis, quia per sanguinem Christi aperta est janua vitæ; qui Christus initiavit, id est, primo paravit ac demonstravit, nobis viam novam et viventem, id est ingressum ad patriam: qui dicitur via nova, quoniam primo a Christo inventa; et vivens, quia ad vitam ducit æternam. Initiavit autem seu inchoavit nobis Christus hanc viam per velamen, id est carnem suam, id est per corporis sui occisionem et ascensionem: quod appellatur velamen, quoniam erat divinæ naturæ seu Verbi vestimentum atque latibulum. De quo apud Isaiam angeli dicunt: Quare ergo rubrum est indumentum tuum?
paras.en: Next the Apostle sets down a moral instruction. [[10:19|Having therefore|Habentes itaque]], namely because we have been redeemed by the one offering of Christ, O [[10:19|brethren|fratres]], therefore having [[10:19|a confidence in the entering into the holies|fiduciam in introitu Sanctorum]], that is, concerning the entry into the heavenly mansions, or the fatherland, which the Saints enter, [[10:19|by the blood of Christ|in sanguine Christi]], that is, by the power and merit of the Lord's passion, since by the blood of Christ the gate of life has been opened; which Christ [[10:20|hath dedicated|initiavit]], that is, first prepared and showed, [[10:20|for us|nobis]], [[10:20|A new and living way|viam novam et viventem]], that is, the entry into the fatherland; which is called a *new* way because it was first found by Christ, and *living* because it leads to eternal life. Now Christ dedicated, or began, this way for us [[10:20|through the veil, that is to say, his flesh|per velamen, id est carnem suam]], that is, through the slaying of his body and its ascension; and this is called a veil because it was the garment and hiding-place of the divine nature, or of the Word. Of which the angels say in Isaias: [[Is 63:2|Why then is thy apparel red|Quare ergo rubrum est indumentum tuum?]]?

paras.t: Habentes quoque et sacerdotem magnum super domum Dei, id est Jesum principem pastorum, et summum pontificem toti Ecclesiæ militantis ac triumphantis præsidentem, accedamus ad Deum, orando, laudando, contemplando, bene vivendo: non cum corporis motu, sed cum corde vero, id est recto et justo, non ficto, in plenitudine fidei, id est fide plenissima, nihil hæsitantes, adspersi corda, id est quantum ad animas, seu intus in mentibus nostris spiritualiter perfusi gratia, eruente nos a conscientia mala, id est a remorsu peccati, ut nihil nobis conscii sumus. Et abluti corpus, id est corpore loti ac emundati, aqua munda, id est unda Baptismatis.
paras.en: Having also [[10:21|a high priest over the house of God|sacerdotem magnum super domum Dei]], that is, Jesus, [[1 Pet 5:4|the prince of pastors|principem pastorum]], and the high priest presiding over the whole Church, militant and triumphant, [[10:22|Let us draw near|accedamus]] to God, by praying, praising, contemplating, living well: not with a movement of the body, but [[10:22|with a true heart|cum corde vero]], that is, upright and just, not feigned, [[10:22|in fulness of faith|in plenitudine fidei]], that is, with the fullest faith, hesitating in nothing, [[10:22|having our hearts sprinkled|adspersi corda]], that is, as to our souls, or inwardly in our minds, spiritually steeped in grace, which delivers us [[10:22|from an evil conscience|a conscientia mala]], that is, from the remorse of sin, so that we are conscious to ourselves of nothing; [[10:22|and our bodies washed|Et abluti corpus]], that is, cleansed and purified in body, [[10:22|with clean water|aqua munda]], that is, with the wave of Baptism.

paras.t: Tales itaque Christo operante effecti, teneamus perseveranter inter prospera et adversa, spei nostræ confessionem, id est confessionem eorum quæ speramus a Deo obtinere: quæ confessio procedit ex spe nobis infusa; indeclinabilem, id est regia via ad cælos tendentem, ita ut nec ad dexteram neque ad sinistram declinet: fidelis enim est Deus qui repromisit, id est, frequenter promisit nobis futura bona in patria.
paras.en: Having been made such, then, by the working of Christ, [[10:23|Let us hold fast|teneamus]] perseveringly, amid prosperity and adversity, [[10:23|the confession of our hope|spei nostræ confessionem]], that is, the confession of the things we hope to obtain from God, a confession which proceeds from the hope infused into us; [[10:23|without wavering|indeclinabilem]] [*indeclinabilem*, literally "not turning aside"], that is, tending to heaven by the royal road, so that it turns aside neither to the right hand nor to the left[[Deut 5:32||]][[Jos 1:7||]]: [[10:23|for he is faithful that hath promised|fidelis enim est Deus qui repromisit]], that is, who has often promised us good things to come in the fatherland[[Deut 31:6||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xxxi, 6" after Jos. i, 7; Josue has no thirty-first chapter, so Deut 31:6 is probably meant].

paras.t: Et consideremus invicem, id est, nos mutuo adspiciamus, pensando quid singuli quique habeant dignum imitatione vel increpatione, in provocationem caritatis et bonorum operum, id est ad hunc finem ut in caritate Dei ac proximi accendamur, atque in bonis operibus excitemur, dum quisque bonum alterius imitatur, ejusque defectum caritative redarguit: quæ omnia sunt caritatis effectus, eamque accendunt. Non tamen esse debemus curiosi scrutatores vel observatores aliorum, sed moderate, prout caritas postulat, unusquisque alium admonere debet sive corripere.
paras.en: [[10:24|And let us consider one another|Et consideremus invicem]], that is, let us look at one another, weighing what each of us has that is worthy of imitation or of reproof, [[10:24|to provoke unto charity and to good works|in provocationem caritatis et bonorum operum]], that is, to this end, that we may be kindled in the love of God and of our neighbour, and stirred up in good works, while each imitates what is good in another and charitably reproves his failing: all of which are effects of charity, and kindle it. Yet we must not be curious searchers or watchers of others; but each ought to admonish or correct another with moderation, as charity requires.

paras.t: Non deserentes collectionem nostram, id est congregationem fratrum seu cœtum fidelium, inter quos habitamus; sicut est consuetudinis quibusdam, qui tempore persecutionis, vel ex præsumptione, levitate aut impatientia recedere quæruntur. Unde Sapiens: Sicut avis, inquit, transmigrans de nido suo, sic vir qui relinquit locum suum. Sed consolantes collectionem, id est fratres nostros, animando eos ad patientiam et inseparabilem unionem. Et tanto magis hoc facite, quanto amplius videritis oculo cordis appropinquantem diem mortis atque judicii particularis. Qui dies quia quotidie appropinquat, debemus quotidie magis ac magis invite collectionem nostram deserere. Scriptum est enim: Ecce quam bonum et quam jucundum habitare fratres in unum.
paras.en: [[10:25|Not forsaking our assembly|Non deserentes collectionem nostram]], that is, the congregation of the brethren, or the company of the faithful among whom we dwell, [[10:25|as some are accustomed|sicut est consuetudinis quibusdam]], who in time of persecution, or out of presumption, levity or impatience, seek to withdraw. Hence the Wise Man: [[Prov 27:8|As a bird|Sicut avis]], he says, [[Prov 27:8|that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that leaveth his place|transmigrans de nido suo, sic vir qui relinquit locum suum]]. [[10:25|but comforting|Sed consolantes]] the assembly, that is, our brethren, encouraging them to patience and to inseparable union. [[10:25|and so much the more|Et tanto magis]] do this, [[10:25|as you see|quanto amplius videritis]] with the eye of the heart [[10:25|the day approaching|appropinquantem diem]] of death and of the particular judgment. Since that day draws nearer every day, we ought every day to be more and more unwilling to forsake our assembly. For it is written: [[Ps 132:1|Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity|Ecce quam bonum et quam jucundum habitare fratres in unum]].

paras.t: Hæc ergo bona agenda et mala vitanda sunt. Voluntarie enim, id est ex habitu, electione, certa malitia seu deliberatione, peccantibus nobis post acceptam notitiam veritatis, id est post cognitionem christianæ doctrinæ, in qua pœnæ impiorum gaudiaque justorum describuntur, jam non relinquitur pro peccatis hostia, id est, talibus non restat sacrificium pro peccatis eorum immolandum aliud a sacrificio seu hostia quam pro nobis obtulit Christus. Et per consequens nulla hostia pro peccatis relinquitur eis, sicut in lege. Christus enim non rursus offeretur pro eis in cruce: imo passio ejus eis non proderit, quum perseverent in malis. Terribilis autem quædam exspectatio judicii, id est metuendum ipsum Dei judicium, et sollicite exspectandum, et ignis æmulatio, id est pœna seu infestatio ignis gehennalis, seu ejus qui præcedet faciem Judicis, de quo legitur: Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus; quæ pœna seu æmulatio consumptura, non annihilatura seu corruptura, sed æternaliter afflictura, et quantum ad bene esse consumptura, est adversarios veritatis, id est æmulos Christi seu reprobos. Quod ostenditur per locum a minori:
paras.en: These good things, then, are to be done, and evil things avoided. [[10:26|For if we sin|peccantibus nobis]] [[10:26|wilfully|Voluntarie enim]] (wilfully, that is, from habit, by choice, out of sure malice or deliberation) [[10:26|after having the knowledge of the truth|post acceptam notitiam veritatis]], that is, after coming to know the Christian teaching, in which the punishments of the wicked and the joys of the just are described, [[10:26|there is now left no sacrifice for sins|jam non relinquitur pro peccatis hostia]]: that is, for such men there remains no sacrifice to be offered for their sins other than the sacrifice or victim which Christ offered for us. And consequently no victim for sins is left them, as there was in the law. For Christ will not be offered again for them on the cross; rather, his passion will not profit them, since they persevere in evil. [[10:27|But a certain dreadful expectation of judgment|Terribilis autem quædam exspectatio judicii]], that is, the very judgment of God, to be feared and anxiously awaited, [[10:27|and the rage of a fire|et ignis æmulatio]] [*æmulatio*, literally "jealousy" or "zeal"], that is, the punishment or assault of the fire of hell, or of the fire that will go before the face of the Judge, of which we read: [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him, and shall burn his enemies round about|Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus]]; [[10:27|which shall consume|quæ pœna seu æmulatio consumptura]] (that punishment or rage, which will not annihilate or corrupt them, but afflict them eternally, and consume them as to their well-being) [[10:27|the adversaries|est adversarios]] of the truth, that is, the rivals of Christ, or the reprobate. This is shown by an argument from the lesser:

paras.t: Irritam enim, id est vacuam, quis faciens, id est transgrediens quis, legem Moysis, sine ulla miseratione judicis, duobus vel tribus testibus moritur, id est, ad testimonium tot testium occiditur, secundum legis præceptum: si tamen peccati magnitudo id exigat. Quanto magis putatis deteriora, id est graviora, mereri supplicia, eum qui Filium Dei conculcaverit, eum inhonorando, ejusque mandata spernendo, et sanguinem testamenti pollutum duxerit, id est, sanguinem Christi quo confirmatum est novum testamentum, parvi penderit, et quasi insufficientem putaverit ad auferenda peccata, ob hoc asserens legalia simul cum Evangelio observanda, in quo sanguine, id est cujus effusione, sanctificatus est, id est a vitiis expurgatus et gratia decoratus, primum in Baptismo, deinde in Pœnitentia, et spiritui gratiæ contumeliam fecerit, id est, gratiam Spiritus Sancti contempserit, seu Spiritum Sanctum, omnis gratiæ collatorem, a se repulerit, ejusque effectum, videlicet peccatorum remissionem, non ei, sed observantiis legis adscripserit? Talis graviter punietur.
paras.en: For [[10:28|A man|quis faciens]] [[10:28|making void|Irritam enim]] (making void, that is, emptying; a man, that is, a man transgressing) [[10:28|the law of Moses|legem Moysis]], [[10:28|without any mercy|sine ulla miseratione]] from the judge, [[10:28|under two or three witnesses|duobus vel tribus testibus]] [[10:28|dieth|moritur]], that is, is put to death on the testimony of so many witnesses, according to the precept of the law; provided, however, that the greatness of the sin requires it. [[10:29|How much more, do you think he deserveth worse|Quanto magis putatis deteriora]], that is, heavier, [[10:29|punishments|mereri supplicia]] does he deserve [[10:29|who hath trodden under foot the Son of God|qui Filium Dei conculcaverit]], by dishonouring him and despising his commandments, [[10:29|and hath esteemed the blood of the testament unclean|et sanguinem testamenti pollutum duxerit]], that is, has held cheap the blood of Christ, by which the new testament was confirmed, and thought it as it were insufficient to take away sins, asserting on this account that the observances of the law are to be kept together with the Gospel; [[10:29|by which|in quo]] blood, that is, by whose shedding, [[10:29|he was sanctified|sanctificatus est]], that is, cleansed from vices and adorned with grace, first in Baptism, then in Penance; [[10:29|and hath offered an affront to the Spirit of grace|et spiritui gratiæ contumeliam fecerit]], that is, has despised the grace of the Holy Ghost, or driven away from himself the Holy Ghost, the bestower of all grace, and ascribed his effect, namely the remission of sins, not to him but to the observances of the law? Such a man will be grievously punished.

paras.t: Scimus enim qui dixit, id est, veracem esse cognoscimus Deum, qui ait: Mihi reservate vindictam, id est, mihi vel vicariis meis, puta judicibus, et ego retribuam justam ultionem per me vel meos ministros. Hoc Dominus, quantum ad sensum, loquitur in Deuteronomio: Mea est ultio, et ego retribuam eis in tempore. Secundum quosdam habetur in propria forma apud Ezechielem, secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum. Et iterum dicit Scriptura: Quia judicabit Dominus populum suum, bonos ab impiis liberando. Horrendum est incidere in manus, id est in judiciariam potestatem et justum rigorem, Dei viventis, præsertim post vitam præsentem. Tamen in hac vita melius est incidere in manus Dei quam hominum. Propter quod David ait: Melius est mihi incidere in manus Domini (multæ enim sunt miserationes ejus), quam in manus hominum. Melius itaque nobis est, in hac vita a superioribus nostris ac fratribus increpari et corripi, quam in futuro a Deo redargui.
paras.en: [[10:30|For we know him that hath said|Scimus enim qui dixit]], that is, we know God, who said it, to be truthful: [[10:30|Vengeance belongeth to me|Mihi reservate vindictam]] [Denis's text reads "Reserve vengeance to me"], that is, to me or to my vicars, such as judges, [[10:30|and I will repay|et ego retribuam]] just vengeance, through myself or through my ministers. This the Lord says, as to the sense, in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:35|Revenge is mine, and I will repay them in due time|Mea est ultio, et ego retribuam eis in tempore]]. According to some it is found in its very form in Ezechiel, in the translation of the Septuagint [the margin gives Ezech. xx, without a verse; no verse there has these words]. [[10:30|And again|Et iterum]] Scripture says: [[10:30|The Lord shall judge his people|Quia judicabit Dominus populum suum]][[Deut 32:36||]][[Ps 134:14||]], by delivering the good from the wicked. [[10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands|Horrendum est incidere in manus]], that is, into the judicial power and just rigour, [[10:31|of the living God|Dei viventis]], especially after the present life. Yet in this life it is better to fall into the hands of God than of men. For which reason David says: [[2 Kings 24:14|it is better that I should fall into the hands of the Lord (for his mercies are many) than into the hands of men|Melius est mihi incidere in manus Domini (multæ enim sunt miserationes ejus), quam in manus hominum]] [the margin reads "Ps. xxx?"; the words are David's in 2 Kings 24:14]. It is better for us, therefore, to be rebuked and corrected in this life by our superiors and brethren than to be reproved by God in the life to come.

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus instruit eos, commemorando præterita bona eorum, ut sic provocentur ad meliora. Rememoramini autem pristinos dies, id est, ad memoriam revocate conversationem vestram quam in principio conversionis vestræ habuistis, in quibus diebus illuminati a Spiritu Sancto, magnum certamen sustinuistis passionum, id est validam impugnationem persecutionum. Et in altero quidem, id est in uno genere impugnationis, opprobriis et tribulationibus, id est convitia et tribulationes patiendo in propria persona, spectaculum hominum facti, qui vos cum admiratione inspexerunt propter magnitudinem calamitatis afflictionisque vestræ. In altero autem, id est in alio genere tribulationis, socii taliter conversantium, id est adversa patientium, estis effecti, condolendo afflictis, eorum miseriam quasi propriam æstimantes. Ideo subditur: Nam et vinctis compassi estis corde, et opere eis subvenistis, et rapinam bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis, id est, hilari animo tolerastis quod vestra vobis violenter ablata sunt. Infideles namque Judæi rapuerunt bona primitivæ Ecclesiæ in Jerusalem et Judæa collectæ. Ideo autem fecistis ista ac sustinuistis, quia eratis cognoscentes vos habere meliorem et manentem substantiam, id est cœlestes divitias, quas nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit. Hæc modo habetur in spe, et si propter eam temporalia contemnantur, acquiretur cito in re.
paras.en: Next the Apostle instructs them by recalling their past good deeds, so that they may thus be stirred up to better things. [[10:32|But call to mind the former days|Rememoramini autem pristinos dies]], that is, bring back to memory the way of life you had at the beginning of your conversion, [[10:32|wherein, being illuminated|in quibus diebus illuminati]] by the Holy Ghost, [[10:32|you endured a great fight of afflictions|magnum certamen sustinuistis passionum]], that is, a strong assault of persecutions. [[10:33|And on the one hand indeed|Et in altero quidem]], that is, in one kind of assault, [[10:33|by reproaches and tribulations|opprobriis et tribulationibus]], that is, by suffering insults and tribulations in your own person, you [[10:33|were made a gazingstock|spectaculum hominum facti]] to men, who looked on you with wonder because of the greatness of your calamity and affliction; [[10:33|and on the other|In altero autem]], that is, in another kind of tribulation, you [[10:33|became|estis effecti]] [[10:33|companions of them that were used in such sort|socii taliter conversantium]], that is, of those suffering adversity, by sympathizing with the afflicted and reckoning their misery as your own. Therefore it is added: [[10:34|For you both had compassion on them that were in bands|Nam et vinctis compassi estis]] in heart, and came to their help in deed, [[10:34|and took with joy the being stripped of your own goods|et rapinam bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis]], that is, bore with a cheerful mind that what was yours was taken from you by violence. For the unbelieving Jews plundered the goods of the primitive Church gathered in Jerusalem and Judæa. And you did and bore these things because you were [[10:34|knowing that you have a better and a lasting substance|cognoscentes vos habere meliorem et manentem substantiam]], that is, heavenly riches, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit]][[Is 64:4||]]. This is held now in hope, and if temporal things are despised for its sake, it will soon be gained in reality.

paras.t: Nolite itaque amittere confidentiam vestram, id est, non cessetis in Deo confidere, in quo hucusque confisi estis inter tot adversa et aspera, quæ confidentia magnam habet, id est meretur, remunerationem gratiæ et consolationis in præsenti, et gloriæ in futuro. Unde Isaias testatur: Deus judicii Dominus; beati omnes qui exspectant eum.
paras.en: [[10:35|Do not therefore lose your confidence|Nolite itaque amittere confidentiam vestram]], that is, do not cease to trust in God, in whom you have trusted until now amid so many adversities and hardships; [[10:35|which hath a great|quæ confidentia magnam habet]] (that is, merits a great) [[10:35|reward|remunerationem]] of grace and consolation in the present, and of glory in the future. Hence Isaias testifies: [[Is 30:18|the Lord is the God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him|Deus judicii Dominus; beati omnes qui exspectant eum]].

paras.t: Patientia enim, quæ est virtus moralis passionem tristitiæ reprimens, estque æquanimis tolerantia adversitatum, vobis necessaria est. Hæc virtus præcipue necessaria est Christiano volenti pacem cordis habere, et Deo tranquilla mente servire. Ideo dicit Salvator: In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras; et Judith, Illi qui tentationes non susceperunt in timore Domini et in patientia sua, exterminati sunt. Denique, ut Salomon profitetur, Qui impatiens est, operatur stultitiam; et, Melior est patiens viro forti. Ut voluntatem Dei, id est divina præcepta, facientes, non cessando a bonis operibus propter quæcumque adversa, reportetis, id est, pro vestro labore recipiatis ac referatis in futuro, quum dimissi fueritis a tribunali Christi, promissionem, id est promissam felicitatem: juxta illud, Venientes autem venient cum exsultatione, portantes manipulos suos. Unde dicit Petrus: Videntes Jesum, exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili, reportantes finem fidei vestræ salutem animarum vestrarum.
paras.en: [[10:36|For patience|Patientia enim]], which is a moral virtue restraining the passion of sorrow, and is the even-minded bearing of adversities, [[10:36|is necessary for you|vobis necessaria est]]. This virtue is especially necessary for the Christian who wishes to have peace of heart and to serve God with a tranquil mind. That is why the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:19|In your patience you shall possess your souls|In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras]]; and Judith: [[Jdt 8:24|they that did not receive the trials with the fear of the Lord|Illi qui tentationes non susceperunt in timore Domini]] and in their patience, [[Jdt 8:25|Were destroyed|exterminati sunt]] [the margin's verse number is lost (Judith viii, […]); the words are from Jdt 8:24–25, where the Vulgate has "and uttered their impatience" for Denis's "and in their patience"]. Finally, as Solomon declares: [[Prov 14:17|The impatient man shall work folly|Qui impatiens est, operatur stultitiam]]; and: [[Prov 16:32|The patient man is better than the valiant|Melior est patiens viro forti]]. [[10:36|that, doing|facientes]] [[10:36|the will of God|Ut voluntatem Dei]], that is, the divine precepts, [the margin here gives Hebr. x, 32, which does not fit; the words are those of v. 36], not ceasing from good works because of any adversities whatever, [[10:36|you may receive|reportetis]], that is, may receive and bring back in the future for your labour, when you are dismissed from the judgment-seat of Christ, [[10:36|the promise|promissionem]], that is, the promised happiness; according to that saying: [[Ps 125:7|But coming they shall come with joyfulness, carrying their sheaves|Venientes autem venient cum exsultatione, portantes manipulos suos]] [the margin gives Ps. cxxv, 6; in the Vulgate's division of verses these words are v. 7]. Hence Peter says: Seeing Jesus, you [[1 Pet 1:8|shall rejoice with joy unspeakable|exsultabitis lætitia inenarrabili]], [[1 Pet 1:9|Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls|reportantes finem fidei vestræ salutem animarum vestrarum]].

paras.t: Merito autem servanda est patientia. Adhuc enim modicum aliquantulum, id est, valde breve restat spatium, et qui venturus est Christus, veniet, vel in die finali judicii per localem descensum a cœlo super vallem Josaphat, vel in morte cujuslibet per judicii exhibitionem. Dicitur enim Deus ad aliquem venire, quando visitat eum per pœnam vel gloriam, prout ipse loquitur: Si non vigilaveris, veniam ad te tanquam fur. Et non tardabit. Vita enim nostra brevissima est. Et quamvis tempus præsens usque ad diem judicii longum videatur, tamen comparatione æternitatis sequentis, brevissimum est, sicut ait Psalmista: Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos, tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit. Hinc scriptum est: Patientes estote usque ad adventum Domini, et confirmate corda vestra, quoniam adventus Domini appropinquabit; ecce judex ante januam adsistit.
paras.en: And rightly is patience to be kept. [[10:37|For yet a little and a very little while|Adhuc enim modicum aliquantulum]], that is, a very short space remains, [[10:37|and he that is to come|et qui venturus est]], Christ, [[10:37|will come|veniet]], either on the last day of judgment, by a descent in place from heaven upon the valley of Josaphat, or at the death of each man, by the presenting of judgment. For God is said to come to someone when he visits him by punishment or by glory, as he himself says: [[Apoc 3:3|If then thou shalt not watch, I will come to thee as a thief|Si non vigilaveris, veniam ad te tanquam fur]] [the margin here gives Habac. ii, 3, the source of the Apostle's words in this verse; the words Denis quotes are from Apoc 3:3]. [[10:37|and will not delay|Et non tardabit]][[Hab 2:3||]]. For our life is very short. And though the present time until the day of judgment seems long, yet in comparison with the eternity that follows it is very short, as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 89:4|For a thousand years in thy sight are as yesterday, which is past|Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos, tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit]]. Hence it is written: [[Jas 5:7|Be patient therefore, brethren, until the coming of the Lord|Patientes estote usque ad adventum Domini]], [[Jas 5:8|and strengthen your hearts: for the coming of the Lord is at hand|et confirmate corda vestra, quoniam adventus Domini appropinquabit]]; [[Jas 5:9|Behold the judge standeth before the door|ecce judex ante januam adsistit]].

paras.t: Justus autem meus, id est homo justus mihi acceptus atque electus, ex fide, id est per fidem et meritum ejus, tanquam per fundamentum virtutum, vivit vita gratiæ: loquendo de fide formata, de qua ait Joannes, Hæc est victoria nostra quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra. Qui enim incredulus est, infideliter agit. Quod si subtraxerit se, id est, a fide et æquitate recesserit, non placebit animæ meæ, id est voluntati meæ. Anima enim non convenit Deo secundum divinitatis naturam, nisi metaphorice. Sine fide autem impossibile est Deo placere, ut infra habetur. Hæc verba habentur apud prophetam Habacuc, secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum. Nostra vero translatio talis est: Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit recta anima ejus in semetipso; justus autem ex sua fide vivet.
paras.en: [[10:38|But my just man|Justus autem meus]], that is, the just man accepted by me and chosen, [[10:38|by faith|ex fide]], that is, through faith and its merit, as through the foundation of the virtues, [[10:38|liveth|vivit]][[Hab 2:4||]][[Rom 1:17||]] the life of grace: speaking of formed faith [that is, faith given its form by charity], of which John says: [[1 John 5:4|this is the victory which overcameth the world: Our faith|Hæc est victoria nostra quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra]]. For [[Is 21:2|he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully|incredulus est, infideliter agit]]. [[10:38|but if he withdraw himself|Quod si subtraxerit se]], that is, departs from faith and justice, [[10:38|he shall not please my soul|non placebit animæ meæ]], that is, my will. For a soul does not belong to God according to the nature of the Godhead, except by metaphor. [[Heb 11:6|But without faith it is impossible to please God|Sine fide autem impossibile est Deo placere]], as is said below. These words are found in the prophet Habacuc, according to the translation of the Septuagint.
