[[12:5|And you have forgotten the consolation|Et obliti estis consolationis]], that is, the consoling Scripture, [[12:5|which speaketh to you, as unto children|quæ vobis tanquam filiis]] of God by adoption, [[12:5|saying|dicens]] in the person of the Wise Man: [[12:5|My son, neglect not|Fili mi, noli negligere]][[Prov 3:11||]], that is, despise not, do not disregard or refuse, [[12:5|the discipline of the Lord|disciplinam Domini]], that is, punishment or tribulation inflicted by God; [[12:5|neither be thou wearied|neque fatigeris]] through impatience or faint-heartedness, [[12:5|whilst thou art rebuked by him|dum ab eo argueris]] by just reproof, in words or in stripes [*verborum seu verberum*, a play on words], mediately or immediately [that is, through others or by God himself]. Therefore we read in Job: [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth: refuse not, therefore, the chastising of the Lord|Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino: increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes]] [Denis reads *by the Lord* for *by God*]. And Jeremias prays: [[Jer 10:24|Correct me, O Lord, but yet with judgment: and not in thy fury|Corripe me, Domine; verumtamen in judicio, et non in furore]].

paras.t: Quem enim diligit, id est, cui bonum gratiæ in præsenti et bonum gloriæ in futuro vult, Dominus castigat, id est, paterne corrigit in præsenti, ne postea durius crucietur. Flagellat autem omnem filium quem recipit ad numerum Beatorum, et quem habet acceptum: nam et proprio naturalique Filio non pepercit. Hoc est quod in Apocalypsi protestatur: Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo. Imo periculosissimum est, et maximum divini odii reprobationisque signum, non castigari nec argui a Deo in sæculo isto, prout per Ezechielem Dominus ait populo reprobo: Zelus meus recessit a te, non irascar tibi amplius; itemque in Psalmo: Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum; ibunt in adinventionibus suis.
paras.en: [[12:6|For whom the Lord loveth|Quem enim diligit]], that is, the one for whom he wills the good of grace in the present and the good of glory in the future, [[12:6|he chastiseth|Dominus castigat]], that is, corrects him like a father in the present, lest he be more harshly tormented afterwards. [[12:6|and he scourgeth every son whom he receiveth|Flagellat autem omnem filium quem recipit]] into the number of the Blessed, and whom he holds accepted: for he [[Rom 8:32|spared not even his own Son|proprio naturalique Filio non pepercit]] [Denis: *his own and natural Son*]. This is what he declares in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. Indeed, it is most perilous, and the greatest sign of God's hatred and of reprobation, not to be chastised or rebuked by God in this world; as the Lord says through Ezechiel to the reprobate people: [[Ezech 16:42|my jealousy shall depart from thee|Zelus meus recessit a te]], I will [[Ezech 16:42|be angry no more|non irascar tibi amplius]] with thee; and likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: they shall walk in their own inventions|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum; ibunt in adinventionibus suis]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxx, 11; the words are v. 13].

paras.t: Ex præinducta insuper auctoritate infert Apostolus instructionem moralem. In disciplina, id est correctione juste illata, perseverare, usque in finem eam æquanimiter sustinendo, dicentes singuli illud Job: Peccavi et vere deliqui, et ut eram dignus, non recepi. Hinc enim scriptum est: Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit arguenti, glorificabitur. Alio quoque loco Salomon loquitur: Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis. Cur autem in disciplina perseverandum sit, subditur: Tanquam filiis offert se vobis Deus, id est, tam clementer et providentialiter se habet ad vos, sicut decet patrem se habere ad filios: ideo corripit. Quis enim filius quem non corripit pater si peccaverit? tanquam dicat, Nullus. Scriptum est enim: Qui parcit virgæ, odit filium suum; qui autem diligit illum, instanter erudit. Et alibi: Qui diligit filium suum, assiduat illi flagella, ut lætetur in novissimo.
paras.en: Moreover, from the authority brought in above, the Apostle draws a moral instruction. [[12:7|Persevere|perseverare]] [[12:7|under discipline|In disciplina]], that is, under correction justly inflicted, bearing it with equanimity to the end, each of you saying that word of Job: [[Job 33:27|I have sinned, and indeed I have offended, and I have not received what I have deserved|Peccavi et vere deliqui, et ut eram dignus, non recepi]]. For hence it is written: [[Prov 13:18|Poverty and shame to him that refuseth instruction: but he that yieldeth to reproof shall be glorified|Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit arguenti, glorificabitur]]. In another place, too, Solomon says: [[Prov 15:32|He that rejecteth instruction, despiseth his own soul: but he that yieldeth to reproof, possesseth understanding|Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis]] [literally, *is master of his heart*]. Why one must persevere under discipline is then added: [[12:7|God dealeth with you as with his sons|Tanquam filiis offert se vobis Deus]], that is, he bears himself towards you as mercifully and providently as it befits a father to bear himself towards his sons: therefore he corrects you. [[12:7|For what son is there whom the father doth not correct|Quis enim filius quem non corripit pater]] if he has sinned? as if to say, None. For it is written: [[Prov 13:24|He that spareth the rod, hateth his son: but he that loveth him, correcteth him betimes|Qui parcit virgæ, odit filium suum; qui autem diligit illum, instanter erudit]] [the margin gives Ibid. xxiv, 24; the words are Prov 13:24]. And elsewhere: [[Ecclus 30:1|He that loveth his son, frequently chastiseth him, that he may rejoice in his latter end|Qui diligit filium suum, assiduat illi flagella, ut lætetur in novissimo]].

paras.t: Quod si extra disciplinam estis, ita quod virga Dei non est super vos, sicut de impiis legitur, cujus disciplinæ participes facti sunt omnes filii et electi, eam experiendo; ergo adulteri, id est non spiritualiter a Deo geniti, sed filii adulterini, filii utique hujus sæculi atque diaboli, et non filii estis: prout apud Joannem scribitur de quibusdam: Vos ex patre diabolo estis.
paras.en: [[12:8|But if you be without chastisement|Quod si extra disciplinam estis]], so that [[Job 21:9|the rod of God is not upon|virga Dei non est super]] you, as we read of the wicked, [[12:8|whereof all are made partakers|cujus disciplinæ participes facti sunt omnes]], all the sons and the elect, by experiencing it; [[12:8|then are you bastards|ergo adulteri]], that is, not begotten of God spiritually, but adulterine sons [*adulteri*, literally "adulterous ones"], sons, that is, of this world and of the devil, [[12:8|and not sons|et non filii estis]]: as is written in John of certain men: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]].

paras.t: Deinde probat Apostolus per locum a majori, et per exemplum in naturalibus, quod obediendum sit Deo, recipiendo disciplinam patienter ab eo. Deinde, id est, ex sequentibus idem patescit, patres quidem carnis nostræ, id est patres nostros carnales, a quibus corpus, non animam, sortiti sumus, eruditores habuimus, præsertim tempore nostræ juventutis. Pater enim debet filio nutrimentum ac documentum. Et reverebamur eos, id est, honorem cum timore eis impendebamus. Non multo magis obtemperabimus, id est obediemus, Patri spirituum, id est Deo creatori animarum, et vivemus vita gratiæ? quasi dicat: Hoc multo rationabilius est, sicut et anima corpore est nobilior. Quanto enim plura ac potiora a Deo bona suscepimus, tanto amplius ei parere tenemur. Et illi quidem patres nostri carnales, in tempore paucorum dierum, videlicet durante adolescentia nostra, secundum voluntatem suam erudiebant nos, id est in his quæ eis bona apparuerunt, videlicet in honestate humana et traditionibus sæcularibus; hic autem Pater spirituum erudit nos per inspirationem internam et sacræ Scripturæ lectionem seu prædicationem, ad id quod utile est, id est ad bona gratiæ et beatitudinem gloriæ, ut ea assequamur, in recipiendo sanctificationem ejus, id est cordis expurgationem a viciis, et puritatem divinæ illustrationis. Hæc est enim voluntas Dei, sanctificatio nostra.
paras.en: Then the Apostle proves, by an argument from the greater and by an example from nature, that God is to be obeyed by receiving discipline patiently from him. [[12:9|Moreover|Deinde]], that is, the same is made plain from what follows, [[12:9|we have had fathers of our flesh|patres quidem carnis nostræ]], that is, our fathers in the flesh, from whom we received the body, not the soul, [[12:9|for instructors|eruditores habuimus]], especially in the time of our youth. For a father owes his son nourishment and teaching. [[12:9|and we reverenced them|Et reverebamur eos]], that is, we paid them honour with fear. [[12:9|Shall we not much more obey|Non multo magis obtemperabimus]], that is, be obedient to, [[12:9|the Father of spirits|Patri spirituum]], that is, God the creator of souls, [[12:9|and live|et vivemus]] the life of grace? as if to say: This is much more reasonable, just as the soul is nobler than the body. For the more and the greater the goods we have received from God, the more we are bound to obey him. [[12:10|And they indeed|Et illi quidem]], our fathers in the flesh, [[12:10|for a few days|in tempore paucorum dierum]], namely while our youth lasted, [[12:10|according to their own pleasure, instructed us|secundum voluntatem suam erudiebant nos]], that is, in the things that seemed good to them, namely in human decency and worldly traditions; [[12:10|but he|hic autem]], the Father of spirits, instructs us, by inward inspiration and by the reading or preaching of holy Scripture, [[12:10|for our profit|ad id quod utile est]], that is, to the goods of grace and the beatitude of glory, so that we may attain them, [[12:10|that we might receive his sanctification|in recipiendo sanctificationem ejus]], that is, the cleansing of the heart from vices and the purity of divine enlightenment. For [[1 Thess 4:3|this is the will of God, your sanctification|Hæc est enim voluntas Dei, sanctificatio nostra]] [Denis has *our* sanctification].

paras.t: Præterea, admonet in disciplina persistendum, propter copiosissimum fructum ex ea sequentem. Omnis autem disciplina, id est correptio pro peccatis inflicta, in præsenti quidem sæculo; vel, In præsenti, id est ea durante; […] gaudii, sed mœroris, id est non delectabilis, sed molesta. Talis enim videtur carnalibus, quamvis spirituales eam delectabiliter patiantur propter utilitatem ipsius, quemadmodum æger libenter recipit potionem amaram propter spem sanitatis. Vere tamen disciplina ista est in se molesta, quum sit quædam pœna. Disciplina vero quæ a discendo nomen accepit, quæ et scientia dicitur, in sua natura jucunda et dulcis est. Postea autem, id est in vita futura, fructum pacatissimum exercitatis per eam reddet justitiæ, id est, in patria reddet, id est, dari faciet, per modum causæ meritoriæ, fructum pacatissimum justitiæ, id est quietissimam mercedem, seu beatitudinem desiderium quietantem: qui fructus ex justitia oritur, et juste confertur exercitatis, id est in actibus virtuosis habituatis per eam disciplinam. Ideo dictum est alio loco: Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam quæ revelabitur in nobis. Et rursus: Id quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis.
paras.en: Further, he admonishes them to persist under discipline because of the most abundant fruit that follows from it. [[12:11|Now all chastisement|Omnis autem disciplina]], that is, correction inflicted for sins, [[12:11|for the present indeed|in præsenti quidem]], in this world; or, [[12:11|for the present|In præsenti]], that is, while it lasts; […] [[12:11|joy, but sorrow|gaudii, sed mœroris]], that is, not delightful, but painful. For so it seems to carnal men, although spiritual men suffer it with delight because of its usefulness, as a sick man willingly takes a bitter draught in the hope of health. Yet truly this discipline is painful in itself, since it is a kind of punishment. But the discipline that takes its name from learning, which is also called knowledge, is pleasant and sweet in its own nature [*disciplina* means both "chastisement" and "learning", from *discere*, "to learn"]. [[12:11|but afterwards|Postea autem]], that is, in the life to come, [[12:11|it will yield to them that are exercised by it the most peaceable fruit of justice|fructum pacatissimum exercitatis per eam reddet justitiæ]], that is, in the fatherland [that is, heaven] it will yield, that is, will cause to be given, by way of meritorious cause, the most peaceable fruit of justice, that is, a most restful reward, or the beatitude that brings desire to rest: which fruit springs from justice, and is justly bestowed on those who are exercised, that is, made habitual in virtuous acts, by that discipline. Therefore it is said in another place: [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam quæ revelabitur in nobis]]. And again: [[2 Cor 4:17|that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation worketh for us above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory|Id quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis]].

paras.t: Propter quod remissas manus, id est pigras et tepidas affectiones, et soluta genua, id est fortitudinem qua ante stetistis, nunc debilitatam, erigite ad Deum, id est, perficite ut caritatis affectus in vobis flammescant, et ad cœlos vos sublevent. Fortitudo quoque animæ corroboretur in vobis. Corporis etiam manus ac genua debemus ad Deum levare, stando erecti ad eum in oratione ac contemplatione, juxta illud: Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Deum in cœlos. Et gressus rectos, id est opera justa, facite pedibus vestris, id est ex interioribus virtutibus animæ, quibus itur ad Deum, videlicet ex fide, spe et caritate, sine quibus nulla actio meritoria est; ut non claudicans, id est instabilis, vagus et in via Domini nutans, quis vestrum erret ab ultimo fine, magis autem sanetur a vulneribus animæ, id est peccatis.
paras.en: [[12:12|Wherefore|Propter quod]] [[12:12|the hands which hang down|remissas manus]], that is, sluggish and lukewarm affections, [[12:12|and the feeble knees|et soluta genua]][[Is 35:3||]], that is, the strength by which you stood before, now weakened, [[12:12|lift up|erigite]] to God: that is, bring it about that the affections of charity blaze up in you and raise you to heaven. Let the strength of the soul also be made firm in you. We ought also to lift up the hands and knees of the body to God, standing upright towards him in prayer and contemplation, according to that saying: [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Deum in cœlos]] [Denis has *to God* for *to the Lord*]. [[12:13|And make straight steps|Et gressus rectos]], that is, just works, [[12:13|with your feet|facite pedibus vestris]], that is, from the inward virtues of the soul by which one goes to God, namely from faith, hope and charity, without which no action is meritorious; [[12:13|that no one, halting|ut non claudicans]], that is, unstable, wandering and wavering in the way of the Lord, [[12:13|may go out of the way|quis vestrum erret]] from the last end [that is, God, the final end of man], [[12:13|but rather be healed|magis autem sanetur]] of the wounds of the soul, that is, of sins.

paras.t: Pacem, id est tranquillitatem sive concordiam, sequimini, id est, servare curare, cum omnibus proximis, amicis ac æmulis. Quod intelligendum est de vera spiritualique pace. Propter quod et Romanis dictum est: Si fieri potest, cum omnibus hominibus pacem habentes. Et sanctimoniam, id est cordis munditiam, juxta illud: Omni custodia custodi cor tuum. Sine qua pace et sanctimonia nemo videbit Deum in patria. Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Beati quoque mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt.
paras.en: [[12:14|peace|Pacem]], that is, tranquillity or concord, [[12:14|Follow|sequimini]], that is, take care to keep it, [[12:14|with all men|cum omnibus proximis]], neighbours, friends and rivals alike. This is to be understood of true and spiritual peace. For this reason the Romans too were told: [[Rom 12:18|If it be possible|Si fieri potest]], [[Rom 12:18|have peace with all men|cum omnibus hominibus pacem habentes]]. [[12:14|and holiness|Et sanctimoniam]], that is, cleanness of heart, according to that saying: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum]]. [[12:14|without which|Sine qua]] peace and holiness [[12:14|no man shall see God|nemo videbit Deum]] in the fatherland. For [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God|Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur]]. And also: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati quoque mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]].

paras.t: Contemplantes, id est sollicite præcaventes, ne quis desit gratiæ Dei, id est, ne aliquis vestrum elongetur ac separetur a gratia Dei, quæ omnibus præsto est, dummodo fecerint quod in se est; vel, Ne quis desit gratiæ Dei, id est, ne gratia Dei in vobis imperfecta sit propter negligentiam vestram. Sed potius in ea proficite, ne qua radix amaritudinis, id est, ne aliqua passio vitiosa, pœnalis, seu pœnam promerens, sursum germinans, id est in consensum vel opus prorumpens, impediat gratiam et salutem, et per illam amaritudinem inquinentur, id est, scandalizentur seu perturbentur, multi ex impatientia. Unde in lege præcipitur: Non sit inter vos radix germinans fel et amaritudinem; et Sapiens, Non est sensus ubi abundat amaritudo.
paras.en: [[12:15|Looking diligently|Contemplantes]], that is, carefully guarding beforehand, [[12:15|lest any man be wanting to the grace of God|ne quis desit gratiæ Dei]], that is, lest any of you be drawn away and separated from the grace of God, which is at hand for all, provided they do what is in them [that is, what lies in their power]; or, [[12:15|lest any man be wanting to the grace of God|Ne quis desit gratiæ Dei]], that is, lest the grace of God be imperfect in you through your negligence. But rather make progress in it, [[12:15|lest any root of bitterness|ne qua radix amaritudinis]], that is, lest any vicious passion, penal or deserving of punishment, [[12:15|springing up|sursum germinans]], that is, breaking out into consent or deed, [[12:15|do hinder|impediat]] grace and salvation, [[12:15|and by it|et per illam amaritudinem]] [Denis's text has *by that bitterness*] [[12:15|be defiled|inquinentur]], that is, be scandalized or troubled, [[12:15|many|multi]], through impatience. Hence it is commanded in the law: Let not [[Deut 29:18|a root bringing forth gall and bitterness|radix germinans fel et amaritudinem]] be among you; and the Wise Man: [[Ecclus 21:15|there is no understanding where there is bitterness|Non est sensus ubi abundat amaritudo]] [Denis: *where bitterness abounds*].

paras.t: Ne quis sit fornicator spiritualis, recedendo a fide. Est enim spiritualis fornicatio, qua Deus relinquitur. De qua Propheta: Fornicati sunt a Deo; et in Psalmo, Fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis. Vel, Ne quis sit fornicator corporalis, illicitum concubitum committendo. Aut profanus, id est penitus irreligiosus, tanquam procul a fano, id est remotus a templo, serviens suo ventri magis quam Deo, ut gulosi; ut Esau, qui propter unam escam, puta lenticulam a Jacob paratam, vendidit ipso Jacob primitiva sua, id est primogenita, scilicet dignitatem primogenitorum, hoc est honorem sacerdotii, prout in Genesi narratur. Primogeniti autem in lege naturæ erant sacerdotes, et speciales vestes habebant, quibus tempore sacerdotii utebantur: habebantque duplicem portionem in hereditate. Jus autem primogenituræ et dignitas sacerdotii, spirituale sunt bonum. Ideo Esau id vendendo, incidit simoniam: non tamen Jacob, quoniam proprie non emit ea: sed sui vexationem redemit, quoniam ex ordinatione divina ei debebantur primogenita.
paras.en: [[12:16|Lest there be any fornicator|Ne quis sit fornicator]] in the spiritual sense, by falling away from the faith. For there is a spiritual fornication, by which God is forsaken. Of it the Prophet says: [[Osee 4:12|they have committed fornication against their God|Fornicati sunt a Deo]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 105:39|they went aside after their own inventions|Fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis]] [literally, *they committed fornication in their own inventions*]. Or, [[12:16|Lest there be any fornicator|Ne quis sit fornicator]] in the bodily sense, by committing unlawful intercourse. [[12:16|or profane person|Aut profanus]], that is, wholly irreligious, as it were far from the *fanum*, that is, removed from the temple [*pro fano*, "outside the shrine", is the root of *profanus*], serving his own belly rather than God[[Rom 16:18||]], as gluttons do; [[12:16|as Esau who for one mess|ut Esau, qui propter unam escam]], namely the lentils prepared by Jacob, [[12:16|sold|vendidit]] to Jacob himself [[12:16|his first birthright|primitiva sua]], that is, his rights as firstborn, namely the dignity of the firstborn, that is, the honour of the priesthood, as is told in Genesis[[Gen 25:29||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxv, 29–34]. Now in the law of nature the firstborn were priests, and had special vestments, which they wore at the time of their priestly service; and they had a double portion in the inheritance. But the right of the firstborn and the dignity of the priesthood are a spiritual good. Therefore Esau, by selling it, fell into simony; not so Jacob, since he did not properly buy them, but redeemed himself from injury [that is, paid only to obtain what was already his due, which is not simony], since by divine ordinance the birthright was owed to him.

paras.t: Itaque non sit aliquis vestrum fornicator aut profanus ut Esau: Scitote enim quoniam et postea reversus de agro, et Jacob jam benedicto, cupiens Esau hereditare, id est hereditarie possidere vel sumere, benedictionem Isaac, reprobatus est a Deo, et ab impetratione benedictionis prohibitus. Verumtamen in Genesi legitur Isaac benedixisse Esau filio suo, sed non benedictione primogenituræ, quam Esau primo et principaliter postulavit. Non enim invenit pœnitentiæ locum ad recuperandum amissam benedictionem, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam, id est pœnitentiæ veniam seu benedictionem. Non enim ex amore justitiæ vel vera contritione profluxerunt lacrimæ illæ, sed ex temporalis damni mœrore, vel indignatione sive rancore. Simili modo de Antiocho scribitur: Orabat scelestus Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam consecuturus. Neminem tamen Deus repellit, si recta intentione convertatur ad eum. Quis enim invocavit Deum, et despexit eum?
paras.en: So let none of you be a [[12:16|fornicator or profane person, as Esau|fornicator aut profanus ut Esau]]: [[12:17|For know ye that afterwards|Scitote enim quoniam et postea]], when he had come back from the field, Jacob being already blessed[[Gen 27:30||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxvii, 30–37], Esau, [[12:17|when he desired to inherit|cupiens Esau hereditare]], that is, to possess or take as an inheritance, [[12:17|the benediction|benedictionem Isaac]] of Isaac, [[12:17|he was rejected|reprobatus est]] by God, and kept from obtaining the blessing. Yet we read in Genesis that Isaac blessed his son Esau[[Gen 27:39||]] [the margin gives Ibid. 34, 40; Isaac's blessing of Esau is Gen 27:39–40], but not with the blessing of the firstborn, which Esau had asked for first and chiefly. [[12:17|For he found no place of repentance|Non enim invenit pœnitentiæ locum]] to recover the blessing he had lost, [[12:17|although with tears he had sought it|quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam]], that is, pardon through repentance, or the blessing. For those tears did not flow from love of justice or from true contrition, but from grief at a temporal loss, or from indignation or rancour. In like manner it is written of Antiochus: [[2 Mach 9:13|this wicked man prayed to the Lord, of whom he was not like to obtain mercy|Orabat scelestus Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam consecuturus]]. Yet God repels no one, if he turns to him with a right intention. For [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him|Quis enim invocavit Deum, et despexit eum]]? [the margin gives Ecclus. xii, 12; the words are Ecclus 2:12]

paras.t: Deinde assignat Apostolus rationem, cur nullus deesse debet gratiæ Dei: eo quod nova lex sit lex pietatis, amoris et gratiæ; vetus autem lex, erat lex timoris, rigoris et mortis. Non enim accessistis ad tractabilem, id est palpabilem, et accessibilem motu corporeo, ignem, qualis fuit ignis ardens in monte Sinai tempore dationis legis antiquæ. Nec accessistis et ad turbinem, id est ventum vehementem qui fit cum grandine et pluvia, et caliginem, id est ignis tenebrositatem, et procellam, id est ingentem tempestatem, et tubæ sonitum, qualis audiebatur in monte Sinai, et vocem verborum, id est vocem angeli loquentis cum Moyse. De his namque legitur: Ceperunt audiri tonitrua, et micare fulgura, et nubes densissima operuit montem; clangor quoque buccinæ vehementius perstrepebat, totusque mons Sinai fumigabat. In his quippe terribilibus data est lex, ad significandum ejus rigorem. Quam procellam et vocem qui audierunt, videlicet filii Israel perterriti, excusaverunt se, suam infirmitatem allegando, ne eis fieret verbum immediate ab angelo loquente in persona Dei, sed a Moyse, dicentes: Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus; non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur. Quid enim est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis? Ideo subditur: Non enim portabant, id est, sustinere et audire non poterant, quod dicebatur, id est verbum angeli cum Moyse terribiliter loquentis. Et si bestia tetigerit montem, lapidabitur, id est, hoc quoque dictum fuit a Deo per angelum et per Moysen ad populum, quod si bestia tetigerit montem Sinai, transeundo ultra terminum præfixum, lapidibus obrueretur. Hoc dictum fuit etiam de hominibus. Et ita terribile erat quod videbatur in monte Sinai. Moyses dixit: Exterritus sum corde, et tremebundus in corpore. Multo magis alii formidabant. Hoc Moyses non legitur dixisse in datione legis; sed in visione rubi ardentis ostendit se territum, abscondendo faciem suam, quoniam non audebat respicere contra Dominum.
paras.en: Then the Apostle gives the reason why no one ought to be wanting to the grace of God: because the new law is a law of loving-kindness, love and grace, while the old law was a law of fear, of rigour and of death. [[12:18|For you are not come|Non enim accessistis]] to something [[12:18|that might be touched|ad tractabilem]], that is, palpable, and approachable by bodily movement, a [[12:18|fire|ignem]], such as was the fire burning on mount Sinai at the time the old law was given [Denis's text reads *ad tractabilem et accessibilem ignem*, "to a fire that may be touched and approached", without *montem*, "mountain", and with *accessibilem* for *accensibilem*, "burning"]. Nor are you come [[12:18|and a whirlwind|et ad turbinem]], that is, a violent wind that comes with hail and rain, [[12:18|and darkness|et caliginem]], that is, the murkiness of the fire, [[12:18|and storm|et procellam]], that is, a mighty tempest, [[12:19|And the sound of a trumpet|et tubæ sonitum]], such as was heard on mount Sinai, [[12:19|and the voice of words|et vocem verborum]], that is, the voice of the angel speaking with Moses. For of these we read: [[Ex 19:16|thunders began to be heard, and lightning to flash, and a very thick cloud to cover the mount, and the noise of the trumpet sounded exceeding loud|Ceperunt audiri tonitrua, et micare fulgura, et nubes densissima operuit montem; clangor quoque buccinæ vehementius perstrepebat]], and [[Ex 19:18|all Mount Sinai was on a smoke|totusque mons Sinai fumigabat]]. For the law was given amid these terrors, to signify its rigour. [[12:19|which|Quam]], the storm and the voice, [[12:19|they that|qui audierunt]] heard, namely the terrified children of Israel, [[12:19|had excused themselves|excusaverunt se]], pleading their weakness, [[12:19|that the word might not be spoken to them|ne eis fieret verbum]] directly by the angel speaking in the person of God, but by Moses, saying: [[Ex 20:19|Speak thou to us, and we will hear: let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die|Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus; non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur]]. For [[Deut 5:26|What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God, who speaketh out of the midst of the fire|Quid enim est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis?]]? Therefore is added: [[12:20|For they did not endure|Non enim portabant]], that is, they could not bear and hear, [[12:20|that which was said|quod dicebatur]], that is, the word of the angel speaking terribly with Moses. [[12:20|and if so much as a beast shall touch the mount, it shall be stoned|Et si bestia tetigerit montem, lapidabitur]], that is, this too was said by God, through the angel and through Moses, to the people: that if a beast touched mount Sinai, passing beyond the boundary set, it should be overwhelmed with stones. This was said of men too. [[12:21|And so terrible was that which was seen|Et ita terribile erat quod videbatur]] on mount Sinai. [[12:21|Moses said: I am frighted, and tremble|Moyses dixit: Exterritus sum corde, et tremebundus in corpore]] [Denis's text adds *in heart* and *in body*]. Much more were the others afraid. We do not read that Moses said this at the giving of the law; but at the vision of the burning bush he showed that he was afraid, hiding his face, because [[Ex 3:6|he durst not look at God|non audebat respicere contra Dominum]].

paras.t: Per ista ostendit Apostolus, quod non sumus sub lege timoris, sed amoris et gratiæ: ideo gratia nobis parata est. Unde subjungitur: Sed accessistis per Baptismatis susceptionem, ad Sion montem, id est Ecclesiam militantem, Deum in alto contemplantem. Sion enim interpretatur speculatio. Ecclesia vero mons dicitur, propter vitæ et gratiæ eminentiam. Accessistis quoque per spem ad civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem, id est Ecclesiam triumphantem, […] millium angelorum frequentiam, id est frequentem multitudinem. Nunc enim speratis pertingere ad societatem angelorum, qui pene innumerabiles sunt, juxta illud: Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei; et in Job: Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surgit lumen ipsius? Et ad ecclesiam primitivorum, id est congregationem et societatem Apostolorum, et aliorum qui primo crediderunt in Christum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis, id est in libro vitæ, quatenus ad cœlestem gloriam perducantur, quemadmodum dixit eis Salvator: Gaudete et exsultate, quia nomina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis.
paras.en: By these things the Apostle shows that we are not under a law of fear, but of love and grace: and so grace is made ready for us. Hence he adds: [[12:22|But you are come|Sed accessistis]], by the receiving of Baptism, [[12:22|to mount Sion|ad Sion montem]], that is, the Church militant, which contemplates God on high. For Sion is interpreted *watching* [*speculatio*, a looking out from a height]. And the Church is called a mountain because of the eminence of its life and grace. You are come also by hope [[12:22|to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem|ad civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem]], that is, the Church triumphant, […] [[12:22|the company of many thousands of angels|millium angelorum frequentiam]], that is, a thronging multitude. For now you hope to attain to the fellowship of the angels, who are almost innumerable, according to that saying: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]; and in Job: [[Job 25:3|Is there any numbering of his soldiers? and upon whom shall not his light arise?|Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surgit lumen ipsius?]] [[12:23|And to the church of the firstborn|Et ad ecclesiam primitivorum]], that is, the congregation and fellowship of the Apostles, and of others who first believed in Christ, [[12:23|who are written in the heavens|qui conscripti sunt in cœlis]], that is, in the book of life, so that they may be brought to heavenly glory; as the Saviour said to them: [[Luke 10:20|rejoice in this, that your names are written in heaven|Gaudete et exsultate, quia nomina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis]] [Denis's wording: *Rejoice and be glad, for your names are written in heaven*].

paras.t: Accessistis quoque per fidem et caritatem et ad judicem omnium Deum, id est ad Deum Patrem, cui ex propria auctoritate primarie competit judicare. Unde ait Salvator: Ego non judico quemquam; est qui quærat et judicet. Tamen prosecutio judicii collata est Christo homini. Et spiritum justorum perfectorum, id est ad Spiritum Sanctum, qui facit atque inhabitat justos et perfectos, tanquam familiaris cum eis; et testamenti novi mediatorem Jesum, id est ad Christum Filium Dei, qui est medius dator evangelicæ legis, inter Deum Trinitatem et homines medians, pacemque faciens, et sanguinis adspersionem, id est ad participationem efficaciæ seu fructus ac meriti sanguinis Christi, per quem mundamur a pœna et culpa in Baptismo, in quo adspergimur merito sanguinis Christi, id est infusione gratiæ: adspersionem, inquam, melius loquentem quam loquitur effusio sanguinis Abel. Sanguis enim Christi clamat et efficit pacem ac veniam; sanguis vero Abel, vindictam et damnationem.
paras.en: You are come also, by faith and charity, [[12:23|and to God the judge of all|et ad judicem omnium Deum]], that is, to God the Father, to whom it belongs primarily, by his own authority, to judge. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]]; [[John 8:50|there is one that seeketh and judgeth|est qui quærat et judicet]]. Yet the carrying out of judgment has been committed to Christ as man. [[12:23|and to the spirits of the just made perfect|Et spiritum justorum perfectorum]] [Denis reads *spiritum*, singular, "the spirit"], that is, to the Holy Spirit, who makes the just and perfect and dwells in them as one of their household; [[12:24|And to Jesus the mediator of the new testament|et testamenti novi mediatorem Jesum]], that is, to Christ the Son of God, who is the giver in the middle [*medius dator*, a play on *mediator*] of the law of the Gospel, mediating between God the Trinity and men[[Eph 2:14||]], and [[Eph 2:15|making peace|pacemque faciens]] [the margin gives Eph. iv, 14, 15; the words are Eph 2:14–15], [[12:24|and to the sprinkling of blood|et sanguinis adspersionem]], that is, to a share in the efficacy, or the fruit and merit, of the blood of Christ, by which we are cleansed from punishment and guilt in Baptism, in which we are sprinkled by the merit of Christ's blood, that is, by the infusion of grace: a sprinkling, I say, [[12:24|which speaketh better than that of Abel|melius loquentem quam loquitur effusio sanguinis Abel]] [Denis: *than the shedding of Abel's blood speaks*]. For the blood of Christ cries out for peace and pardon and brings them about; but the blood of Abel, for vengeance and damnation[[Gen 4:10||]].

paras.t: Videte ne recusetis loquentem, id est, ne Christum in Evangelio vos exhortantem audire spernatis. Si enim, id est quia, illi rebelles Judæi non effugerunt debitam pœnam, recusantes, id est audire contemnentes, eum qui super terram loquebatur eis, id est Moysen vel angelum loquentem in monte Sinai; multo magis nos, qui de cœlis loquentem nobis, id est Christum in cœlo jam residentem et nobis in Evangelio loquentem, avertimus, id est, per inobedientiam a cordibus nostris repellimus, non evademus pœnas condignas.
paras.en: [[12:25|See that you refuse him not that speaketh|Videte ne recusetis loquentem]], that is, lest you scorn to hear Christ exhorting you in the Gospel. [[12:25|For if|Si enim]], that is, since, those rebellious Jews [[12:25|escaped not|non effugerunt]] the punishment due, [[12:25|who refused|recusantes]], that is, scorned to hear, [[12:25|him that spoke upon earth|eum qui super terram loquebatur]] to them, that is, Moses, or the angel speaking on mount Sinai; [[12:25|much more shall not we|multo magis nos]], [[12:25|that turn away from him that speaketh to us from heaven|qui de cœlis loquentem nobis]], that is, from Christ, now dwelling in heaven and speaking to us in the Gospel, [[12:25|turn away|avertimus]], that is, drive him from our hearts by disobedience, escape the punishment we deserve.

paras.t: Cujus Christi vox, id est potestas et sermo, movit terram, id est montem Sinai, qui tremere videbatur, tunc, quum lex dabatur. Vox enim angeli movientis tunc terram, dicitur vox Christi, quoniam in persona Dei, et per consequens in persona Christi loquebatur, quum ipse sit verus Deus. Unde et ipse ait: Creditis in Deum, et in me credite. Nunc autem, id est pro tempore novi testamenti, Christus repromittit, dicens: Adhuc semel, præter id scilicet quod ante feci in monte Sinai, hoc est in primo meo adventu: et ego movebo non solum terram, quæ mota est tempore passionis, sed et cœlum aerium, quod insolito more motum est, angelis tempore nativitatis Christi apparentibus, et novo sidere radiante de cœlo, Christo quoque cum Sanctis innumerabilibus ascendente in cœlum. Quemadmodum autem per motum terræ intelligi potest motio et admiratio hominum; sic per motum cœli intelligi potest ascensus atque descensus et admiratio angelorum, qui in primo Christi adventu frequenter apparuerunt, et vehementer mirati sunt de mysteriis Christi, dicentes in ascensione: Quis est iste qui venit de Edom? et, Quis est iste Rex gloriæ?
paras.en: [[12:26|Whose voice|Cujus Christi vox]], Christ's, that is, his power and word, [[12:26|moved the earth|movit terram]], that is, mount Sinai, which was seen to tremble[[Ex 19:16||]][[Ex 19:18||]], [[12:26|then|tunc]], when the law was given. For the voice of the angel who then moved the earth is called the voice of Christ, since he spoke in the person of God, and consequently in the person of Christ, since Christ is true God. Hence he himself says: [[John 14:1|You believe in God: believe also in me|Creditis in Deum, et in me credite]]. [[12:26|but now|Nunc autem]], that is, for the time of the new testament, Christ [[12:26|promiseth, saying|repromittit, dicens]]: [[12:26|Yet once more|Adhuc semel]][[Agg 2:7||]], besides, namely, what I did before on mount Sinai, that is, in my first coming: [[12:26|and I will move, not only the earth|et ego movebo non solum terram]], which was moved at the time of the passion[[Matt 27:51||]], [[12:26|but heaven also|sed et cœlum]], the heaven of the air, which was moved in an unwonted manner when angels appeared at the time of Christ's birth[[Luke 2:13||]], and a new star shone from heaven[[Matt 2:2||]], and when Christ, too, ascended into heaven with innumerable Saints[[Acts 1:9||]]. And as by the moving of the earth may be understood the stirring and wonder of men, so by the moving of heaven may be understood the ascending and descending and the wonder of the angels, who often appeared at Christ's first coming and greatly marvelled at the mysteries of Christ, saying at the ascension: [[Is 63:1|Who is this that cometh from Edom|Quis est iste qui venit de Edom]]? and, [[Ps 23:8|Who is this King of Glory|Quis est iste Rex gloriæ]][[Ps 23:10||]]?

paras.t: Consequenter exponit quædam verba auctoritatis inductæ. Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit, id est, per hoc quod Propheta hæc duo connectit, Adhuc, et, Semel, declarat mobilium, id est variabilium rerum, scilicet elementorum et orbium, translationem, id est corruptionem, quantum ad statum et formas quasdam accidentales, seu transmutationem in meliorem statum, tanquam factorum, id est a Deo creatorum. Idcirco, quum sint a Deo creata, possunt ab eo transferri in alium statum. Quod erit in die judicii. Ut maneant ea quæ sunt, immobilia, id est, hæc eadem in melius transmutata, in æternum perseverent: quia post diem judicii cessabit generatio et corruptio in rebus corporeis.
paras.en: Next he explains certain words of the authority brought in. [[12:27|And in that he saith: Yet once more|Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit]], that is, by the Prophet's joining these two, *Yet* and *once*, [[12:27|he signifieth|declarat]], [[12:27|of the moveable things|mobilium]], that is, of changeable things, namely the elements and the spheres, [[12:27|the translation|translationem]], that is, their corruption as to their state and certain accidental forms, or their change into a better state, [[12:27|as made|tanquam factorum]], that is, created by God. Therefore, since they were created by God, they can be translated by him into another state. This will be at the day of judgment. [[12:27|that those things may remain which are immoveable|Ut maneant ea quæ sunt, immobilia]], that is, that these same things, changed for the better, may endure for ever: because after the day of judgment generation and corruption will cease in bodily things.

paras.t: Vel sic: Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit, id est, per hoc quod de tempore gratiæ loquitur, declarat mobilium translationem, id est cæremonialium veteris legis cessationem, tanquam factorum, id est quasi ad tempus institutorum a Deo, non ut semper durarent: ut maneant ea quæ sunt immobilia, id est, status, ritus, et sacramenta novæ legis usque ad finem sæculi perseverent.
paras.en: Or thus: [[12:27|And in that he saith: Yet once more|Quod autem, Adhuc semel, dicit]], that is, by speaking of the time of grace, [[12:27|he signifieth the translation of the moveable things|declarat mobilium translationem]], that is, the ceasing of the ceremonies of the old law, [[12:27|as made|tanquam factorum]], that is, as instituted by God for a time, not to last for ever: [[12:27|that those things may remain which are immoveable|ut maneant ea quæ sunt immobilia]], that is, that the state, rites and sacraments of the new law may endure until the end of the world.

paras.t: Itaque regnum immobile, id est ecclesia, suscipientes, modo in spe, suscepturi illud in re, habemus gratiam gratum facientem, per quam serviamus, observando præcepta, placentes Deo, id est opera meritoria perpetrantes: serviamus, inquam, cum metu, in quantum est Domi[…]
paras.en: [[12:28|Therefore|Itaque]] [[12:28|an immoveable kingdom|regnum immobile]], that is, the Church, [[12:28|receiving|suscipientes]] now in hope, as we shall receive it hereafter in reality, [[12:28|we have grace|habemus gratiam]] that makes us pleasing [*gratia gratum faciens*, that is, sanctifying grace], [[12:28|whereby let us serve|per quam serviamus]] by keeping the commandments, [[12:28|pleasing God|placentes Deo]], that is, doing meritorious works: let us serve, I say, [[12:28|with fear|cum metu]], in so far as he is […]

13.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI DECIMI TERTII : C[…]
13.title_en: Explanation of the thirteenth chapter: Let the charity of the brotherhood abide in you.

paras.t: Ex hoc loco usque ad finem epistolæ ponit Apostolus moralia documenta.
paras.en: From this place to the end of the epistle the Apostle sets down moral teachings.

paras.t: Caritas fraternitatis, id est fraterna seu proximorum dilectio maneat in vobis. Qui enim diligit proximum, legem implevit. Ante et Petrus jubet: Ante omnia mutuam caritatem in vobis continuam habentes, quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum. Id est peccata in vobis obtegit, sed eam pro viribus exercete.
paras.en: [[13:1|Let the charity of the brotherhood|Caritas fraternitatis]], that is, brotherly love or the love of neighbours, [[13:1|abide in you|maneat in vobis]]. For [[Rom 13:8|he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law|Qui enim diligit proximum, legem implevit]] [no margin reference is given here; the words are Rom 13:8]. And Peter too commands: [[1 Pet 4:8|before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves|Ante omnia mutuam caritatem in vobis continuam habentes]], [[1 Pet 4:8|for charity covereth a multitude of sins|quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum]] [the margin reads *Ire.*, evidently I Petr. iv, 8]. That is, it covers the sins in you; but exercise it with all your strength.

paras.t: […] (sicut et Petrus hortatur: Hospitales invicem sine murmuratione, ne Christus in vobis […] de vobis improperet. Hospes […] Q[…]que in pede hominum ex apparuerunt. Unde et primo putabant eos homines esse, quod patet, quoniam corporalem refectionem paraverunt eis. Ex quibusdam tamen indiciis videbantur eis esse homines sancti, in quibus Deus honorabatur: propter quod adoraverunt eos. Postmodum vero cognoverunt quod angeli essent.
paras.en: […] (as Peter also exhorts: [[1 Pet 4:9|Using hospitality one towards another, without murmuring|Hospitales invicem sine murmuratione]]), lest Christ […] reproach you: [[Matt 25:43|I was a stranger|Hospes]] […] [the margin beside these lines reads only *41*; the words are Matt 25:43. The lemma of v. 2 and the lines that follow are lost in the transcription] […] who appeared in the likeness of men [the transcription reads *in pede hominum*, apparently for *in specie hominum*]. Hence at first they thought them to be men, as is plain, since they prepared bodily refreshment for them. Yet from certain signs they seemed to them to be holy men in whom God was honoured: for which reason they adored them. Afterwards, however, they learned that they were angels.

paras.t: Memento vinctorum, id est, captis: memento necessitatum nam tamen corpore laborem seu tribulationem impendentem. […] corpore hujus detenti vel. Timeam […] eos repausetis, tanquam et ipsi in corpore morantes, id est, corporales necessitates quotidie sentientes, per quod experti estis quid illis necessarium sit.
paras.en: [[13:3|Remember them that are in bands|Memento vinctorum]], that is, captives [the rest of this passage is garbled in the transcription and part of it is lost; the surviving words speak of remembering the needs of those who undergo labour or tribulation in the body, and of those held in bonds] […] that you may give them rest, [[13:3|as being yourselves also in the body|tanquam et ipsi in corpore morantes]], that is, feeling bodily needs every day, by which you have learned by experience what is needful for them.

paras.t: Honorabile connubium, id est honestum matrimonium, sit in omnibus vobis conjugatis: ut tria bona matrimonii inveniantur in vobis, videlicet fides, proles et sacramentum; et torus immaculatus, id est, non nisi legitime copulati condormiant. Fornicatores enim simplici fornicatione, et adulteros, nisi pœniteant, judicabit Deus judicio reprobationis æternæ. Ex quibus constat, quod actus matrimonialis possit esse sine peccato, et quod fornicatio simplex sit peccatum mortale.
paras.en: [[13:4|Marriage honourable|Honorabile connubium]], that is, honest matrimony, let it be [[13:4|in all|in omnibus]] of you who are married: so that the three goods of marriage may be found in you, namely faith, offspring and sacrament [that is, fidelity, children, and the holy and indissoluble bond]; [[13:4|and the bed undefiled|et torus immaculatus]], that is, let none sleep together save those lawfully joined. [[13:4|For fornicators|Fornicatores enim]] by simple fornication [that is, between persons not married], [[13:4|and adulterers|et adulteros]], unless they repent, [[13:4|God will judge|judicabit Deus]] with the judgement of eternal reprobation. From this it is established that the marriage act can be without sin, and that simple fornication is a mortal sin.

paras.t: Sint mores, id est actus et vita vestra, sine avaritia. Avaro enim nihil est scelestius; et radix omnium malorum est cupiditas. Contenti præsentibus, id est bonis jam habitis, ut non studeatis cumulare superflua; sed habentes victum, et quibus tegamur, contenti simus. Ipse enim Dominus dixit in libro Josue (quod ad litteram dicitur ipsi Josue, moraliter autem unicuique in Deo speranti): Non te deseram quin tibi necessaria tribuam, neque derelinquam in adversis. Hoc et Christus in Evangelio ait: Scit Pater vester quia his omnibus indigetis. Quærite ergo primum regnum Dei, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis.
paras.en: [[13:5|Let your manners|Sint mores]], that is, your acts and life, be [[13:5|without covetousness|sine avaritia]]. For [[Ecclus 10:9|nothing is more wicked than the covetous man|Avaro enim nihil est scelestius]]; and [[1 Tim 6:10|the desire of money is the root of all evils|radix omnium malorum est cupiditas]] [the margin's verse number is lost; the words are 1 Tim 6:10]. [[13:5|contented with such things as you have|Contenti præsentibus]], that is, with the goods you already have, so that you do not strive to heap up superfluities; but [[1 Tim 6:8|having food and wherewith to be covered, with these we are content|habentes victum, et quibus tegamur, contenti simus]]. [[13:5|For he hath said|Ipse enim Dominus dixit]] in the book of Josue (which literally is said to Josue himself, but morally to everyone who hopes in God): [[13:5|I will not leave thee|Non te deseram]] without bestowing on thee what is needful, [[13:5|neither will I forsake thee|neque derelinquam]] in adversity[[Jos 1:5||]]. This Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Matt 6:32|your Father knoweth that you have need of all these things|Scit Pater vester quia his omnibus indigetis]]. [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God|Quærite ergo primum regnum Dei]], [[Matt 6:33|and all these things shall be added unto you|et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]] [the margin's chapter number is lost; Matt 6:32–33].

paras.t: Ita ut confidenter dicamus singuli illud Psalmistæ: Dominus mihi adjutor est, non timebo quid faciat mihi homo, quamvis rapiat mea. Si enim Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Nam etsi permittat nos tribulari, exspoliari sive occidi, hoc facit propter majus commodum nostrum et gloriam ampliorem. Idcirco debemus nos ejus dispositioni confidenter committere.
paras.en: [[13:6|So that we may confidently say|Ita ut confidenter dicamus]], each of us, that word of the Psalmist: [[13:6|The Lord is my helper: I will not fear what man shall do to me|Dominus mihi adjutor est, non timebo quid faciat mihi homo]][[Ps 117:6||]] [the margin's numeral is lost; the Psalm is Ps 117:6], even though he rob me of what is mine. For [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us?|Si enim Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?]] Indeed, though he permit us to be afflicted, despoiled or slain, he does this for our greater profit and more ample glory. Therefore we ought to commit ourselves confidently to his disposition.

paras.t: Mementote præpositorum vestrorum, Apostolorum et discipulorum, seu successorum eorum, qui vobis locuti sunt verbum Dei; quorum intuentes, id est considerantes, exitum conversationis, id est finem et passionem quæ vitam hanc terminaverunt; vel, Exitum conversationis, id est conversationem ad alios; imitamini fidem, ut sitis parati mori pro fide, tanquam fideliter agatis ut ipsi.
paras.en: [[13:7|Remember your prelates|Mementote præpositorum vestrorum]], the Apostles and disciples, or their successors, [[13:7|who have spoken the word of God to you|qui vobis locuti sunt verbum Dei]]; [[13:7|considering|quorum intuentes]], that is, contemplating, [[13:7|the end of their conversation|exitum conversationis]], that is, the end and passion that closed this life; or, [[13:7|the end of their conversation|exitum conversationis]], that is, their conversation toward others [*conversatio*: manner of life, dealings with others]; [[13:7|whose faith follow|imitamini fidem]], so that you may be ready to die for the faith, acting faithfully as they did.

paras.t: Sic autem in Christo sperandum est: nam Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula, id est, Christus qui fuit adjutor præcedentium Sanctorum, est adjutor et posterorum, omniumque qui usque ad finem mundi in ipso sperabunt. Vel, per has differentias temporis designatur æternitas Christi secundum divinitatem, quemadmodum et alibi dicitur: Gratia vobis ab eo qui est, et qui erat, et qui venturus est.
paras.en: Thus, then, must we hope in Christ: for [[13:8|Jesus Christ, yesterday, and today: and the same for ever|Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula]], that is, Christ, who was the helper of the Saints who went before, is the helper also of those who come after, and of all who will hope in him until the end of the world. Or, by these differences of time the eternity of Christ according to his divinity is designated, as is said elsewhere also: [[Apoc 1:4|Grace be unto you|Gratia vobis]] [[Apoc 1:4|from him that is and that was and that is to come|ab eo qui est, et qui erat, et qui venturus est]].

paras.t: Consequenter docet vitare magistros fallaces, in cathedra pestilentiæ sedentes. Doctrinis variis, id est a sacra Scriptura diversis ac dissonis, et peregrinis, id est extraneis, nolite abduci a fide catholica, ne quis vos decipiat per inanem philosophiam, aut falsam Scripturarum interpretationem, vel simili modo. Optimum est enim gratia, id est per gratiam gratificantem, stabiliri cor, id est animam confirmari a Deo: quoniam gratia ista est omnium operum meritoriorum principium, sicut natura principium est operationum naturalium. Idcirco per gratiam vitantur errores ac hæreses: et tanto perfectius bona aguntur ac mala vitantur, quanto amplius cor in gratia stabilitur. Optimum ergo est gratia stabiliri cor, non escis, id est non superfluitate ciborum, vel non discretione escarum secundum legem, quoniam escæ secundum legem licitæ, non magis conferunt gratiam quam illicitæ. Ideo subditur: quæ escæ non profuerunt spiritualiter ambulantibus in eis, id est gulosis, vel observatoribus legis, quantum ad esum quarumdam escarum, et aliarum evitationem. Talia enim cærimonialia tempore novi Testamenti, mortifera sunt; nec propria virtute gratiam conferebant, etiam tempore veteris legis.
paras.en: Next he teaches them to shun false masters, who sit in the chair of pestilence. With [[13:9|various|Doctrinis variis]] doctrines, that is, differing from and discordant with sacred Scripture, [[13:9|and strange|et peregrinis]], that is, foreign, [[13:9|Be not led away|nolite abduci]] from the Catholic faith, lest anyone deceive you through vain philosophy, or false interpretation of the Scriptures, or in some like way. [[13:9|For it is best|Optimum est enim]] [[13:9|with grace|gratia]], that is, by grace that makes pleasing [*gratia gratificans*: sanctifying grace, which makes the soul pleasing to God], [[13:9|that the heart be established|stabiliri cor]], that is, that the soul be strengthened by God: since this grace is the principle of all meritorious works, as nature is the principle of natural operations. Therefore through grace errors and heresies are avoided; and good is done and evil avoided the more perfectly, the more fully the heart is established in grace. [[13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|Optimum ergo est gratia stabiliri cor]], then, [[13:9|not with meats|non escis]], that is, not by abundance of food, or not by the distinction of meats according to the law, since meats lawful under the law confer grace no more than unlawful ones. Hence it is added: [[13:9|which have not profited|quæ escæ non profuerunt]] spiritually [[13:9|those that walk in them|ambulantibus in eis]], that is, the gluttonous, or the observers of the law as regards eating some meats and avoiding others. For such ceremonial observances are deadly in the time of the New Testament; nor did they confer grace by their own power even in the time of the old law.

paras.t: Habemus enim altare de quo edere non habent potestatem qui tabernaculo deserviunt. Altare istud intelligi potest corpus Christi, vel crux in qua Christus oblatus est, vel materiale altare ecclesiæ. De corpore autem Christi, vel de altari et cruce, id est de sacrificio oblato in altari materiali in quo Christus quotidie immolatur, vel in cruce in qua oblatus est semel, non habent potestatem, id est licentiam, manducandi, qui tabernaculo deserviunt, id est, cultui veteris Testamenti, seu observationibus legalibus quæ fiebant in tabernaculo, dediti sunt, volentes observare legalia simul cum Evangelio. Tales enim censentur hæretici: ideo sacramentum corporis Christi manducare non possunt. Unde constat quod escæ legales non prosunt, sed optimum sit gratia stabiliri cor: quod fit in participatione corporis Christi. Quod deinde probat Apostolus per allegoriam veteris Testamenti, seu figuram hujus rei significativam.
paras.en: [[13:10|We have an altar whereof they have no power to eat who serve the tabernacle|Habemus enim altare de quo edere non habent potestatem qui tabernaculo deserviunt]]. This altar can be understood as the body of Christ, or the cross on which Christ was offered, or the material altar of the church. Now of the body of Christ, or of the altar and the cross, that is, of the sacrifice offered on the material altar [the end of every line of this column is lost in the transcription; from here to the end of v. 11 the line ends are read from fragments that the transcription carried into the next column] on which Christ is immolated daily, or on the cross on which he was offered once, [[13:10|they have no power|non habent potestatem]], that is, no leave, to eat, [[13:10|who serve the tabernacle|qui tabernaculo deserviunt]], that is, who are given over to the worship of the Old Testament, or to the legal observances that were performed in the tabernacle, wishing to keep the legal ordinances together with the Gospel. For such are reckoned heretics: and so they cannot eat the sacrament of the body of Christ. Hence it is established that legal meats do not profit, but that it is best that the heart be established with grace: which is done in partaking of the body of Christ. This the Apostle next proves by an allegory of the Old Testament, that is, a figure signifying this thing.

paras.t: Quorum enim animalium, scilicet hirci et vituli, qui in die Expiationis offerebantur solenniter intra castra, infertur sanguis pro peccato in Sancta per pontificem. Horum quippe animalium sanguinem intulit summus sacerdos in Sancta sanctorum. Horum quoque animalium corpora, id est carnes oblatæ, cremantur extra castra. Non enim licuit alicui his carnibus vesci, quoniam pro peccato pontificis erant animalia ista oblata: propter quod carnes eorum comburebantur omnino extra castra.
paras.en: For [[13:11|those beasts|Quorum enim animalium]], namely the buck goat and the calf, which on the day of Expiation were solemnly offered within the camp[[Lev 16:14||]] [the margin reads Lev. xvi and below it a garbled numeral, perhaps 14], [[13:11|whose blood is brought|infertur sanguis]] [[13:11|for sin|pro peccato]] [[13:11|into the holies by the high priest|in Sancta per pontificem]]: for the blood of these beasts the high priest carried into the Holy of holies. [[13:11|The bodies|Horum quoque animalium corpora]] of these beasts, that is, the flesh offered, [[13:11|are burned without the camp|cremantur extra castra]][[Lev 16:27||]]. For no one was allowed to eat this flesh, since these beasts were offered for the sin of the high priest: for which reason their flesh was burned wholly outside the camp.

paras.t: Porro hircus et vitulus præfiguraverunt Christum pro nostris peccatis oblatum, et similitudine carnis peccati indutum. Quod vero pontifex tulit sanguinem illorum animalium intra Sancta sanctorum, signavit quod per sanguinem Christi patefactus est aditus regni cœlorum. Combustio autem corporum, præfiguravit quod Christus extra portam pateretur. Sed quod sacerdotes vesci non poterant carnibus illis, significavit quod Judæi legalibus inhærentes et tabernaculo deservientes, non habent potestatem edendi de altari nostro, videlicet participando corpus et sanguinem Christi: propter quod declarandum introduxit Apostolus hanc figuram legalem.
paras.en: Now the buck goat and the calf prefigured Christ, offered for our sins and clothed in the likeness of sinful flesh[[Rom 8:3||]] [the margin here reads only *Hebr.*; the phrase is from Rom 8:3]. And that the high priest carried the blood of those beasts into the Holy of holies signified that through the blood of Christ the entrance of the kingdom of heaven has been opened. The burning of the bodies prefigured that Christ would suffer outside the gate. But that the priests could not eat that flesh signified that the Jews, clinging to the legal observances and serving the tabernacle, [[13:10|have no power|non habent potestatem]] to eat of our altar, namely by partaking of the body and blood of Christ: to make which plain the Apostle brought in this figure from the law.

paras.t: […]l est, qua[…] corpora animalium illorum cremabantur extra castra, idcirco ut figuratum corresponderet figuræ, et Jesus, ut sanctificaret, id est, a peccato purgaret gratiamque conferret, per suum sanguinem, id est pretio sanguinis sui, populum, id est genus humanum, extra portam Jerusalem passus est, scilicet in loco Calvariæ. Nunc tamen locus ille intra Jerusalem reædificatam includitur.
paras.en: […] [the first words of this sentence are lost] the bodies of those beasts were burned without the camp; therefore, so that the thing figured might answer to the figure, [[13:12|Jesus also|et Jesus]], [[13:12|that he might sanctify|ut sanctificaret]], that is, cleanse from sin and confer grace, [[13:12|by his own blood|per suum sanguinem]], that is, at the price of his blood, [[13:12|the people|populum]], that is, the human race, [[13:12|suffered|passus est]] [[13:12|without the gate|extra portam]] of Jerusalem, namely in the place of Calvary[[Matt 27:33||]]. Now, however, that place is enclosed within Jerusalem as it was rebuilt.

paras.t: Exeamus ergo gressibus mentis, videlicet credendo ac diligendo, ad eum extra castra, id est extra propria corpora, ea spiritualiter mortificando. Qui enim sunt Christi, ait Apostolus ad Galatas, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Et: Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt. Improperium ejus portantes, id est, passioni ejus nos conformantes, et crucem nostram quotidie post ipsum bajulantes, patiendo libenter pro Christi amore omnia dura atque adversa.
paras.en: [[13:13|Let us go forth therefore|Exeamus ergo]] with the steps of the mind, namely by believing and loving, [[13:13|to him without the camp|ad eum extra castra]], that is, outside our own bodies, mortifying them spiritually. For [[Gal 5:24|they that are Christ's|Qui enim sunt Christi]], says the Apostle to the Galatians, [[Gal 5:24|have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. And: [[Rom 8:8|they who are in the flesh cannot please God|Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt]]. [[13:13|bearing his reproach|Improperium ejus portantes]], that is, conforming ourselves to his passion, and carrying our cross daily after him[[Luke 9:23||]], suffering gladly for the love of Christ all things hard and adverse.

paras.t: Non enim habemus hic, id est in sæculo vel corpore isto mortali, manentem civitatem, id est stabilem mansionem. Velox namque est depositio tabernaculi nostri; et nec diem scimus nec horam, quemadmodum scriptum est: Nescio quamdiu subsistam, et si post modicum tollat me factor meus. Et rursus alibi: Dies nostri quasi umbra super terram, et nulla est mora. Sed futuram, id est cœlestem civitatem ac patriam Beatorum, inquirimus. De ipsa in Apocalypsi legitur: Civitas […] non eget sole neque luna: nam claritas Dei illuminabit eam, et lucerna ejus est Agnus.
paras.en: [[13:14|For, we have not here|Non enim habemus hic]], that is, in this world or in this mortal body, [[13:14|a lasting city|manentem civitatem]], that is, a stable dwelling. For [[2 Pet 1:14|the laying away of this my tabernacle is at hand|Velox namque est depositio tabernaculi nostri]] [Denis says *our* tabernacle, where Peter says *my*]; and we know neither the day nor the hour[[Matt 25:13||]], as it is written: [[Job 32:22|I know not how long I shall continue, and whether after a while my Maker may take me away|Nescio quamdiu subsistam, et si post modicum tollat me factor meus]]. And again elsewhere: [[1 Par 29:15|Our days upon earth are as a shadow, and there is no stay|Dies nostri quasi umbra super terram, et nulla est mora]]. But [[13:14|one that is to come|futuram]], that is, the heavenly city and fatherland of the Blessed, [[13:14|we seek|inquirimus]]. Of it we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:23|the city|Civitas]] […] [[Apoc 21:23|hath no need of the sun, nor of the moon|non eget sole neque luna]]: [[Apoc 21:23|For the glory of God hath enlightened it: and the Lamb is the lamp thereof|nam claritas Dei illuminabit eam, et lucerna ejus est Agnus]].

paras.t: Per ipsum ergo, id est, quatenus ad hanc civitatem hujusmodi perducamur, per ipsum Christum mediatorem, advocatum atque pontificem nostrum, offeramus […] id est […] sacrificium laudis […] obedientiam promptam, et divini nominis laudationem, semper, id est omni hora convenienti ac debita, Deo Trinitati, qui ait in Psalmo: Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me. De tali sacrificio scriptum est et alibi: Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate. Quod autem dicat hostiam laudis, declarat […] hoc est sa[…]monem, nostrorum labiorum confitentium nomini ejus, id est laudantium Deum, quemadmodum in Propheta legitur: Tollite vobiscum verba, et dicite ei, Reddemus vitulos labiorum nostrorum. Et in Psalmo: Confitebor Domino nimis in ore meo.
paras.en: [[13:15|By him therefore|Per ipsum ergo]], that is, so that we may be brought to such a city, through Christ himself, our mediator, advocate and high priest, [[13:15|let us offer|offeramus]] […] that is, […] a sacrifice of praise [the margin here reads Hebr. xiii, 15, the verse treated] […] prompt obedience, and the praise of the divine name, [[13:15|always|semper]], that is, at every fitting and due hour, [[13:15|to God|Deo]] the Trinity, who says in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:23|The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me|Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me]]. Of such a sacrifice it is written elsewhere also: [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity|Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate]] [the margin gives Eccli. xxxv, 1; in the Vulgate as numbered here the words are Ecclus 35:2]. And as to his saying [[13:15|the sacrifice of praise|hostiam laudis]], he makes it plain […], that is, the […] [probably *sermonem*, the speech] of our [[13:15|lips confessing|labiorum confitentium]] [[13:15|to his name|nomini ejus]], that is, praising God, as we read in the Prophet: [[Osee 14:3|Take with you words|Tollite vobiscum verba]], [[Osee 14:3|and say to him|et dicite ei]]: [[Osee 14:3|we will render the calves of our lips|Reddemus vitulos labiorum nostrorum]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 108:30|I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth|Confitebor Domino nimis in ore meo]].

paras.t: Beneficentiæ autem, id est liberalitatis et bonæ operationis in alios, et communionis, id est caritativæ communicationis bonorum vestrorum spiritualium, nolite oblivisci, sed opere exercete. Talibus enim hostiis, id est operibus ad Dei honorem exhibitis, promeretur, id est, pro præmio acquiritur, Deus, quum sint opera meritoria vitæ æternæ.
paras.en: [[13:16|to do good|Beneficentiæ autem]], that is, liberality and good working toward others, [[13:16|and to impart|et communionis]], that is, the charitable sharing of your spiritual goods: [[13:16|do not forget|nolite oblivisci]] these, but practise them in deed. [[13:16|for by such sacrifices|Talibus enim hostiis]], that is, by works shown forth to the honour of God, [[13:16|God's favour is obtained|promeretur]], that is, God is gained as a reward [*promeretur Deus*: God is merited, won as the reward of merit], since they are works meritorious of eternal life.

paras.t: Obedite præpositis, id est prælatis ac superioribus vestris, Christi vicariis, eorum præcepta servando, et subjacete illis, reverentiam exhibendo. Ait enim Salvator suis vicariis: Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit. Ipsi enim pervigilant, id est, de vestra salute solliciti sunt, quasi rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri Christo. Ut cum gaudio hoc faciant, id est, lætanter pro vobis pervigilent, adspicientes se non inaniter desudare pro vobis, sed de vestro profectu gratulentur. Maxima quippe consolatio boni prælati, est digna conversatio subditorum, prout Joannes in tertia sua testatur Canonica: Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare. Cum gaudio ergo hoc faciant, et non gementes, id est non desolati propter rebellionem et ingratitudinem vestram. Hoc enim expedit vobis, id est, in hac obedientia et subjectione salus vestra consistit. Melior namque est obedientia quam victimæ, et auscultare magis quam offerre adipem arietum: quoniam quasi peccatum ariolandi est repugnare, et quasi scelus idololatriæ, nolle acquiescere.
paras.en: [[13:17|Obey your prelates|Obedite præpositis]], that is, your prelates and superiors, the vicars of Christ, by keeping their precepts, [[13:17|and be subject to them|et subjacete illis]], by showing them reverence. For the Saviour says to his vicars: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]]. [[13:17|For they watch|Ipsi enim pervigilant]], that is, they are solicitous for your salvation, [[13:17|as being to render an account of your souls|quasi rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri]] to Christ. [[13:17|that they may do this with joy|Ut cum gaudio hoc faciant]], that is, may watch over you gladly, seeing that they do not toil for you in vain, and may rejoice at your progress. For the greatest consolation of a good prelate is the worthy conversation of his subjects, as John testifies in his third Canonical epistle: [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare]]. Let them do this with joy, then, [[13:17|and not with grief|et non gementes]], that is, not desolate because of your rebellion and ingratitude. [[13:17|For this is not expedient for you|Hoc enim expedit vobis]] [Denis reads *Hoc enim expedit vobis*, for this is expedient for you, without *not*, and takes it of obedience], that is, in this obedience and subjection your salvation consists. For [[1 Kings 15:22|obedience is better than sacrifices: and to hearken rather than to offer the fat|Melior namque est obedientia quam victimæ, et auscultare magis quam offerre adipem arietum]] of rams: [[1 Kings 15:23|Because it is like the sin of witchcraft, to rebel: and like the crime of idolatry, to refuse to obey|quoniam quasi peccatum ariolandi est repugnare, et quasi scelus idololatriæ, nolle acquiescere]].

paras.t: Orate pro nobis. Ecce Paulus confirmatus in gratia, petit ab inferioribus orationis suffragium. Nemo ergo adeo magnus aut sanctus sit in propriis oculis, ut spernat aut negligat petere orationis auxilium a proximis seu subjectis. Insuper manifestat Apostolus se esse capacem effectus orationis aliorum. Confidimus enim in Domino, quia, id est quod, bonam conscientiam habemus, id est, de nullo peccato, præsertim mortali, nobis conscii sumus, in omnibus locis, horis et causis, bene volentes conversari, id est laudabiliter vivere, neminem decipiendo.
paras.en: [[13:18|Pray for us|Orate pro nobis]]. Behold, Paul, confirmed in grace [that is, so strengthened by grace that he will not fall into mortal sin], asks the support of prayer from those beneath him. Let no one, then, be so great or so holy in his own eyes as to scorn or neglect to ask the help of prayer from his neighbours or his subjects. Moreover, the Apostle shows that he is capable of receiving the fruit of others' prayers. [[13:18|For we trust|Confidimus enim]] in the Lord that [[13:18|we have a good conscience|bonam conscientiam habemus]], that is, we are conscious to ourselves of no sin, especially of no mortal one, [[13:18|in all|in omnibus]] places, hours and causes, [[13:18|being willing to behave ourselves well|bene volentes conversari]], that is, to live laudably, deceiving no one.

paras.t: Amplius autem deprecor vos hoc facere, id est pro nobis orare, quo celerius restituar vobis, id est, ut cito permittar redire ad vos, ad vestram utilitatem.
paras.en: [[13:19|And I beseech you the more to do this|Amplius autem deprecor vos hoc facere]], that is, to pray for us, [[13:19|that I may be restored to you the sooner|quo celerius restituar vobis]], that is, that I may soon be allowed to return to you, for your profit.

paras.t: Deus autem pacis amator ac dator, qui eduxit de mortuis, id est, de morte suscitavit, pastorem magnum ovium, id est Christum, summum principemque pastorum, hominum humilium, innocentium et electorum (de quibus ait, Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis; et ad Petrum, Pasce, inquit, oves meas), qui facti sunt oves in sanguine testamenti æterni, id est per meritum effusionis sanguinis Christi: quo sanguine confirmatum est novum testamentum: quod appellatur æternum, quoniam aliud ei non succedit, et quia æterna bona promittit; Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum;
paras.en: [[13:20|And may the God of peace|Deus autem pacis]], the lover and giver of peace, [[13:20|who brought again from the dead|qui eduxit de mortuis]], that is, raised from death, [[13:20|the great pastor of the sheep|pastorem magnum ovium]], that is, Christ, the supreme [[1 Pet 5:4|prince of pastors|principemque pastorum]], of men humble, innocent and elect (of whom he says, [[John 10:15|I lay down my life for my sheep|Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]; and to Peter, [[John 21:17|Feed|Pasce]], he says, [[John 21:17|my sheep|oves meas]]), who have been made sheep [[13:20|in the blood of the everlasting testament|in sanguine testamenti æterni]], that is, through the merit of the shedding of Christ's blood: by which blood the new testament was confirmed, which is called everlasting because no other succeeds it, and because it promises everlasting goods; [[13:20|our Lord Jesus Christ|Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]],

paras.t: aptet, id est, per gratiam expeditos vos faciat, in omni bono, id est in cogitatione pura, locutione vera, operatione et passione sancta et recta, [ut faciatis ejus voluntatem,] faciens in vobis, id est dans vobis gratiam agendi, id quod placeat coram se, id est, suæ justitiæ sit acceptum. Ipse enim operatur in nobis et velle et perficere; et omnia opera nostra operatur in nobis. Faciatque hoc per Christum Jesum, id est merito Christi, per quem omnia divina nobis charismata conferuntur, cui est gloria in sæcula sæculorum, id est sine fine. Amen.
paras.en: [[13:21|Fit you|aptet]], that is, make you ready through grace, [[13:21|in all goodness|in omni bono]], that is, in pure thought, true speech, holy and upright action and suffering, [[13:21|that you may do his will|ut faciatis ejus voluntatem]] [these words stand in square brackets in the edition], [[13:21|doing in you|faciens in vobis]], that is, giving you the grace to act, [[13:21|that which is well pleasing in his sight|quod placeat coram se]], that is, what may be acceptable to his justice. For he [[Phil 2:13|worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish|operatur in nobis et velle et perficere]]; and he works [[Is 26:12|all our works|omnia opera nostra]] in us. And may he do this [[13:21|through Jesus Christ|per Christum Jesum]], that is, by the merit of Christ, through whom all divine gifts [*charismata*, gifts of grace] are bestowed on us, [[13:21|to whom is glory for ever and ever|cui est gloria in sæcula sæculorum]], that is, without end. [[13:21|Amen|Amen]].

paras.t: Rogo autem vos, fratres, ut sufferatis, id est, ut gratanter ac patienter audiatis, verbum solatii, id est epistolam hanc solatiosam et consolatoriam. Etenim perpaucis, id est valde brevi sermone, scripsi vobis, respectu sententiarum quæ in hac continentur epistola.
paras.en: [[13:22|And I beseech you, brethren, that you suffer|Rogo autem vos, fratres, ut sufferatis]], that is, that you hear gladly and patiently, [[13:22|this word of consolation|verbum solatii]], that is, this solacing and consoling epistle. For [[13:22|in a few words|Etenim perpaucis]], that is, in a very brief discourse, [[13:22|I have written to you|scripsi vobis]], considering how much is contained in this epistle.

paras.t: Cognoscite fratrem nostrum Timotheum dimissum a carcere, in quo dudum vinctus jacebat; cum quo, si celerius, id est festinanter, venerit ad me, videbo vos, visitando vos cum eo, si Deus sic dederit.
paras.en: [[13:23|Know ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty|Cognoscite fratrem nostrum Timotheum dimissum]] from the prison in which he had long lain bound; [[13:23|with whom|cum quo]], [[13:23|if he come shortly|si celerius]], that is, speedily, come to me, [[13:23|I will see you|videbo vos]], visiting you with him, if God so grant.

paras.t: Salutate omnes præpositos, id est prælatos vestros, et omnes sanctos, id est viros perfectos inter vos exsistentes. Ex hoc elicitur, quod præsentem epistolam scripsit communitati seu inferioribus, non rectoribus, quia fortassis non indigebant. Salutant vos, id est, beatitudinem vobis dicunt et optant, omnes fratres, id est Christiani, de Italia: cujus metropolis est Roma. Ex quo patet ex Roma hanc scriptam esse epistolam.
paras.en: [[13:24|Salute all your prelates|Salutate omnes præpositos]], that is, your superiors, [[13:24|and all the saints|et omnes sanctos]], that is, the perfect men living among you. From this it is gathered that he wrote the present epistle to the community, or to those beneath, not to the rulers, perhaps because they did not need it. There [[13:24|salute you|Salutant vos]], that is, wish and pray blessedness for you, all [[13:24|The brethren|fratres]], that is, the Christians, [[13:24|from Italy|de Italia]], whose metropolis is Rome. From this it is plain that this epistle was written from Rome.

paras.t: Gratia gratum faciens finalis et consummata, sit cum omnibus vobis. Amen. Ipsa enim est donum supernaturale, ad supernaturalem finem perducens, quam solus Creator infundit, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[13:25|Grace|Gratia]], the grace that makes pleasing [that is, sanctifying grace], final and consummate, be [[13:25|with you all. Amen|cum omnibus vobis. Amen]]. For it is a supernatural gift, leading to a supernatural end, which the Creator alone infuses, who is God above all, exalted and blessed. Amen.
